Dropping an idiom's own literal gloss into the option list draws every arm toward it, taking 65% to 96% of each arm's remaining Bengali errors. A model-by-language matrix over one shared item set shows how far this depends on the test language: every arm is 1.9 to 6.4 times more captured in Bengali than in English on the same paired entries, the commercial model's apparent resistance is a property of its test language, and capability does not order the failure. Calibration degrades in all three arms, and on the open arms confidence inverts, so gating on it is worse than gating at random. On a semantics-free option list, where accuracy is at chance, the best-calibrated arm still reports mean confidence 0.82. Code and data: https://github.com/sakhadib/literal-lock-in.

papers.title: Pearl-Chat: Engineering a native Luganda language model from first principles in JAX and Flax NNX
papers.summary: Autoregressive foundation language models predominantly target high-resource Indo-European languages, imposing computational and morphological penalties on under-represented African languages. Generic multilingual tokenizers routinely exceed fertility rates of 3.2 tokens per word on agglutinative Bantu languages, degrading context efficiency and inflating latency. We present Pearl-Chat, an 8,473,122-parameter ($\sim$8.5M) causal decoder-only transformer engineered for Luganda (Oluganda, ISO 639-2: lg), a low-resource Niger-Congo Bantu language spoken by over 10 million people in East Africa. Built from first mathematical principles in JAX and Flax NNX, Pearl-Chat uses explicit functional state decomposition (nnx.split and nnx.merge), deterministic resumable data streaming via Google Grain, and SPMD tensor parallelism using jax.sharding.Mesh. We introduce a byte-level byte-pair encoding (BPE) subword tokenizer trained from scratch on curated Luganda corpora ($V = 8,192$), achieving 4.88 characters per token compression and 1.60 tokens per word fertility, a two-fold compression improvement over LLaMA-3 (128K) and Gemma (256K). The model is trained with a two-stage curriculum: Stage 1 pre-training on 59,501 sequences across parallel, biblical, encyclopedic, and journalistic corpora, and Stage 2 instruction fine-tuning on 510 dialogues with assistant-only loss masking. Across 4,000 optimization steps, validation cross-entropy loss drops monotonically from 9.4695 (perplexity: 12,958.98) to 0.1818 (perplexity: 1.20), a decrease of 9.2877 nats. On a three-tier held-out diagnostic benchmark, Pearl-Chat achieves 0.9792 ROUGE-L and 0.9405 BLEU while maintaining concordial agreement across Bantu noun classes. We provide a Python Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming runtime and open-source all weights, tokenizers, and code.

papers.title: HeRE: A Novel Benchmark for Hebrew Relation Extraction via LLM-Guided Denoising of Knowledge Graph Alignments
papers.summary: While LLMs demonstrate strong capabilities in English Relation Extraction (RE) tasks, a significant gap remains in assessing their RE performance in low-resource languages, due to a lack of standardized benchmarks. Creating native, language-specific annotated RE benchmarks is expensive and requires human expertise, while relying on translation yields suboptimal, inaccurate datasets that introduce English-centric biases. To tackle this, we propose a scalable, language-agnostic methodology to create RE data by denoising naturally occurring yet noisy alignments of knowledge bases and corresponding texts. We define a proper alignment via a Natural Language Inference (NLI) task, where a relation triplet is entailed by an input text. We empirically assess five denoising strategies, and demonstrate that multilingual models outperform language-specific models in the few-shot LLM setting, while Hebrew-specific encoders remain competitive under NLI fine-tuning and are strongest in the label-free cross-training setting. We further find that prompting in the native language achieves performance on par with or slightly exceeding English prompts, confirming that the pipeline operates naturally in the target language. The best open-weights model, Gemma-4-31B-it (F1\,=\,0.915), matches the best API model, GPT-5.4 (0.921), and reaches F1\,=\,0.844 on a fully held-out, dual-annotated test set. Applying the optimized pipeline, we release HeRE: a novel, massive, 1.5-million-instance silver dataset for Hebrew RE, designed to support data-intensive experimentation and model fine-tuning. HeRE bridges a critical gap in standard Hebrew RE evaluation, while providing the NLP community with a reproducible, language-agnostic pipeline for RE dataset construction in other low-resource settings.

papers.title: Cultural (In)Competence: Investigating Culture-Specific Stereotype Detection Capabilities of LLMs
papers.summary: Stereotypes are subjective constructs that are mediated by the cultural context in which they are viewed. Successfully modeling them thus also requires cultural competence. When using large language models (LLMs) for stereotype-related tasks, such as their detection, it is therefore crucial that models can access relevant cultural knowledge and adjust responses accordingly. Since LLMs have shown disparities in what cultural knowledge is available to them, their capacity regarding stereotypes may also be disparate across languages and cultural contexts (e.g., for non-English languages or for non-US contexts). In this paper, we systematically investigate the effectiveness of LLMs for culture-specific stereotype detection across three factors: (1) the prompting language, (2) the instruction tuning language, and (3) the fine-tuning dataset size. We conduct experiments for US, Dutch, and Chinese cultural contexts. Our results suggest that LLMs do not reliably account for cultural contexts and overpredict the presence of stereotypes. Non-English prompts seem to improve consideration of cultural context and thus lead to more effective predictions. Moreover, we find that additional instruction tuning reduces false-positive rates and that training data size moderates detection effectiveness non-monotonically.
papers.title_zh: 文化（不）胜任力：探究大型语言模型对文化特定刻板印象的检测能力
papers.abstract_zh: 刻板印象是主观建构，受到审视它们的文化语境的中介。因此，要成功地对它们进行建模，也需要文化胜任力。因此，在使用大型语言模型（LLMs）执行与刻板印象相关的任务（例如检测刻板印象）时，模型能否获取相关文化知识并相应调整回答至关重要。由于大型语言模型在可获取何种文化知识方面表现出差异，它们处理刻板印象的能力也可能在不同语言和文化语境之间（例如对非英语语言或非美国语境）存在差异。本文系统考察大型语言模型在文化特定刻板印象检测方面的有效性，涉及三个因素：(1) 提示语言，(2) 指令微调语言，(3) 微调数据集规模。我们针对美国、荷兰和中国文化语境开展实验。我们的结果表明，大型语言模型不能可靠地考虑文化语境，并会过度预测刻板印象的存在。非英语提示似乎能改善对文化语境的考虑，从而产生更有效的预测。此外，我们发现额外的指令微调会降低假阳性率，并且训练数据规模会非单调地调节检测有效性。

papers.title: Who Do Perspectivist Models Predict Well? Annotator Agreement, Sparsity, and Performance
papers.summary: Successful completion of perspectivist natural language processing (NLP) annotation tasks requires algorithms to be aligned across diverse perspectives in order to predict how different humans will rate text. This work studies how the performance of such algorithms varies for annotators who behave differently than others, either by providing annotations that diverge from others' responses or by providing fewer annotations altogether. To aid with characterizing model performance, we curate the largest collection to date of perspectivist NLP datasets with ordinal annotations. After evaluating multiple classes of perspectivist algorithms across each of the datasets, we model the relationship between individual annotator idiosyncrasy and algorithm performance. In general, we find that algorithms perform better on annotators who tend to agree with others, but that annotator response rate does not have a statistically significant positive correlation with algorithm performance.

papers.title: Mitigating Demographic Disparities in Explanation-Human Alignment via Rationale Regularization
papers.summary: We study explanation fairness in hate speech detection. High classification performance does not always mean that a model produces equally plausible explanations for different demographic groups. Using the HateXplain dataset, we introduce Plausibility-EFG, a metric that measures the largest difference in explanation plausibility across demographic groups by comparing model-generated token attributions with human-annotated rationales. We evaluate BERT, RoBERTa, and ADV-RoBERTa, an adversarially trained model, using Integrated Gradients and SHAP. Our results show that ADV-RoBERTa improves classification performance and alignment between explanations and human rationales while reducing explanation disparities across demographic groups. These improvements are observed with both attribution methods and remain consistent across training, validation, and test splits. We also show that reducing prediction-level bias alone does not eliminate disparities in explanations, suggesting that predictive fairness and explanation fairness are related but distinct objectives. Finally, our fairness-performance analysis shows that stronger adversarial regularization can further reduce Plausibility-EFG, although it may cause a small decrease in macro-F1. Overall, this work presents explanation fairness as an important objective in hate speech moderation and introduces Fair-REF, a framework designed to reduce disparities in model explanations across demographic groups.

papers.title: SAG2: Embedding-Free Multi-Hop Retrieval with BM25 and JEV
papers.summary: Strong multi-hop retrieval should be practical to deploy without expensive corpus preparation or complex database infrastructure. We present SAG2, an embedding-free retrieval architecture built around a single SQLite database, BM25, and contextual evidence decisions from JEV. SAG2 follows the query-time association principle of SAG (SQL-Retrieval Augmented Generation), while replacing its event-entity and dense indexes with a lexical index over original passages. Selected passages supply terms for further retrieval, and newly retrieved evidence guides subsequent decisions. This moves semantic evidence selection to query time, eliminating offline embedding computation, LLM-based event-entity extraction, and dedicated database servers. The resulting system combines lightweight preparation with strong retrieval accuracy: on 1,000-question subsets of MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and HotpotQA, SAG2 achieves the highest Recall@5 and Recall@10 among the compared methods, with Recall@10 of 86.62%, 97.43%, and 99.00%. It also reaches 81.10% document Recall@10 over the 511,962-document EnterpriseRAG-Bench corpus. Indexing all 11,656 MuSiQue passages takes 2.36 seconds, produces a 25.87 MiB database, and requires no model calls. SAG2 demonstrates that accurate multi-hop evidence retrieval can be supported by compact, rapidly prepared infrastructure, making it a practical foundation for knowledge retrieval applications.

papers.title: The Model Knows Better: Defending Medical Multi-Agent Systems Against Prompt Injection
papers.summary: Medical multi-agent systems, in which LLM agents discuss a case, are increasingly studied for clinical decision support. Prompt injection, text that an attacker adds to a model's input, can manipulate LLMs into wrong decisions. How it affects these systems, and how to protect them, remains unclear. Across two systems, two model families and three benchmarks, a single injected passage succeeds in up to 61% of cases, and collaboration does not consistently protect against it. Existing defenses help only partly: they miss injections that look like ordinary clinical text. Yet when asked to check the injected text against the patient's findings, a model that followed the injection usually rejects it. We therefore propose a training-free defense that verifies the clinical judgments behind the system's decision. Following clinical practice, it separates the patient's findings from clinical judgments, such as diagnoses, recommendations and instructions, and checks each judgment against the findings alone, so the decision rests only on supported judgments. Our defense outperforms all baselines on every benchmark, lowering attack success on MedQA to 4-7% while maintaining accuracy on cases without an attack, and remains effective with a medical model and against defense-aware and adaptive attacks.

papers.title: Broad and Efficient PII Detection with Unified Labels
papers.summary: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) detection models must efficiently find identifiers across diverse contexts while maintaining a low false-positive rate (FPR) on high-volume traffic. Recent detectors increasingly rely on complex architectures that raise deployment cost, yet many are fine-tuned on only a few synthetic datasets that limit their coverage. Combining public datasets is challenging because their taxonomies differ, and even after categories are mapped to a common schema, labels can disagree on what counts as a detection, producing inconsistent training and evaluation signals. To address these problems, we present a practical 141M-parameter encoder-based detector trained on 1.12 million examples from 77 public datasets, relabeled under a detailed definition of broad contextual detection for 12 structured PII categories. Evaluated on the AI4Privacy and Nemotron-PII benchmarks at a low-FPR operating point, our model achieves the highest recall against larger baselines in 11 of 14 comparisons under our labels and 9 of 14 under the original labels. Its largest recall gains include useful additional coverage, such as multilingual disclosures and IP addresses embedded in URLs. It achieves this with 2-10x higher throughput and 94-97% less peak GPU memory than the baselines, delivering leading detection performance at substantially lower cost.

papers.title: When Does Uncertainty Measure RAG Hallucination Risk?
papers.summary: Uncertainty can measure hallucination risk in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), but only when retrieved evidence constrains the answer. When evidence is present, unsupported factual claims become less likely; when retrieval coverage is poor, the model can answer from internal knowledge and assign high probability to unsupported claims. We test this across four instruction-tuned models on HotpotQA and SQuAD. After matching faithful and hallucinated answers within word-count bins, length-only classifiers fall near chance, while perplexity reaches 0.81--0.91 AUROC on targeted unsupported edits. Varying retrieval depth shows why the score changes meaning: detection can weaken with only the top-ranked passage, then recover after adding a second passage. A combined uncertainty and semantic-drift score improves calibration, and measurements remain above chance on RAGTruth QA. Results support a conditional view of uncertainty as a useful measure of RAG hallucination risk.

papers.title: Trajectory-Guided Steering: Mitigating Spurious Feature Bias in Clinical Classification
papers.summary: Large language models rely on spurious features in clinical classification: swapping a single gender token in clinical notes alters gender-irrelevant diagnoses in up to 53.5% of cases. Existing inference-time corrections either need counterfactual data built around the specific spurious feature or behave unpredictably. We observe that how a model's preference between answers evolves across layers, its prediction trajectory, indicates for each document whether a correction is likely to help. We propose Trajectory-Guided Steering (TGS), which decides from the trajectory alone whether to correct each prediction and in which direction, with no counterfactual data and no knowledge of the spurious feature. On 16 clinical classification tasks from i2b2, TGS fixes 17.7% of errors while breaking only 1.3% of correct predictions and stays net-positive across all tested hyperparameter settings; all baselines are net-negative or near zero. The same corrections reduce reliance on the spurious feature: on the most affected diseases, gender-swap inconsistency falls sharply (hypertension 53.5% -> 38.0%, diabetes 35.1% -> 21.5%). Applying the correction to every document instead raises breaks on correct positive predictions from 0.1% to 6.4%, so per-document selection is essential. TGS also transfers to three model families and three other clinical and biomedical datasets.
papers.title_zh: 轨迹引导的操控：缓解临床分类中的虚假特征偏倚
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型在临床分类中依赖虚假特征：在临床记录中替换单个性别标记，会在高达53.5%的病例中改变与性别无关的诊断。现有的推理时校正要么需要围绕特定虚假特征构建的反事实数据，要么表现不可预测。我们观察到，模型在答案之间的偏好如何跨层演变，即其预测轨迹，能够指示对于每个文档，校正是否可能有所帮助。我们提出轨迹引导的操控（Trajectory-Guided Steering, TGS），它仅根据轨迹决定是否校正每个预测以及朝哪个方向校正，无需反事实数据，也无需知道虚假特征。在来自i2b2的16个临床分类任务上，TGS修复了17.7%的错误，同时仅破坏1.3%的正确预测，并且在所有测试的超参数设置下保持净正收益；所有基线均为净负或接近零。相同的校正降低了对虚假特征的依赖：在受影响最严重的疾病上，性别替换不一致性大幅下降（高血压 53.5% -> 38.0%，糖尿病 35.1% -> 21.5%）。相反，将校正应用于每个文档会使正确阳性预测的破坏率从0.1%升至6.4%，因此逐文档选择至关重要。TGS还可迁移到三个模型家族和另外三个临床与生物医学数据集。

papers.title: A Plausible Explanation Is Enough to Mislead Multimodal Judges
papers.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) increasingly serve as judges in training and evaluation pipelines, often assessing answers together with explanations. Although AI judges are sensitive to textual factors, it remains unclear whether ordinary plausible explanations can sway judgments requiring visual verification. We introduce JUPE, a visual-question-answering (VQA)-style benchmark that fixes answers while varying explanations. Across 14 MLLM judges, ordinary explanations that sound plausible mislead judges, with effects comparable on average to deliberately persuasive arguments. Plain justifications and chain-of-thought rationales reduce rejection of incorrect answers by 12.7 and 13.8 percentage points, respectively. We call this failure plausibility capture. Using signal detection theory, we find a significant mean shift in decision criterion toward acceptance, without a clear change in mean discriminability. Explanations sway judgments across domains, explanation generators, and judging protocols, while tested mitigations offer limited, model-dependent protection. Such shifts can inflate performance estimates when judges evaluate answers with explanations.
papers.title_zh: 一个看似合理的解释就足以误导多模态评判模型
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）越来越多地在训练和评估流程中充当评判者，常常连同解释一起评估答案。尽管 AI 评判者对文本因素较为敏感，但普通的看似合理的解释是否能够影响需要视觉验证的判断，仍不清楚。我们提出 JUPE，一个视觉问答（VQA）风格的基准，它固定答案而改变解释。在 14 个 MLLM 评判者上，听起来合理的普通解释会误导评判者，其平均效应与刻意说服性论证相当。朴素理由和思维链推理分别将错误答案的拒绝率降低了 12.7 和 13.8 个百分点。我们将这一失败称为合理性俘获（plausibility capture）。利用信号检测理论，我们发现决策标准均值显著向接受方向偏移，而平均辨别力没有明显变化。解释在不同领域、解释生成器和评判协议下都会影响判断，而所测试的缓解措施提供的保护有限且依赖于模型。当评判者在有解释的情况下评估答案时，这种偏移可能会抬高性能估计。

papers.title: ToMStories: Interpreting Theory-of-Mind in Synthetic Narratives
papers.summary: Understanding people often requires inferring what they feel or want from how they behave rather than from what they state outright. We ask whether language models can make these inferences, and how they do so. We introduce Theory-of-Mind Stories (ToMStories), an evaluation dataset of ~6,000 short synthetically generated narrative vignettes, each paired with a multiple-choice or open-ended question about a character's emotion, fear, motivation, or emotional wound. These psychological states are conveyed implicitly (showing), explicitly (telling), or with conflict between dialogue and description. Evaluating thirteen open-weight models (1B-72B parameters), we find that the largest models match humans on multiple choice but not open-ended questions. Our analyses point to simplifications models make in both interpretation and generation of implicit psychological states, indicating that synthetic data can help us understand how models perform interpretation, but likely overestimates how well models interpret humans.

papers.title: Measuring Mechanistic Uncertainty in Large Language Models via Causal Robustness
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in critical domains, where their susceptibility to hallucinations makes reliable and interpretable uncertainty quantification essential. We introduce the concept of mechanistic uncertainty, which characterizes uncertainty through the stability of the internal mechanisms supporting a model's response. We propose the causal robustness margin, defined as the minimum internal intervention required to deviate the model's output, and operationalize it using Jacobian Lens (Jlens) concept steering vectors. Across three open-source models and five question-answering datasets, we show incorrect and uncertain responses exhibit smaller margins, indicating greater sensitivity to internal interventions, and the causal robustness margin complements conventional output-based uncertainty methods. Finally, in a controlled knowledge injection experiment, correctly learned facts show increased margins after training, suggesting that causal robustness provides a mechanistically grounded signal of uncertainty.
papers.title_zh: 通过因果鲁棒性测量大型语言模型中的机制性不确定性
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地被用于关键领域，在这些领域中，它们易受幻觉影响的特性使得可靠且可解释的不确定性量化变得至关重要。我们引入了机制性不确定性的概念，它通过支撑模型响应的内部机制的稳定性来刻画不确定性。我们提出了因果鲁棒性裕度，将其定义为使模型输出偏离所需的最小内部干预，并使用 Jacobian Lens（Jlens）概念引导向量将其操作化。在三个开源模型和五个问答数据集上，我们表明错误和不确定的响应表现出更小的裕度，表明对内部干预的敏感性更高，并且因果鲁棒性裕度补充了传统的基于输出的不确定性方法。最后，在一项受控的知识注入实验中，正确学习的事实显示训练后裕度增加，这表明因果鲁棒性提供了一种具有机制基础的不确定性信号。

papers.title: Inductive Learning of Concept Embeddings from Cross-Linguistic Colexification Patterns with Textual Attributes
papers.summary: The advent of distributional semantics as a framework for computational semantics marked a paradigm shift in the nature of representations, by which meanings are represented as dense vectors commonly known as word embeddings. Computational approaches to historical or typological language comparison, on the other hand, still mostly rely on discrete representations, while the potential of embedding-based methods remains largely untapped in this context. Recent studies have proposed concept embeddings as a language-independent, onomasiological counterpart to word embeddings, based on networks of cross-linguistic colexification patterns. While the resulting concept embeddings reflect meaningful semantic properties and relations, they suffer from a lack of scalability, since they rely on transductive embedding approaches which only learn embeddings for nodes present in the training data. In this study, we present an inductive framework for learning concept embeddings, combining the structural properties of full and partial colexification networks with semantic information from short concept descriptions. This framework allows the embedding of unseen concepts based on a short definition. We show that the resulting concept embeddings correlate with various cross-linguistic measures of similarity or relatedness, while generalizing well to new concepts that were absent from the training data.

papers.title: SAFETYEDIT: Sparse Internal Targets with Prompt-Wide Control for LLM Jailbreak Backdoors
papers.summary: Model-editing backdoors aim to induce harmful responses under a trigger while preserving ordinary behavior on untriggered input. Recent model-editing approaches target affirmative response prefixes through rank-one updates to a small subset of model weights. Yet when this prefix-level target is satisfied, the model may still revert to refusal or produce a coherent, apparently compliant response that does not address the request. To overcome this limitation, existing internal-representation approaches shift focus from output tokens to dense, high-dimensional compliance directions in latent space. Existing representation-level approaches rely on preservation constraints to maintain conditionality, motivating us to ask whether a smaller internal target can offer a different effectiveness-preservation trade-off. Motivated by the comparable control capability of single-coordinate interventions, we investigate a sparse refusal-related MLP coordinate as this target. We propose SAFETYEDIT, which optimizes a single refusal-related coordinate and uses KV-cache marking in early attention layers to propagate a prefix-trigger signal across subsequent instruction positions. On some checkpoints a downstream MLP reader converts this signal into control of the coordinate, while on others the propagated signal alone suffices; the method is defined by the sparse target rather than by a fixed writer-reader pair. Across four open-weight LLMs and three dataset groups, SAFETYEDIT achieves the highest triggered Guard ASR in 11 of 12 comparisons and the highest mean StrongREJECT score in all 12, relative to the baselines evaluated for each model. Crucially, comprehensive ablation and behavioral audits confirm generally minimal changes in untriggered behavior and general capabilities in the tested configurations.

papers.title: Evidence-Gated Bilingual RAG for Reliable Consumer Banking Search
papers.summary: Consumers often describe what they need rather than use the terminology found on a banking website. For example, a natural-language request ("a card for travel") may not share the keywords of the relevant product page, and the problem is harder in bilingual services, where the same intent may be expressed in Arabic or English. This paper presents an evidence-gated bilingual retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework for consumer banking search that operates entirely on local infrastructure. The framework combines structured web-content refinement, hybrid dense-lexical retrieval, intent-aware evidence selection, cross-encoder reranking, and a three-outcome Answer / Related Mismatch / No Answer decision mechanism. On 210 URL-labeled Arabic and English queries, the proposed approach improves Top-1 hit rate from 50.48% to 79.05% and MRR@5 from 0.571 to 0.797 over a hybrid baseline. A separate 26-case end-to-end evaluation achieved 69.2% strict success, with 72.7% of generated answers classified as supported by an automated faithfulness judge. These results are preliminary: the retrieval queries are paraphrases of a small reference set, and the end-to-end test is small and uses an automated rather than human judge, so they do not establish human-verified answer correctness or generalizable performance.

papers.title: Secondhand Stress: How Stressful Disclosures Affect Psychosocial Wellbeing in Online Graduate Admissions Communities
papers.summary: Online communities provide spaces for individuals navigating stressful life transitions to disclose difficulties and seek peer support. Yet encountering others' distress may also have psychosocial implications for community members. Drawing on stress crossover theory, we examine how engagement with peer distress during graduate admissions is associated with subsequent psychosocial expression and participation, and whether similar associations extend through downstream interactions. We analyze 171,981 posts and 1,130,413 comments from two Reddit communities across three admissions cycles, using propensity-score stratification and baseline-adjusted comparisons. Users who engaged with distress disclosures during application preparation subsequently exhibited higher classifier-estimated anxiety, depression, and stress expression, alongside greater commenting activity and lexical redundancy. These associations recurred across admissions cycles, while no significant psychosocial associations were detected among downstream respondents interacting with previously exposed users. Our findings highlight how greater distress-related expression can coexist with continued community participation, while distinguishing direct engagement with distress disclosures from subsequent social contact. We discuss implications for designing online communities that preserve opportunities for self-disclosure and peer support while remaining attentive to the experiences of those encountering distress-related content.

papers.title: ProPerAgent: Toward Memory-Driven Proactive Assistance
papers.summary: As assistants move from reactive answering toward proactive intervention, memory changes role: it no longer only supplies the answer to a query, it determines whether and when to speak at all. Prior work in this setting hands the system the relevant fact in context; we study the regime that makes the problem hard, where the evidence justifying an intervention must be mined from a long-horizon personal memory. We introduce ProPerMem, a benchmark for memory-driven proactive assistance (MPA), pairing egocentric video with year-long, distractor-rich user memories (~618K tokens on average), human-verified trigger windows, and a protocol that scores content and timing jointly. Every baseline we evaluate performs poorly (at most 15%), including frontier models given summarized or retrieval-augmented memory. A controlled study explains why: with oracle evidence delivered inside the trigger window GPT-5.3-Chat reaches 96%; letting it choose the timing drops it to 38%, and replacing oracle evidence with retrieval drops it to 15%. Content and timing are separately necessary, and missing either is catastrophic. Guided by this, we build ProPerAgent (Proactive Personalized Agent) with a plug-and-play harness that surfaces memory from a graph-organized store and gates it down to what is worth interrupting for, plus a lightweight RL stage that curbs early and repeated firing. Without any training, ProPerAgent lifts strict accuracy from below 10% to 37.5% on Qwen3.8-27B and 38% on GPT-5.3-Chat; RL post-training reaches 42.4%.

papers.title: Multimodal Filesystem Memory For Long-Horizon Embodied Agents
papers.summary: Agents operating over long horizons need an effective memory that allows them to reuse their experience throughout long interactions. If the entire history of an interaction is retained, it becomes difficult to find the relevant experience, while compressing it into summaries may result in the loss of visual and spatial details that are required later on. We present \textbf{MFM}, a multimodal filesystem memory architecture that keeps complementary types of agent memory. \textbf{Episodic memory} stores the observations, actions, and outcomes, and \textbf{spatial memory} associates experiences with locations. \textbf{Semantic and procedural memory} build up general knowledge and reusable methods of acting, and \textbf{working memory} holds the current plans. MFM makes use of searchable textual records to connect these different representations to the underlying multimodal episodes. The agents are able to find previous experiences by means of contextual cues and to examine the original observations in order to recover details that are missing from their textual descriptions. Through consolidation, the agents convert experience into higher-level knowledge and procedures while still keeping references to the original episodes. In the case of long-horizon Minecraft and computer-use tasks, MFM leads to improved performance with three base models. With GPT-6-Astra, MFM completes \emph{Mine Diamond from Scratch} and reaches 16 out of 24 milestones on the \emph{Ender Dragon} task, as against 12.7 for the best baseline. On CUABench-KiCad it attains a mean reward of 0.440, as compared to 0.400 for the best baseline and 0.267 in the case of no persistent memory.

papers.title: Explore Separately, Adopt Selectively: Execution-Guided Tool Use over Large Tool Libraries
papers.summary: Large language model agents must discover relevant tools from large libraries, e.g., thousands of tools, as new needs arise during task execution. When several candidates could satisfy the same need, execution may be required to identify the relevant one. Investigating candidates in a shared trajectory can leave alternatives unexplored or allow failed attempts to influence subsequent reasoning. To address this, we present BRIA (BRanch-Inspect-Adopt), a simple yet effective agent that temporarily isolates candidate investigations in separate branches. Each branch retrieves and executes tools to investigate its candidate; a task agent inspects the resulting execution evidence and adopts only useful results into its continuing trajectory. BRIA retrieves additional tools as new capability needs arise during task execution. We evaluate BRIA on PlanBench-XL and MCP-Atlas using a shared pool of 1897 tools, three language models, and static and adaptive retrieval baselines. Across all settings, BRIA matches or exceeds the strongest retrieval baseline. On MCP-Atlas, it achieves an average claim score of 89.77, compared with 75.40 for MCP-Zero, a gain of 14.37 percentage points. BRIA also lies on the Pareto frontier for task performance and input-token cost.
papers.title_zh: 分开探索，选择性采纳：大型工具库上的执行引导式工具使用
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型智能体必须在任务执行过程中出现新需求时，从大型工具库（例如数千个工具）中发现相关工具。当多个候选工具可能满足同一需求时，可能需要通过执行来识别相关工具。在共享轨迹中考察候选工具可能导致其他备选方案未被探索，或使失败尝试影响后续推理。为解决这一问题，我们提出 BRIA（BRanch-Inspect-Adopt），这是一种简单而有效的智能体，它暂时将候选工具的考察隔离在独立分支中。每个分支检索并执行工具以考察其候选工具；任务智能体检查由此产生的执行证据，并仅将有用结果采纳到其持续进行的轨迹中。BRIA 在任务执行过程中出现新的能力需求时检索额外工具。我们在 PlanBench-XL 和 MCP-Atlas 上评估 BRIA，使用包含 1897 个工具的共享工具池、三个语言模型以及静态和自适应检索基线。在所有设置下，BRIA 达到或超过最强检索基线的表现。在 MCP-Atlas 上，它取得了 89.77 的平均 claim score，而 MCP-Zero 为 75.40，提升了 14.37 个百分点。BRIA 还位于任务性能和输入 token 成本的帕累托前沿上。

papers.title: First Passage Attention
papers.summary: Augmenting softmax attention with forget gates typically relies on summing decay contributions along the key--query path. Because such accumulation is monotonic, these mechanisms cannot selectively erase intermediate context while preserving older, structurally relevant tokens. We propose First Passage Attention (FPA), which shifts from path summation to path extrema by lowering a key's logit proportionally to the deepest dip of a learned scalar field below that key's level over the intervening span. FPA encompasses the Forgetting Transformer (FoX) as a special case, and when the field and levels follow a shared learned walk, the alive keys with unpenalised logits naturally form a stack. We show that a constant-dimension FPA head realises any subset of keys left alive by subsequent dips, whereas softmax heads with positional biases or token-level forget gates require a head dimension linear in the number of keys. In synthetic experiments, one-layer FPA heads converge to these target sets while comparable softmax and FoX baselines fail on every seed. Scaling to a 110M-parameter language model, FPA matches FoX in perplexity and uniquely achieves perfect passkey retrieval at $8\times$ the training length, even with its key--value cache compressed to about $25\%$.

papers.title: ARBOR: Locating Reasoning Failures in Long Chains of Thought through Reasoning State Tracking
papers.summary: Large reasoning models solve complex problems through long chains of thought, in which prior work has documented failure modes such as overthinking, underthinking, and unsupported deductions. Existing methods detect these failures from local signals: textual similarity to nearby steps, switch tokens, or an LLM's judgment of a step's correctness. However, what a step contributes to the solution depends on the state that earlier steps have established, so identifying failures requires a global view that tracks that state across the trajectory. Therefore, we propose ARBOR, a reasoning-failure attribution framework that represents each trajectory as a tree of reasoning states, built as each step creates, verifies, prunes, or revisits a state, and attributes each failure to a relation between a step and the state preceding it. Using ARBOR, we refine the three failure modes into distinct subtypes that harm reasoning through different mechanisms and at different costs. We find that the tree state ARBOR maintains before a step separates failure steps from the at-risk steps at which the failure did not occur. We discuss how ARBOR integrates with existing mitigations at inference time and in training data. Code, data and interactive examples are available at https://inklab.usc.edu/ARBOR.

papers.title: CoLU: Confidence-Weighted Layerwise Unlearning for Large Language Models
papers.summary: Large language model (LLM) unlearning aims to forget certain information while preserving others, without retraining from scratch. SoTA methods such as NPO, SimNPO, and SatImp balance forgetting and retain through whole model fine-tuning, while FOM-UL explores selective layer updates. Prior works show that suppressing target information can damage retained knowledge. This trade-off can vary across layers even under the same unlearning loss. In this work, we propose Confidence-Weighted Layerwise Unlearning (CoLU), which combines a novel confidence-weighted forgetting and retain regularization while updating a single selected transformer layer, rather than the whole model for unlearning. To reduce CoLU compute cost, we further propose Brief Layer Screening (BLS), which uses a newly defined normalized forgetting-retention (NFR) score to first rank layers through a brief unlearning trials using a subset of forgetting dataset and fewer epochs. BLS pre-selects top-k ranked layer candidates, which will then be fully profiled using full data analysis. BLS is proven to reduce the runtime of CoLU by 60.2-79.7% with almost the same performance. On TOFU dataset, CoLU improves both forgetting and retention over NPO, SatImp, and GA-based FOM-UL in all six TOFU settings, and over SimNPO in five of the six settings. On MUSE Books and News datasets, CoLU achieves the highest retained KnowMem and the PrivLeak closest to zero among the compared SOTA unlearning methods. CoLU presents a new record performance in both unlearning and retain in most settings up to date. Moreover, across the measured settings, average CoLU GPU memory usage is 77.4% to 79.5% lower than full-model unlearning.
papers.title_zh: CoLU：面向大语言模型的置信度加权逐层遗忘
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLM）遗忘旨在忘记某些信息而保留其他信息，且无需从头重新训练。NPO、SimNPO 和 SatImp 等 SoTA 方法通过全模型微调来平衡遗忘与保留，而 FOM-UL 则探索选择性层更新。已有工作表明，抑制目标信息可能损害保留的知识。即使在相同的遗忘损失下，这种权衡在不同层之间也可能有所不同。在这项工作中，我们提出置信度加权逐层遗忘（CoLU），它在更新单个选定的 Transformer 层而非整个模型进行遗忘的同时，结合了一种新颖的置信度加权遗忘与保留正则化。为降低 CoLU 的计算成本，我们进一步提出简要层筛选（BLS），它使用新定义的归一化遗忘-保留（NFR）分数，先通过使用遗忘数据集的子集和更少轮次的简短遗忘试验对层进行排名。BLS 预先选择排名前 k 的层候选，随后将使用全数据分析对其进行全面刻画。经验证，BLS 在性能几乎相同的情况下将 CoLU 的运行时间减少了 60.2-79.7%。在 TOFU 数据集上，CoLU 在全部六个 TOFU 设置中在遗忘和保留两方面均优于 NPO、SatImp 和基于 GA 的 FOM-UL，并在六个设置中的五个设置上优于 SimNPO。在 MUSE Books 和 News 数据集上，在所比较的 SOTA 遗忘方法中，CoLU 实现了最高的保留 KnowMem 和最接近零的 PrivLeak。CoLU 在迄今为止的大多数设置中在遗忘和保留两方面均呈现出新的纪录性能。此外，在所测量的设置中，CoLU 的平均 GPU 内存使用量比全模型遗忘低 77.4% 至 79.5%。

papers.title: TokenEconomizer: Experience-Driven Black-Box Cost Control for Coding Agents
papers.summary: Advances in frontier coding agents have sharply increased the token costs of AI-assisted software engineering. Their token efficiency is typically evaluated on isolated tasks, whereas real-world developers use them to continuously build, update, and maintain large-scale projects. This mismatch motivates us to evaluate agents over sequences of realistic coding tasks, where we find that agents exhibit recurring environment-dependent token costs that existing methods struggle to reduce. To minimize these costs, we introduce TokenEconomizer, an external controller that cuts environment-specific token costs over a sequence of tasks. These cuts come from determining (i) which operational micro-skills to inject, (ii) which persistently irrelevant tools to prune, and (iii) when to intervene in unproductive failure loops. Across Claude Code, Codex, and GitHub Copilot CLI paired with frontier models, TokenEconomizer reduces the average token cost by 18.4-30.9% with comparable task success. Savings hold in every repository under every tested agent-model setting and generalize to diverse domains such as sequential web development and security auditing, where costs fall by 6.4-21.2% depending on task structure. Our work establishes adaptive black-box cost control as a promising direction for reducing token costs of coding agents in realistic settings.

papers.title: Thunder-DeID+: Boundary-Aware Korean De-identification from Court Judgments to Broader Sensitive Documents
papers.summary: This study examines the transferability of a de-identification model developed for Korean court judgments to a broader range of sensitive documents, focusing on boundary precision, label granularity, and recall. The agglutinative structure of Korean causes Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenizers to frequently merge Personally Identifiable Information (PII) with adjacent particles, which complicates accurate span recovery. Furthermore, current PII taxonomies lack sufficient granularity for legal texts. To address these issues, this study introduces Thunder-DeID+, which integrates a refined three-tier PII taxonomy with a boundary-aware tokenizer. The tokenizer enhances a pretrained BPE vocabulary by incorporating N-gram and boundary-scoring components to better align token and PII span boundaries. The proposed approach is evaluated using a tokenizer-independent word-segment-level protocol. On full-length judgments, the tokenizer consistently improves W. Strict Typed F1-score from 0.76-0.77 to 0.87-0.88 across four model sizes (150M, 395M, 750M, and 1B), mainly by increasing precision rather than model scale. With fine-tuning on 1,000 broader sensitive documents, the judgment-trained model further achieves 0.93 W. Strict Typed F1-score, indicating effective transfer beyond court judgments.

papers.title: Self-Evolving Coding Agents via Harness-Policy Optimization
papers.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents have shown promising potential in coding tasks, and their performance is jointly determined by the policy model and the harness that mediates their interaction with the environment. Indeed, harness and policy are mutually reinforcing and evolving only one component is suboptimal---a harness tuned for one checkpoint may not target the failure modes of an updated policy, while policy learning remains limited to the trajectories elicited by a fixed harness. In light of this, we propose Self-HPO, a recursive self-improving framework for coding agents that alternates harness and policy optimization, using the evolving policy as its own harness proposer. Specifically, in each round, the current policy first analyzes its own failures and proposes new harness candidates (H-step). The policy is then updated through reinforcement learning (RL) under the selected harness (P-step), and hard tasks identified during training form the next harness search set, keeping harness optimization targeted to the policy's evolving failure modes. Across three coding benchmarks, Self-HPO consistently outperforms harness-only and policy-only baselines, improving Qwen3.5-35B-A3B's average resolve rate from 57.8% to 64.8%, with gains generalizing to out-of-distribution settings. Further analysis shows that both optimized components retain gains even when paired with their base counterparts, while their joint gain exceeds the sum of their individual gains. Self-HPO also improves reliability (Pass@1) and expands the capability frontier (Pass@k) over the base agent. Additionally, we show that with a stronger external model (e.g., Opus 4.8) as the harness proposer, the same framework yields a further performance boost.
papers.title_zh: 通过执行框架—策略优化实现自进化编码智能体
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLM）智能体在编码任务中展现出可观潜力，其性能由策略模型以及中介其与环境交互的执行框架共同决定。事实上，执行框架与策略相互增强，仅演化其中一个组件是次优的——为某一检查点调优的执行框架可能无法针对更新后策略的失败模式，而策略学习仍受限于固定执行框架所引出的轨迹。鉴于此，我们提出 Self-HPO，一种用于编码智能体的递归自改进框架，它交替进行执行框架优化与策略优化，并将演化中的策略作为其自身的执行框架提出者。具体而言，在每一轮中，当前策略首先分析自身的失败并提出新的候选执行框架（H-step）。随后，策略在所选执行框架下通过强化学习（RL）进行更新（P-step），训练过程中识别出的困难任务构成下一轮执行框架搜索集，从而使执行框架优化持续针对策略不断演化的失败模式。在三个编码基准上，Self-HPO 始终优于仅执行框架和仅策略的基线，将 Qwen3.5-35B-A3B 的平均解决率从 57.8% 提升至 64.8%，且增益可泛化到分布外设置。进一步分析表明，两个优化后的组件即使与各自的基座对应组件配对时仍能保留增益，而它们的联合增益超过各自单独增益之和。Self-HPO 还在基座智能体基础上提升了可靠性（Pass@1）并扩展了能力前沿（Pass@k）。此外，我们表明，使用更强的外部模型（例如 Opus 4.8）作为执行框架提出者时，同一框架可带来进一步的性能提升。

papers.title: Prune the Leaky Neurons: Mitigating Private Data Leakage in Fine-Tuned LLMs via Joint-Embedding-Guided Pruning
papers.summary: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) on proprietary records enables domain adaptation but introduces two challenges: (i) privacy leakage of memorized private data, such as personally identifiable information (PII), and (ii) balancing private data removal with utility preservation. Existing defenses, including data sanitization and differential privacy, often degrade performance, while privacy-neuron editing lacks a PII-free reference to distinguish identity-specific neurons from those supporting useful text. We propose JEPA-Prune, a post-hoc neuron pruning framework guided by a model trained exclusively on PII-free views. Alongside the fine-tuned private model, JEPA-Prune, trains a public model on surrogate and masked views of the same records using a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA), capturing domain knowledge without identifiers. A cross-model representation probe quantifies deviations between private representations of leaked records and this PII-free reference. Integrated gradients and a scale-invariant specificity score then identify PII-responsive neurons, which are pruned without retraining. Experiments show that pruning just 1.6% of neurons reduces PII inference accuracy by up to 7.4x and PII extraction recall by up to 13.9x, while keeping unseen-text perplexity within 16% of that of the unpruned model for most LLMs. In contrast, privacy-neuron editing increases perplexity by at least 26x.
papers.title_zh: 修剪泄漏神经元：通过联合嵌入引导的剪枝缓解微调大语言模型中的私有数据泄漏
papers.abstract_zh: 在专有记录上微调大语言模型（LLM）能够实现领域适应，但会带来两个挑战：(i) 被记忆的私有数据（例如个人可识别信息（PII））的隐私泄漏，以及 (ii) 在移除私有数据与保持效用之间取得平衡。现有防御方法，包括数据净化和差分隐私，往往会降低性能，而隐私神经元编辑缺乏一个不含PII的参考，以区分身份特定神经元与支持有用文本的神经元。我们提出 JEPA-Prune，一个事后神经元剪枝框架，由仅在无PII视图上训练的模型引导。与微调的私有模型并行的，JEPA-Prune 使用联合嵌入预测架构（JEPA）在相同记录的代理视图和掩码视图上训练一个公共模型，从而在不包含标识符的情况下捕获领域知识。一个跨模型表示探针量化泄漏记录的私有表示与该无PII参考之间的偏差。然后，积分梯度和尺度不变的特异性得分识别对PII有响应的神经元，这些神经元无需重新训练即可被剪枝。实验表明，仅剪枝1.6%的神经元就能将PII推断准确率最多降低7.4倍，并将PII提取召回率最多降低13.9倍，同时对于大多数LLM，将未见文本困惑度保持在未剪枝模型的16%以内。相比之下，隐私神经元编辑使困惑度至少增加26倍。

papers.title: Causal Latent Workspaces for Looped Transformers
papers.summary: Reusing a Transformer block across depth increases computation without replicating its parameters, but successive passes have no dedicated state through which positions can exchange compact summaries of their causal prefix. We introduce the causal latent workspace Transformer: an anchored, four-round shared-depth architecture in which each position writes gated vectors into prefix-specific latent slots and retrieves a content-addressed summary before the next shared block application. This path complements causal self-attention while the original input embedding remains accessible at every round. Across three byte-level corpora, three seeds, and two matched parameter budgets, the proposed model achieves the best mean held-out perplexity in five of six settings against five Transformer controls. At 101.71M parameters it leads on WikiText-103 raw, enwik8, and TinyStories, reaching perplexities 2.7820, 2.7843, and 1.6823; these improve upon the strongest non-workspace control on each corpus by 1.06%, 0.73%, and 1.01%. All nine seed-labelled comparisons at this budget favor the workspace. At 0.918M parameters it leads on WikiText-103 and TinyStories, whereas a conditioned loop is stronger on enwik8. Architectural ablations show that adding the workspace improves upon the anchored loop in all six settings and support refreshing its causal summaries at each round. Together, these results identify a causal, content-addressable prefix workspace as an effective structural augmentation of looped Transformers.

papers.title: On the Position Bias of Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Study
papers.summary: Recent studies have shown that position bias remains a critical vulnerability in large language models (LLMs), undermining both the integrity of multiple-choice evaluations and the reliability of retrieval-augmented generation. However, existing understanding of this phenomenon is largely derived from studies with limited model coverage and English-centric benchmarks, leaving the behavior of frontier models and diverse languages underexplored. In this work, we conduct a comprehensive investigation of position bias across model scales ranging from billion-level to trillion-level parameters, covering both multiple-choice and multi-document tasks in five languages. Our experiments reveal that while position bias remains noticeable in small-scale models and Non-English languages, increasing model scale and employing standard Chain-of-Thought prompting significantly mitigate this issue. Moreover, we demonstrate that emerging \emph{thinking models} with extended reasoning capabilities are nearly immune to position bias, suggesting a costly but general approach toward resolving this vulnerability.
papers.title_zh: 论大型语言模型的位置偏差：一项综合研究
papers.abstract_zh: 近期研究表明，位置偏差仍然是大语言模型（LLMs）中的一个关键脆弱性，它既损害了多项选择评估的完整性，也削弱了检索增强生成的可靠性。然而，现有对这一现象的理解主要来自模型覆盖范围有限且以英语为中心的基准研究，这使得前沿模型和多种语言中的行为仍未得到充分探索。在本工作中，我们对从十亿级到万亿级参数的不同模型规模下的位置偏差进行了全面研究，涵盖五种语言中的多项选择任务和多文档任务。我们的实验表明，尽管位置偏差在小规模模型和非英语语言中仍然明显，但增大模型规模并采用标准的思维链提示可以显著缓解这一问题。此外，我们证明，具有扩展推理能力的新兴 \emph{思维模型} 几乎不受位置偏差影响，这暗示了一种代价高昂但通用的解决这一脆弱性的方法。

papers.title: Watermarkability: Measuring and Improving Language-Model Compatibility with Logit-Based Watermarks
papers.summary: Language-model watermarks can help identify model-generated text, encode provenance information, and detect post-generation edits. A broad class of logit-based watermarks increases the logits of a designated token set at each decoding step. Because a base model's native probability mass on this set varies across contexts, models, and watermark rules, the same logit bias can yield different adherence rates and increases in perplexity (PPL). We introduce watermarkability to characterize the compatibility between a model and the token sets requested by a watermark. At a target mass $τ$, we quantify this property through a watermarkability cost: the expected minimum KL divergence from the base-model distribution required to assign probability at least $τ$ to the requested set. A lower cost means that the model is more watermarkable for that request distribution. To reduce this cost, we propose a two-stage method. In the first stage, we train a target-set-conditioned low-rank adapter on unions drawn from a 16-way vocabulary partition to increase the requested set's probability mass. In the second stage, a closed-form controller applies the smallest remaining uniform logit bias needed to reach the target mass. We evaluate the method on six watermark schedules using OPT-125M and Qwen3-8B. Across the 12 model-schedule pairs, the pre-adaptation watermarkability cost correlates with the log-PPL increase under a near-hard fixed-bias baseline (pooled Pearson $r=0.929$). For every schedule, at least 99.80% of sampled tokens fall in the target set requested at their decoding step. At this reliability, the adapter and controller reduce average per-schedule prompt-conditional PPL by 46.3% on OPT-125M and 5.2% on Qwen3-8B relative to the fixed-bias baseline.

papers.title: Causal Edit Serialization
papers.summary: Standard autoregressive language models generate text sequentially, but revision requires referring back to tokens in the input context or those already generated. Causal Edit Serialization (CES) is introduced as a framework for expressing such revisions within the same causal token stream. Special pointer tokens are paired with predicted source addresses, allowing insertion, deletion, replacement, copying and movement to be localized explicitly. A lightweight localization head and dual-index rotary position encoding support both address prediction and conditioning on previously emitted pointers, while retaining a standard causal attention mask. A pretraining procedure combines ordinary language modeling with serialized repairs derived from random corruptions, model-generated edits and repeated text. Across model scales and editing baselines, CES models demonstrate complete applied edits with modestly higher clean-text bits per byte than clean autoregressive models. Supervised and reinforcement-learning post-training provide a grammatical-error-correction proof of concept, producing more beneficial than harmful changes under reference-blind model judging. Correct repair programs also improve subsequent text prediction while the original context and its cached states are retained. CES provides a common interface for generation and localized revision, with potential extensions to iterative refinement and additional pointer-addressed transformations.

papers.title: The Reliance Hypothesis: Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness Rises as Language Resource Level Falls
papers.summary: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) faithfulness matters for monitoring, explaining and safely deploying large language models, yet it has been studied mostly in English. Languages differ in level, the amount of text available to learn from, so models know less in lower-resource languages, which may change how much they rely on their reasoning. To our knowledge, we are the first to relate CoT faithfulness to both resource level and task type (knowledge- or reasoning-intensive). On parallel multiple-choice questions from Multilingual Massive Multitask Language Understanding (MMMLU) in eight languages, faithfulness rises as resource level falls on knowledge-intensive tasks but not on reasoning-intensive ones, a gap that points the same way across four models and several faithfulness measures. We propose, and find support for, the Reliance Hypothesis: models rely more on their reasoning when they cannot recall the answer, as in lower-resource languages on knowledge-intensive tasks. Model confidence partly explains the effect of resource level, but not the knowledge-reasoning gap. Languages in which models are less confident rely more on reasoning, yet less confident answers within a language do not, a Simpson's paradox. In lower-resource languages, models rely on their reasoning for more answers, not more strongly for each. CoT monitoring may therefore be most informative in lower-resource languages, where it is least often validated.
papers.title_zh: 依赖假说：思维链忠实度随语言资源水平下降而上升
papers.abstract_zh: 思维链（Chain-of-Thought, CoT）忠实度对于监测、解释和安全部署大语言模型至关重要，但此前的研究大多集中在英语中。不同语言在资源水平上存在差异，即可供学习的文本数量不同，因此模型在低资源语言中掌握的知识较少，这可能改变它们对其推理的依赖程度。据我们所知，我们是首个将 CoT 忠实度同时与资源水平和任务类型（知识密集型或推理密集型）联系起来的研究。在来自多语言大规模多任务语言理解（Multilingual Massive Multitask Language Understanding, MMMLU）的八种语言平行多项选择题上，在知识密集型任务中，忠实度随资源水平下降而上升，但在推理密集型任务中并非如此；这一差距在四个模型和若干忠实度度量上指向同一方向。我们提出并找到了对“依赖假说”的支持：当模型无法回忆答案时，它们会更依赖自己的推理，正如在知识密集型任务中的低资源语言里那样。模型置信度部分解释了资源水平的影响，但不能解释知识与推理之间的差距。在模型置信度较低的语言中，模型更依赖推理，然而在同一语言内，置信度较低的答案却并非如此，这是一种辛普森悖论。在低资源语言中，模型是对更多答案依赖其推理，而不是对每一个答案依赖得更强。因此，CoT 监测在低资源语言中可能信息量最大，而它在那里却最不常得到验证。

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Budget Allocation for Efficient LLM Tree Search
papers.summary: Tree search enhances multi-step reasoning in large language models (LLMs), yet prevailing methods expand every step with a fixed budget, irrespective of the marginal utility of expansion. We first show, across existing search algorithms, that continuations sampled from a shared intermediate state are largely duplicates and collapse to a few distinct answers. Critically, we find that the semantic dispersion of sibling actions predicts the redundancy of their downstream continuations, permitting a subtree's budget to be fixed before expansion. An information-theoretic analysis motivates this: treating the per-step budget as the Monte Carlo sample size for estimating a step's residual answer entropy, we derive a sufficient budget that shrinks with sibling dispersion. We accordingly propose $\textbf{Uncertainty-Aware Allocation}$ (UAA), a training-free framework that decouples value from uncertainty: values determine which candidates are promising, while uncertainty, estimated from sibling dispersion at no additional model cost, determines how many merit expansion, via uncertainty-aware pruning and uncertainty-aware budgeting. Across mathematical reasoning, logical reasoning, and planning benchmarks, UAA reduces token usage by up to $90\%$ and latency by up to $9\times$ at comparable accuracy, generalizing across four tree search algorithms and both open- and closed-source LLMs.
papers.title_zh: 用于高效 LLM 树搜索的不确定性感知预算分配
papers.abstract_zh: 树搜索增强了大语言模型（LLMs）中的多步推理，但现有方法以固定预算扩展每一步，而不考虑扩展的边际效用。我们首先表明，在现有搜索算法中，从共享中间状态采样得到的延续在很大程度上是重复的，并坍缩为少数几个不同答案。关键的是，我们发现兄弟动作的语义离散度预测其下游延续的冗余度，从而允许在扩展之前固定一个子树的预算。一项信息论分析为此提供了动机：将每一步的预算视为用于估计某一步剩余答案熵的蒙特卡洛样本量，我们推导出一个随兄弟离散度增大而收缩的充分预算。我们据此提出 $\textbf{Uncertainty-Aware Allocation}$（UAA），一个免训练框架，将价值与不确定性解耦：价值决定哪些候选有前景，而不确定性——以不增加额外模型成本的方式由兄弟离散度估计——通过不确定性感知剪枝和不确定性感知预算分配，决定有多少候选值得扩展。在数学推理、逻辑推理和规划基准上，UAA 在准确率相当的情况下将 token 使用量降低最多 $90\%$，将延迟降低最多 $9\times$，并可泛化到四种树搜索算法以及开源和闭源 LLMs。

papers.title: Identify, Classify, Act: Per-Instruction Controlled Compliance for LLMs over External Data
papers.summary: LLMs over external data face a per-instruction tension: a single document or tool return often interleaves legitimate directives with adversarial prompt injections, and the model must follow the former while rejecting the latter. Existing defenses suppress or trust all external instructions, collapsing the safety-utility frontier and forcing a choice between over-refusal and over-compliance. We argue the missing capability is \textbf{per-instruction credit attribution} and formalize it as External-Data Instruction Classification, an identify-classify-act decision over each embedded directive. We propose \textbf{EDIC}, a decomposed reward framework for per-instruction compliance. A scene-grounded pipeline injects mixed beneficial and harmful instructions with counterfactual filtering, while a generative judge is initialized by SFT and refined with GRPO to attribute compliance at the instruction level. The judge then produces a reward that separately encourages beneficial compliance and penalizes harmful compliance for RL training. Across two backbones and five benchmarks, EDIC improves both safety and utility over the strongest prior defense, lifting harmful-rejection by up to 7.7\% and Arena-Hard-Auto utility by 12.5\% on Qwen3-4B. The code repository is hosted at https://github.com/yingyingxia666/EDIC.

papers.title: NLData2Opt: Benchmarking Parameter Derivation and Prediction for Modeling Optimization Problems from Natural Language and Data
papers.summary: Formulating optimization problems from raw inputs of problem descriptions and data is time-consuming and costly. While Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a promising way to automate this process, existing benchmarks overestimate their capabilities by relying on idealized inputs where all data is relevant and complete. This diverges from reality, where data-centric reasoning is required to extract, compute, and predict parameters from noisy sources. To address this, we introduce NLData2Opt, a benchmark to evaluate LLMs on the multi-stage reasoning inherent in practical optimization workflows. NLData2Opt decomposes problems into problem descriptions and data, and requires models to (1) extract relevant parameters from data containing misleading attributes, (2) compute missing parameters derived by transforming existing data attributes, and (3) predict unavailable future values from historical observations. Evaluation results show substantial performance decline relative to existing benchmarks, indicating that benchmark progress does not directly translate to formulation accuracy in practical optimization workflows. NLData2Opt is available at https://github.com/sumarivyn/NLData2Opt.
papers.title_zh: NLData2Opt：面向从自然语言与数据出发的优化问题建模，对参数推导与预测进行基准评测
papers.abstract_zh: 从问题描述和数据的原始输入出发构建优化问题表述既耗时又成本高昂。尽管大语言模型（LLMs）为自动化这一过程提供了有前景的途径，但现有基准依赖理想化输入——即所有数据均相关且完整——从而高估了它们的能力。这与现实情况不符：现实中需要以数据为中心的推理，从含噪来源中抽取、计算并预测参数。为解决这一问题，我们提出 NLData2Opt，一个用于评估 LLMs 在实际优化工作流所固有的多阶段推理方面表现的基准。NLData2Opt 将问题分解为问题描述和数据，并要求模型：(1) 从包含误导性属性的数据中抽取相关参数；(2) 计算通过变换已有数据属性而推导出的缺失参数；(3) 根据历史观测预测不可用的未来值。评估结果表明，相对于现有基准，性能出现显著下降，这表明基准上的进展并不能直接转化为实际优化工作流中的问题表述准确率。NLData2Opt 已在 https://github.com/sumarivyn/NLData2Opt 公开。

papers.title: Bengali Hallucination Detection with Retrieval and Programs: A System Study
papers.summary: Bengali hallucination detection must distinguish unsupported factual claims from incorrect reasoning, often without a supplied reference passage. We present and characterize an inference-only system that combines response-conditioned query rewriting, hybrid retrieval, and task-specific language-model judging. Six retrieval routes search question-answer and passage collections; a router directs each example to a 27B textual judge or a 14B agent that can compare retrieved answers, reason directly, or generate and execute Python. We characterize the system using version-specific code, saved predictions, execution traces, and corpus metadata from the Olikbochon challenge. Kaggle associates a displayed private macro-F1 of 0.956 with Version 2; its saved run processes 2,516 examples in 220.99 minutes on two T4 GPUs. Of 253 math-routed examples, 88 terminate through candidate matching, while execution traces expose 49 stderr-bearing run events across 35 examples. A later run changes six predictions despite identical core worker code. A bounded audit of 1,090 benchmark-related corpus records finds exact question or context overlap for 38 processed evaluation inputs, precluding an unqualified claim of corpus-independent generalization. The contribution is a concrete retrieval-and-computation judging architecture with an auditable operational characterization, not a controlled estimate of component gains. We distinguish the reported leaderboard result from independently recomputed diagnostics and identify the evidence needed for stronger effectiveness and reproducibility claims.

papers.title: Competence-Based Evaluation of Logical Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.summary: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have brought impressive performance across diverse tasks; however, shortcomings remain in logical reasoning, including inconsistencies under linguistic variation. To improve the reasoning capacity of LLMs, we must be able to accurately measure their reasoning capacity. Current benchmarks primarily report single accuracy numbers on selected reasoning tasks. Such a performance-based evaluation methodology says little about a model's generalization capacity in reasoning. To address this limitation, we argue for a different evaluation paradigm, called competence-based evaluation (CBE), which tests whether models reliably apply the same competence across a family of problems. A parameterized generator scales complexity while keeping the required competence fixed, and matched answer-preserving presentations test correctness beyond one formulation. We instantiate CBE on elementary ordering tasks, scaling input size while varying presentations of the same ordering rule. Across six GPT and Qwen models, performance is reasonably good over bounded complexity ranges, but even strong models fail the competence condition across the tested family. Chain-of-thought and GRPO extend strong performance without resolving all tested failures; supervised LoRA shows little held-out transfer. CBE provides diagnostic profiles and an evaluation protocol that can grow with future models.
papers.title_zh: 大型语言模型中逻辑推理的基于能力评估
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLMs）的近期进展已在多种任务上带来令人印象深刻的性能；然而，在逻辑推理方面仍存在不足，包括在语言表述变化下的一致性问题。为了提升 LLMs 的推理能力，我们必须能够准确测量其推理能力。当前的基准测试主要在选定的推理任务上报告单一准确率数值。这种基于性能的评估方法几乎无法说明模型在推理方面的泛化能力。为解决这一局限，我们主张采用一种不同的评估范式，称为基于能力的评估（CBE），它检验模型是否能够在一系列问题上可靠地应用同一种能力。参数化生成器在保持所需能力固定的同时扩展复杂度，而匹配的、保持答案不变的呈现方式则在单一表述之外检验正确性。我们在基本排序任务上实例化 CBE，在扩展输入规模的同时改变同一排序规则的呈现方式。在六个 GPT 和 Qwen 模型上，性能在有界复杂度范围内相当不错，但即便是强模型也未能在所测试的问题族上满足能力条件。思维链和 GRPO 扩展了强性能，但并未解决所有受测试的失败；监督式 LoRA 显示出很小的留出迁移。CBE 提供了诊断性画像以及一种可随未来模型发展而扩展的评估协议。

papers.title: FederatedBytes: Tokenizer-Free, Byte-Level Small Language Models for Efficient Multimodal Federated Learning
papers.summary: Federated Learning (FL) is a powerful machine learning framework that allows building a global model from the contributions of multiple, distributed clients, while ensuring the privacy of their local data. However, its heavy computational and communication overheads challenge its use for contemporary AI workloads such as natural language processing (NLP) and multimodal analysis. For this reason, this paper presents a novel small language model that leverages byte-level text and multimodal data processing, enhanced by a linear attention mechanism, to enable manageable Federated Learning of NLP and multimodal analysis tasks. The proposed model, nicknamed FederatedBytes, manages to process text and any other data types, including images, by treating its input as a mere sequence of bytes, while its lean linear attention mechanism allows abating the overall memory and computational footprint. To prove the effectiveness of the proposed model we have carried out an extensive performance evaluation on sentiment analysis tasks in multilingual and multimodal settings over the Multilingual Amazon Reviews and ScienceQA datasets. The experimental results show that FederatedBytes has been able to outperform comparable models such as ByT5 and LSTM, achieving higher accuracy while significantly reducing memory and communication overheads.

papers.title: Where's the Indirect Evidence? Investigating Grammatical Generalization with Influence Functions
papers.summary: Language models generalize beyond their training corpus to learn linguistic phenomena (Patil et al., 2024; Misra and Mahowald, 2024), showing that there exists indirect evidence driving learning. Prior work has inferred that indirect evidence exists without identifying its character or considered specific hypotheses about what it might be. We explore an alternative bottom-up method for identifying indirect evidence. We use influence functions (Koh and Liang, 2017) to measure how individual training sentences affect model predictions in 15 grammatical phenomena from BLiMP (Warstadt et al., 2020). We filter out a phenomenon's direct evidence using hand-constructed rules and take the 60,000 most influential remaining sentences as indirect evidence. This indirect evidence substantially affects learning: retraining without it lowers held-out accuracy more than removing a matched random group for every phenomenon across five models (by a median of 12 points). We characterize the indirect evidence by its similarity to our direct evidence filters: it (partially) meets the filters' structural conditions at a median of 4.7 times the rate of a matched random group. Finally, clustering phenomena by indirect-evidence overlap recovers three of the five BLiMP categories that include multiple phenomena, suggesting that this method can reveal linguistic relationships.

papers.title: ASR-Style Transcript Normalization Removes Useful Pragmatic Signal for Dialogue Act Classification
papers.summary: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) pipelines often normalize transcripts by removing filled pauses and punctuation and expanding colloquial forms, potentially discarding cues useful for dialogue act classification. We evaluate nine transcript conditions across six classifiers (TF-IDF logistic regression, RoBERTa, BERT, ALBERT, GPT-2, and BiLSTM) and three conversational corpora (Switchboard, ICSI MRDA, and SLUE-HVB), supplemented by multi-seed experiments, normalization controls, and real-ASR evaluations. Across five random seeds, heavy normalization reduces Macro-F1 in all 15 neural model-corpus combinations under the original preprocessing protocols. Removal using the original filler and backchannel lexicon consistently degrades performance on MRDA and SLUE-HVB but produces mixed effects on Switchboard. Punctuation-aware TF-IDF experiments show that punctuation removal reduces Macro-F1 by 0.036 on Switchboard and 0.078 on MRDA, demonstrating that the original linear baseline's apparent insensitivity resulted from tokenization. Restricting filler removal to um, uh, and erm preserves degradation on MRDA but largely eliminates the SLUE-HVB effect, where the original lexicon removes class-defining backchannel expressions. These findings demonstrate that normalization effects depend on preprocessing definitions, feature extraction, and conversational context, supporting task-dependent rather than indiscriminate transcript normalization.

papers.title: Many Biases, One Circuit: Post-Training Tunes a Pretrained Cue-Routing Mechanism
papers.summary: Language models often abandon a correct answer when the prompt contains a cue, a hint toward a wrong option such as "I think the answer is B." Sycophancy and related biases show this failure. They are often studied separately and blamed on alignment. We test this view causally, tracing the attention heads behind these biases through the stages of two post-training pipelines. In multiple-choice tests on most models, four cue types rely largely on the same few heads, a shared circuit already present in pretrained models. Most base models follow cues in plain text. Fine-tuning a base model on about 200 generic assistant examples without cues activates these heads in chat format, so cue-following can be a side effect of assistant tuning. The final reinforcement learning (RL) stage strengthens the effect of cues in almost every comparison. In Tulu-3-8B and OLMo-2-7B, we swap the attention patterns of six middle layers between the RL checkpoint and its predecessor. For suggested-answer cues, this shifts each checkpoint's cue effect most of the way to the other's level. Post-training thus seems to change when and how strongly models use this circuit. Mitigation for these multiple-choice biases could target this circuit.

papers.title: Beyond Surface Cues: Robust LLM-Generated Korean Text Detection
papers.summary: As large language models (LLMs) generate increasingly fluent text, the need for reliable detection of LLM-generated content has grown substantially. However, existing research remains heavily English-centric, leaving Korean largely underexplored. Moreover, current evaluations of Korean text detection often rely on superficial cues, leading to overly optimistic estimates of detection performance. To address these limitations, we introduce \textsc{KoLing}, a bias-controlled adversarial benchmark comprising 50.9k instances that suppresses superficial shortcuts while preserving semantic content and separately evaluates LLM-generated and LLM-modified text detection. We further propose KoLingProbe, an interpretable detector grounded in theoretical linguistics that models Korean-specific properties across multiple linguistic levels. Experiments show that KoLingProbe substantially outperforms strong baselines on all detection tasks while remaining robust to adversarial attacks. Our analyses further reveal that integrating complementary linguistic features across multiple levels yields both improved performance and interpretability.
papers.title_zh: 超越表面线索：鲁棒的LLM生成韩语文本检测
papers.abstract_zh: 随着大语言模型（LLMs）生成越来越流畅的文本，对LLM生成内容进行可靠检测的需求已大幅增长。然而，现有研究仍严重以英语为中心，使韩语在很大程度上未得到充分探索。此外，当前对韩语文本检测的评估往往依赖表面线索，导致对检测性能的估计过于乐观。为解决这些局限，我们提出 \textsc{KoLing}，一个包含50.9k个实例的偏置控制对抗基准，它抑制表面捷径，同时保留语义内容，并分别评估LLM生成文本和LLM修改文本的检测。我们进一步提出 KoLingProbe，一个基于理论语言学的可解释检测器，它在多个语言层面上对韩语特有的属性进行建模。实验表明，KoLingProbe 在所有检测任务上大幅优于强基线，同时对对抗攻击保持鲁棒。我们的分析进一步揭示，整合跨多个层面的互补语言特征能够同时提升性能和可解释性。

papers.title: Aligning Language Models Towards Counterfactual Invariance
papers.summary: Small variations in prompt characteristics can meaningfully alter the semantics, tone, and contextual assumptions of large language model outputs. Such characteristics can involve group variables such as demographics or other sensitive latent attributes. Sensitivity to such input variables is undesirable when demographic information is causally irrelevant to the task, but might still be relevant for generation of semantically coherent responses. This makes the task of enforcing counterfactual invariance while preserving model utility difficult. To study this problem, we first show that standard model alignment recipes (such as reinforcement learning) increase differences in response quality across demographics, while improving overall response quality, ultimately amplifying what is known as counterfactual bias. To address this, we develop a policy gradient technique involving a group-level reward function that operates on matched pairs of counterfactual prompts. For completeness, we build a dataset of controlled counterfactual prompt pairs and design an evaluation that separately measures cases where demographic information is causally relevant to the answer. Finally, we validate our findings on several fairness benchmarks. We demonstrate that our methods reduce counterfactual differences while preserving overall response quality and that the models continue to adapt appropriately when such sensitive information is relevant.
papers.title_zh: 将语言模型对齐到反事实不变性
papers.abstract_zh: 提示特征的微小变化可能会显著改变大语言模型输出的语义、语气和上下文假设。此类特征可能涉及群体变量，例如人口统计信息或其他敏感潜在属性。当人口统计信息与任务因果无关时，对此类输入变量的敏感性是不可取的，但这些信息对于生成语义连贯的响应仍可能相关。这使得在保持模型效用的同时强制实现反事实不变性的任务变得困难。为研究这一问题，我们首先表明，标准模型对齐方法（例如强化学习）会在提高整体响应质量的同时，增大不同人口统计群体之间响应质量的差异，最终放大所谓的反事实偏差。为解决这一问题，我们开发了一种策略梯度技术，涉及一个组级奖励函数，该函数作用于匹配的反事实提示对。为完整起见，我们构建了一个受控反事实提示对数据集，并设计了一种评估，分别测量人口统计信息与答案因果相关的情形。最后，我们在多个公平性基准上验证了我们的发现。我们证明，我们的方法在减少反事实差异的同时保持整体响应质量，并且当此类敏感信息相关时，模型仍能继续适当适应。

papers.title: Recognizing Atari and Assessing Sente: Controlled Evaluation Tasks for Language-Based Go Agents
papers.summary: Domain terminology provides concise descriptions of game states and strategic relationships, but whether game-playing language models can accurately recognize these concepts and relate them to move evaluation remains unclear. We construct a controlled evaluation set centered on atari and its relationship to sente in Go, examining terminology recognition under local board changes and move evaluation under different strategic conditions. We conduct our tests on LoGos, a Go language model, after fine-tuning it with terminology and commentary supervision. The model struggles to recognize changes in the atari relationship and assess its strategic implications. Its terminology predictions are associated with move preferences even when those preferences contradict the reference evaluation. Our controlled tests provide a framework for examining whether language-based Go agents connect domain terminology with precise board relationships and strategic move values.

papers.title: What Shapes Brain Alignment of Large Language Models during Dialogue? Insights from Language Production and Comprehension
papers.summary: Brain alignment of large language models (LLMs) offers a way to investigate representational similarities between LLMs and the human brain during language processing. While previous studies have mainly focused on passive language comprehension, little is known about such alignment during dialogue, in which speakers engage in both language production and comprehension. In this study, using fMRI data collected during dialogue, we examine brain alignment during language production and comprehension across LLM layers and brain regions. We assess its association with the intrinsic dimension (ID) of LLM representations and the contributions of several interpretable linguistic and communicative features. Our results reveal distinct patterns of brain alignment between production and comprehension, as well as strong associations with ID in brain regions associated with each processing mode. Furthermore, we show that the contributions of linguistic and communicative features also vary across processing modes, LLM layers, and brain regions.
papers.title_zh: 是什么塑造了对话过程中大型语言模型的大脑对齐？来自语言产生与理解的洞见
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLMs）的大脑对齐为研究LLMs与人脑在语言加工过程中的表征相似性提供了一种途径。尽管以往研究主要关注被动的语言理解，但人们对于对话过程中的这种对齐却知之甚少，而在对话中，说话者同时参与语言产生和理解。在本研究中，我们利用对话期间收集的fMRI数据，考察了跨LLM层和脑区在语言产生与理解过程中的大脑对齐。我们评估了其与LLM表征的内在维度（ID）的关联，以及若干可解释的语言和交际特征的贡献。我们的结果揭示了语言产生与理解之间不同的大脑对齐模式，以及与每种加工模式相关脑区中ID的强关联。此外，我们还表明，语言和交际特征的贡献也因加工模式、LLM层和脑区的不同而有所差异。

papers.title: KiranaBench: Can a Language Model Run a Neighbourhood Shop?
papers.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly evaluated on long-horizon tasks, including autonomously running a business. Existing benchmarks for this setting are almost exclusively English-language, Western in retail context, and single-agent, with the agent observing the business directly. We study how these results transfer to a multi-agent Indic setting. We introduce KiranaBench, a simulated Indian general store in which four roles (manager, cashier, helper, and bookkeeper) are each played by a separate LLM agent. Interactions with customers and suppliers occur in English, Hindi, or Hinglish, and product demand is calibrated to India's national Household Consumption Expenditure Survey. Evaluating four open-weight LLMs, we find that all fall far short of a fixed-rule shopkeeper baseline: the best model earns only one-eighth of the baseline's profit, and two models finish below an unmanaged shop. Performance is also consistently lower for Hindi and Hinglish than for English supplier communication. KiranaBench offers evidence that current LLM agents are not yet reliable for autonomously operating small businesses in India, and provides a testbed for developing agents suited to settings that are long-horizon, collaborative, and multilingual.
papers.title_zh: KiranaBench：语言模型能经营一家社区小店吗？
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLM）智能体越来越多地在长时程任务上接受评估，其中包括自主经营一家企业。针对这一场景的现有基准几乎全部是英语的、零售情境为西方的、且为单智能体的，智能体直接观察业务。我们研究这些结果如何迁移到多智能体的印度语境场景中。我们提出 KiranaBench，一个模拟的印度杂货店，其中四个角色（经理、收银员、帮工和记账员）各由一个独立的 LLM 智能体扮演。与顾客和供应商的交互以英语、印地语或印地英语进行，商品需求依据印度全国住户消费支出调查进行校准。在评估四个开放权重 LLM 后，我们发现它们全都远远达不到固定规则店主的基线水平：最佳模型仅获得基线利润的八分之一，而有两个模型的最终结果甚至低于无人管理的店铺。在供应商沟通方面，印地语和印地英语的表现也始终低于英语。KiranaBench 提供了证据表明当前 LLM 智能体尚不能可靠地在印度自主经营小企业，并为开发适用于长时程、协作式和多语言场景的智能体提供了一个测试平台。

papers.title: Self-Evolving Agents Can Repair Failures but Struggle to Generalize from Them
papers.summary: Experience-driven self-evolution offers a promising path for large language model (LLM) agents to continually improve through interaction. Yet existing approaches often rely on successful trajectories or external evaluation signals, leaving unclear whether agents can evolve when such positive anchors are unavailable. We study this question through Cold-Start Failure-Only Evolution (CFOE), where agents start without accumulated experience and learn only from failed interactions without privileged guidance. Across three self-evolving paradigms, multiple LLM backbones, and four interactive environments, we uncover a consistent repair-generalization gap: failure-derived experience can help repair previously failed tasks, but rarely yields sustained improvements on unseen tasks. Further analysis shows that agents often misinterpret failures, while even verified-correct experience remains difficult to transfer. Relaxing CFOE reveals that verifier feedback and additional interaction provide limited gains, whereas successful trajectories substantially improve transfer. These findings suggest that current self-evolving agents are better at repairing observed failures than building generalizable capabilities from failure.
papers.title_zh: 自演化智能体能够修复失败，却难以从中泛化
papers.abstract_zh: 经验驱动的自演化为大语言模型（LLM）智能体通过交互持续改进提供了一条有前景的路径。然而，现有方法往往依赖成功轨迹或外部评估信号，这使得当此类正向锚点不可用时智能体能否演化仍不清楚。我们通过冷启动仅失败演化（CFOE）研究这一问题，其中智能体在起步时没有积累的经验，并且仅从失败交互中学习而没有特权引导。在三种自演化范式、多个LLM骨干模型和四个交互环境中，我们揭示出一致的修复—泛化差距：由失败衍生的经验可以帮助修复先前失败的任务，但很少能在未见任务上产生持续改进。进一步分析表明，智能体常常误解失败，而即便是经过验证正确的经验也仍然难以迁移。放宽CFOE表明，验证器反馈和额外交互带来的收益有限，而成功轨迹则显著改善迁移。这些发现表明，当前的自演化智能体更擅长修复已观察到的失败，而不太擅长从失败中构建可泛化的能力。

papers.title: Prism Attention: Proposal-Refined Index Sharing Mechanism for Efficient LLMs Inference
