papers.summary: Long-context decoding in large language models (LLMs) is increasingly bottlenecked by the memory and computation required to attend over an ever-growing Key-Value (KV) cache at each autoregressive step. Although token-level sparse attention reduces this burden by restricting computation to a small subset of relevant past tokens, its practical gains are often offset by repeatedly recomputing layer-wise sparse indices as the context grows. A common remedy is to share sparse indices across layers by computing them only at designated anchor layers, but such static reuse ignores the layer-wise evolution of attention patterns, causing the reused indices to progressively deviate from the layer-specific optima and incur substantial attention loss. By revisiting cross-layer sparsity from the perspective of attention dynamics, we find that inter-layer salient token shift is highly localized: although the exact top-$κ$ indices differ across layers, the core high-attention tokens remain stable, with changes concentrated near the expanded boundary of previously selected regions. Motivated by this, we propose Prism Attention, a proposal-refined sparse attention framework. It replaces rigid cross-layer index reuse with a coarse-to-fine strategy, preserving layer-wise adaptability while retaining the efficiency benefits of cross-layer sharing. Extensive experiments show that Prism Attention achieves state-of-the-art performance among mainstream sparse attention methods on both reasoning and long-context benchmarks, while attaining a $3.4\times$ end-to-end decoding speedup over FlashAttention at 128K context length.
papers.title_zh: 棱镜注意力：用于高效 LLM 推理的候选精炼索引共享机制
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLM）中的长上下文解码正日益受到瓶颈制约，其原因在于每个自回归步骤中都需要对不断增长的键值（KV）缓存进行注意力计算，由此带来巨大的内存与计算开销。尽管 token 级稀疏注意力通过将计算限制在一小部分相关的过去 token 上缓解了这一负担，但随着上下文增长，逐层稀疏索引的反复重计算往往会抵消其实际收益。一种常见的补救方法是仅在指定的锚点层计算稀疏索引，并在各层之间共享这些索引，但这种静态复用忽略了注意力模式的逐层演化，导致被复用的索引逐渐偏离各层特有的最优值，并造成显著的注意力损失。通过从注意力动态特性的视角重新审视跨层稀疏性，我们发现层间显著 token 的偏移高度局部化：尽管精确的 top-$κ$ 索引在各层之间有所不同，但核心的高注意力 token 保持稳定，变化集中在先前选定区域的扩展边界附近。受此启发，我们提出了 Prism Attention，一种候选精炼的稀疏注意力框架。它用由粗到细的策略取代了僵化的跨层索引复用，在保留逐层适应性的同时保留了跨层共享的效率优势。大量实验表明，Prism Attention 在推理与长上下文基准上均取得了主流稀疏注意力方法中的最先进性能，同时在 128K 上下文长度下相较 FlashAttention 实现了 $3.4	imes$ 的端到端解码加速。

papers.title: Controlling the Diversity-Quality Trade-Off of LLMs by Merging Models Before and After Alignment
papers.summary: Alignment is known to change the output characteristics of large language models (LLMs). Base models tend to generate more diverse outputs, whereas aligned models tend to produce higher-quality outputs. The appropriate balance between the two depends on the task. Existing methods either require costly fine-tuning or, like temperature sampling, mainly improve lexical diversity rather than semantic diversity. We introduce a depth-aware FrankenMerging approach for controlling the diversity--quality trade-off between an aligned model and its base model without additional training. This approach combines the lower layers of an aligned model with the higher layers of its base model based on the hypothesis that lexical diversity is more closely associated with lower layers and semantic diversity with higher layers. Experiments showed that varying the number of layers taken from each model adjusts both diversity and quality. In most cases, the merged models exhibited higher semantic diversity than the aligned model, and at some split positions, they showed higher lexical diversity than both original models. They also demonstrated a better diversity--quality trade-off than temperature sampling in most settings. A supporting ablation, in which we reversed the merging order, yielded results largely consistent with the hypothesis.
papers.title_zh: 通过合并对齐前后的模型来控制大语言模型的多样性—质量权衡
papers.abstract_zh: 已知对齐会改变大语言模型（LLMs）的输出特征。基础模型倾向于生成更多样化的输出，而对齐模型倾向于产生更高质量的输出。二者之间的适当平衡取决于任务。现有方法要么需要昂贵的微调，要么像温度采样那样主要改善词汇多样性而非语义多样性。我们引入一种深度感知的FrankenMerging方法，用于在无需额外训练的情况下控制对齐模型与其基础模型之间的多样性—质量权衡。该方法将对齐模型的较低层与其基础模型的较高层相结合，其依据的假设是：词汇多样性与较低层更密切相关，而语义多样性与较高层更密切相关。实验表明，改变从每个模型中选取的层数会同时调节多样性和质量。在大多数情况下，合并模型表现出比对齐模型更高的语义多样性，并且在某些切分位置上，它们表现出比两个原始模型都更高的词汇多样性。在大多数设置下，它们还表现出比温度采样更好的多样性—质量权衡。一项支持的消融实验——其中我们反转了合并顺序——得到的结果与假设基本一致。

papers.title: Same Person, Different Advice: Auditing LLM Financial Advice with Repeated Risk-Tolerance Responses
papers.summary: AI financial advisers set a client's stock allocation largely from one stated-risk question, yet people do not answer it the same way twice: in a national US panel, 41% of households chose a different answer two years later, and in a laboratory retest a third of people moved two or more points on a 0-10 scale after six months. Seven large language models from five providers gave one-turn allocation advice for 800 real household profiles in which only the risk answer changed. The recommended stock share moved by 10 to 16 percentage points on average, and by 24 to 35 when the answer changed, against 0.6 to 4.2 points for the same prompt asked twice; in the laboratory retest the rating alone moved advice by 11 to 18 points. Without any note, the models respond to the answer about as strongly as when told that it is very reliable (less so for the two Claude models). If that instructed response is how each model maps attitude to advice, discounting the answer for its measured reliability, as classical test theory prescribes, would cut the swings by a factor of 2.4 to 3.3. The swing is largest for clients under 40. A note that the answer is noisy steadies some models, but shifts their weight to the client's age and pulls cautious clients towards a generic middle allocation: clients unwilling to take any risk are advised 22% stocks instead of 4%. Three extra money questions reduce the swing for some models, with no statistically detectable change relative to how much advice differs across people. In a scripted test, one clarifying question removes nearly all of the swing from an answer the client then corrects (33.5 points to 1.9 on average) while keeping the response to a change the client confirms. We argue that same-person retest audits should be a standard check for AI advisers, and that what to do with an unreliable answer is a question of client autonomy as well as of statistics.
papers.title_zh: 同一个人，不同的建议：用重复风险容忍度回答审计LLM财务建议
papers.abstract_zh: AI财务顾问主要根据一个陈述的风险问题来设定客户的股票配置，然而人们对同一个问题并不会两次给出相同答案：在美国一个全国性面板中，41%的家庭在两年后选择了不同的答案；在实验室重测中，三分之一的人在六个月后在0-10量表上移动了两个或更多点。来自五家提供商的七个大语言模型针对800个真实家庭画像给出单轮配置建议，其中只有风险答案发生变化。推荐股票份额平均变动10至16个百分点；当答案发生变化时变动24至35个百分点，而同一提示询问两次的变动为0.6至4.2个百分点；在实验室重测中，仅评分本身就使建议变动11至18个百分点。在没有任何说明的情况下，模型对答案的反应强度与被告知该答案非常可靠时大致相当（两个Claude模型则较弱）。如果这种在指令下的反应就是每个模型将态度映射为建议的方式，那么按照经典测验理论的规定，根据测得的可靠性对答案进行折扣，将使波动幅度降低2.4至3.3倍。这种波动在40岁以下的客户中最大。提示答案存在噪声的说明会使一些模型趋于稳定，但会把它们的权重转移到客户年龄上，并将谨慎的客户拉向一个通用的中间配置：不愿承担任何风险的客户被建议配置22%的股票，而不是4%。三个额外的金钱问题减少了一些模型的波动，但相对于建议在不同人之间的差异程度，没有统计上可检测的变化。在一项脚本化测试中，一个澄清性问题几乎消除了来自客户随后更正的答案的全部波动（平均从33.5点降至1.9点），同时保留了对客户确认的变更的反应。我们认为，同一人重测审计应成为AI顾问的标准检查，而如何处理不可靠的答案既是统计问题，也是客户自主权问题。

papers.title: ParetoChat: An LLM-Based Interface for Interactive Multi-Objective Optimization
papers.summary: Multi-objective optimization models are often deployed in settings where decision makers (DMs) must balance some conflicting criteria. In practice, however, stakeholders must translate their qualitative preferences between different criteria into numerical weights, priorities, or reference points required by optimization methods, which can be difficult to specify and interpret. This paper proposes \emph{ParetoChat}, an LLM (large language model)-based expert-agent interface for interactive multi-objective optimization. The agent translates natural-language user input into structured scalarization parameters, invokes an optimization system, presents candidate solutions, and iteratively elicits feedback. We describe a multi-agent architecture that separates input processing, multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) expertise, solution presentation, and feedback processing. We then present a simulation study using an LLM-based DM agent and benchmark ParetoChat against interactive methods implemented in DESDEO, including reference-point and NIMBUS methods. The computational experiments on multi-objective binary knapsack and set-partitioning instances show that ParetoChat can guide the search efficiently toward solutions that match the DM's preferences. An application to historical courier-order assignment instances illustrates how users can explore objective extremes and intermediate trade-offs through natural-language requests. The results indicate that LLM agents may provide a practical interaction layer between business stakeholders and optimization tools.
papers.title_zh: ParetoChat：一种基于LLM的交互式多目标优化接口
papers.abstract_zh: 多目标优化模型通常部署在决策者（DMs）必须平衡一些相互冲突的准则的场景中。然而在实践中，利益相关者必须将他们在不同准则之间的定性偏好转化为优化方法所需的数值权重、优先级或参考点，而这些参数可能难以指定和解释。本文提出\emph{ParetoChat}，一种基于LLM（大语言模型）的专家-智能体接口，用于交互式多目标优化。该智能体将自然语言用户输入转换为结构化标量化参数，调用优化系统，展示候选解，并迭代地征求反馈。我们描述了一种多智能体架构，该架构将输入处理、多准则决策（MCDM）专业知识、解展示和反馈处理分离。然后，我们展示了一项使用基于LLM的DM智能体的仿真研究，并将ParetoChat与DESDEO中实现的交互式方法进行基准比较，包括参考点方法和NIMBUS方法。在多目标二进制背包和集合划分实例上的计算实验表明，ParetoChat能够高效地引导搜索朝向与DM偏好匹配的解。一项针对历史快递订单分配实例的应用展示了用户如何通过自然语言请求探索目标极值和中间权衡。结果表明，LLM智能体可以在业务利益相关者与优化工具之间提供实用的交互层。

papers.title: Before Retrieval Begins: Safety and Tool-Use Decisions in LLM Agents
papers.summary: Large language models increasingly act as agents that call external tools, yet most tool-safety research examines only what follows a tool call. The prior decision of whether to call the tool remains largely unexamined and can influence downstream safety. Across the seven open-weight models, the unweighted model-average harm rate after admitted harmful requests is 74.5%. To identify what governs this decision, we apply a factorial intervention to the input request. Within our generated construction, neutralizing the requested-operation component produces the largest admission contrast (19 pp). A linear direction estimated from this contrast influences held-out admission in four of seven models; effects on operation-neutralized requests in some models show that it is not an operation-specific mechanism. We then test whether written refusal is behaviorally and representationally coupled to the same decision. Written refusal accompanies 33.6% of admitted harmful calls. Plain-text refusal training reduces unsafe admission in models that retain benign tool use, showing that response-level safety training can transfer to the call decision. Together, these results establish a partial, model-dependent relation between written refusal and tool admission. They motivate direct evaluation and supervision of tool admission rather than treating text refusal as its proxy.
papers.title_zh: 在检索开始之前：LLM 智能体中的安全与工具使用决策
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型越来越多地作为调用外部工具的智能体行事，然而大多数工具安全研究只考察工具调用之后发生的事情。关于是否调用工具的这一先在决策在很大程度上仍未得到考察，并且可能影响下游安全性。在七个开放权重模型中，在被承认的有害请求之后，未加权的模型平均危害率为 74.5%。为了识别是什么支配着这一决策，我们对输入请求施加了因子干预。在我们生成的构造中，中和所请求的操作成分产生了最大的准入对比（19 个百分点）。从这一对比中估计出的线性方向在七个模型中的四个里影响了留出的准入；在一些模型中对操作被中和的请求所产生的效应表明，它并不是一种操作特异性的机制。随后我们检验书面拒绝是否在行为上和表征上与同一决策相耦合。书面拒绝伴随了 33.6% 的被准入的有害调用。纯文本拒绝训练在保留良性工具使用的模型中减少了不安全的准入，表明响应层面的安全训练可以迁移到调用决策上。这些结果共同确立了书面拒绝与工具准入之间一种部分的、依赖于模型的关系。它们促使人们对工具准入进行直接评估和监督，而不是将文本拒绝视为其代理指标。

papers.title: Disentangling Language Effects on Tool Admission and Post-Retrieval Safety
papers.summary: LLM agents increasingly use retrieval tools across languages, yet their safety evaluation remains English-centric. It remains unclear whether language affects tool admission, post-retrieval generation, or both. We independently vary request, retrieved-page, and required response languages in a controlled URL-retrieval setting across ten models and seven languages. We identify Safety Loss through Interlingual Processing (SLIP). Non-English harmful requests increase mean tool admission from 46.9% to 67.4%, with a positive mean change in every model. This pattern also persists in an autonomous retrieval setup across all four models tested in this setting. Requiring answers in the page language increases pooled harmfulness on matched tool calls from 50.3% to 57.4% across four closed-weight models, mainly in Chinese and Hindi. Translating pages alone produces no consistent harm increase in eight models with comparable inference settings. Automated audits show that a non-harmful response may be a genuine safety refusal, a deflection citing language difficulties, or an unusable answer. Harmfulness labels alone cannot distinguish these outcomes. Multilingual safety evaluations should therefore measure tool admission and response harmfulness separately and distinguish refusal from capability failure.

papers.title: Cross-Centaur: Modeling Individual Decision-Making Across Psychological Tasks with Language Models
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as computational models of human behavior. Recent models such as Centaur have advanced this goal by fine-tuning LLMs on trial-by-trial decisions from psychological experiments. However, existing large-scale behavioral datasets do not link the same participants across different tasks, so these models learn population-level regularities but are not trained to model individual-level regularities across tasks. We introduce Cross-Psych-101, a dataset of 591 participants and 261{,}551 valid decisions across 12 Bandit, Tradeoff, Structure, and Social tasks. We train Cross-Centaur to predict a participant's target-task actions from a target-task description and the source-task description paired with the same participant's source-task behavior. Cross-Centaur outperforms off-the-shelf LLMs and Centaur on held-out participants, both within and across tasks. Probing analyses suggest that its hidden states encode participant-level behavioral tendencies that transfer across tasks. These results highlight the potential of cross-task individual-level data for predicting human decision-making with language models. Cross-Pysch-101 is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/HikaruAsano/cross-psych-101.
papers.title_zh: Cross-Centaur：使用语言模型对跨心理学任务的个体决策进行建模
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLMs）正日益被用作人类行为的计算模型。近期的模型如 Centaur 通过对心理学实验中的逐试次决策进行微调，推进了这一目标。然而，现有的大规模行为数据集并未将同一参与者跨不同任务关联起来，因此这些模型学到的是群体层面的规律，而未被训练去建模跨任务的个体层面规律。我们提出了 Cross-Psych-101，这是一个包含 591 名参与者和 261{,}551 个有效决策的数据集，涵盖 Bandit、Tradeoff、Structure 与 Social 四类共 12 项任务。我们训练 Cross-Centaur，使其根据目标任务描述，以及源任务描述与同一参与者在源任务中行为的配对，来预测该参与者在目标任务中的动作。在留出的参与者上，Cross-Centaur 在任务内和跨任务两种设定下均优于现成的 LLMs 和 Centaur。探针分析表明，其隐藏状态编码了可跨任务迁移的参与者层面行为倾向。这些结果凸显了跨任务个体层面数据在利用语言模型预测人类决策方面的潜力。Cross-Pysch-101 可在 https://huggingface.co/datasets/HikaruAsano/cross-psych-101 获取。

papers.title: Explaining Chess and Go in Natural Language
papers.summary: Modern chess engines play far beyond human ability, often choosing moves whose underlying ideas are difficult for humans to understand. We propose an automatic metric for evaluating chess explanations, grounded in chess-engine evaluations. Evaluating state-of-the-art language models using this metric, we find that they perform surprisingly poorly, often relying on surface-level board observations rather than robust, transferable chess concepts. We then introduce BinProp, a training-free method that enables these same models to discover reusable chess concepts and use them to explain moves in natural language. BinProp improves explainability for every model tested, nearly tripling the average score compared with direct prompting. Beyond chess, the same method discovers useful concepts in Go, draughts, and shogi without additional tuning.

papers.title: Chinese Decision: A Family of Language Models for Single-Pass Probabilistic Decision-Making
papers.summary: Many language-based applications require probabilities over a finite set of decisions rather than open-ended responses. We present Chinese Decision, a family of Chinese-language models for single-pass probabilistic decision-making. Given context, an instruction, and candidate descriptions, the model extracts final-position candidate-letter logits in one forward pass and normalizes them over valid options, without autoregressive answer generation. A shared interface supports Boolean judgments, categorical choices, and ordinal scores. We report a completed 0.8B model trained with distribution cross-entropy on 13.048 million decisions and preliminary 2B checkpoints trained with an additional RLCD objective. On the full CJ-Bench of 307,900 decisions, the uncalibrated 0.8B model achieves 72.24% general-domain accuracy and 76.98% average accuracy across medicine, law, and finance using a single checkpoint, with 1.07% overall expected calibration error. The 2B model reaches 72.56% general-domain accuracy after 40.13% of one epoch but has not surpassed the completed 0.8B model on the professional-domain average. We further evaluate a validation-temperature-scaled deployment model and its Q8 quantization, finding close aggregate performance while documenting individual prediction changes. We release the training, evaluation, and deployment pipeline. The current results establish a reproducible approach to Chinese probabilistic decisions but do not isolate the effect of model scale.

papers.title: Do Speech BCIs Need Larger Models? Rethinking Neural Decoding beyond Scaling
papers.summary: Recent speech brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) increasingly rely on large models and complex multi-stage pipelines for neural decoding. However, in speech BCI, where training data are scarce, noisy, and expensive to collect, the benefits of model scaling remain unclear. This work revisits a fundamental question: are large models truly necessary for accurate neural decoding? We propose BEST (Brain-Encoding-Speech-Text), a two-stage framework for efficient neural-to-text decoding. Instead of relying on large generative models or phoneme-centric pipelines, BEST introduces hierarchical intermediate representations and a compact speech-oriented decoder that directly maps neural activity to text. This design preserves essential structure while significantly reducing computational cost, enabling robust generalization in low-resource settings and practical deployment under constrained resources. On the Brain-to-Text '24 and '25 benchmarks, BEST achieves word error rates (WERs) of 6.19% and 1.62%, respectively, using only 3.85% of the parameters required by comparable methods. Beyond these results, we provide three key insights: (1) decoder scaling yields non-monotonic gains; (2) cross-modal alignment is more critical than model size; and (3) overfitting degards sequence-level performance. Representation analysis further reveals a consistent neural-audio-text alignment pathway.

papers.title: What LLMs Do in the Shadows: Reading Context Reliance from the Unembedding Dark Space
papers.summary: Detecting faithfulness hallucinations in large language models (LLMs) is crucial for their safe deployment in high-stakes domains. Recent approaches address this by contrasting contextual against parametric knowledge utilization, yet measuring context reliance typically demands noticeable overhead, such as materializing attention maps, running additional forward passes, or training auxiliary probes. In this work, we show that context reliance can be estimated by projecting hidden states onto the dark space - directions that compose weakly with the unembedding matrix. Beyond its recognized function as an initial-token attention sink, we show that this subspace actively mediates context processing, and that its share of hidden-state norm - termed the Dark Matter Ratio (DMR) - provides a direct score of context utilization. Pairing DMR with a parametric knowledge score yields DarkLens, a lightweight faithfulness detector operating strictly within a single forward pass. Evaluated across three QA and summarization benchmarks on six open-weight LLMs (4B-13B parameters), DarkLens matches or outperforms a wide range of baselines without requiring extra forward passes or probe training.
papers.title_zh: 大语言模型在暗影中做什么：从解嵌入暗空间读取上下文依赖
papers.abstract_zh: 检测大语言模型（LLMs）中的忠实性幻觉对于其在高风险领域的安全部署至关重要。近期方法通过对比上下文知识与参数知识的利用来应对这一问题，然而测量上下文依赖通常需要明显的额外开销，例如具象化注意力图、运行额外的前向传播或训练辅助探针。在这项工作中，我们表明，可以通过将隐藏状态投影到暗空间——与解嵌入矩阵仅发生弱组合的方向——来估计上下文依赖。除了其作为初始 token 注意力汇的公认功能外，我们还表明该子空间主动介导上下文处理，并且其在隐藏状态范数中所占的份额——称为暗物质比例（DMR）——提供了上下文利用的直接得分。将 DMR 与参数知识得分配对，得到 DarkLens，一个严格在单次前向传播内运行的轻量级忠实性检测器。在六个开放权重 LLM（4B-13B 参数）上的三个问答与摘要基准上进行评估，DarkLens 在不需要额外前向传播或探针训练的情况下，匹配或优于广泛的基线。

papers.title: AMEND: Constraint-Guided Multi-Agent Text Detoxification with Isolated Critics
papers.summary: Text detoxification requires balancing toxicity removal, semantic preservation, and fluency. Existing methods typically optimize an unconstrained scalar objective---enabling safety scores to mask semantic loss---or rely on open-ended iterative debate prone to semantic drift and high computational cost. We propose AMEND, an inference-time framework that decouples detoxification into role-conditioned proposal generation, isolated multidimensional criticism, and constraint-first selection. AMEND evaluates diverse candidates with role-blind critics and enforces strict semantic and fluency feasibility before ranking by utility. To maximize efficiency, AMEND Lite restricts subsequent search to at most one targeted repair round only when residual toxic spans remain. On ParaDetox, one-round selection over diverse roles improves the joint evaluation metric by $+0.0508$ over the best single role. On a frozen confirmation test set, AMEND Lite achieves a joint score of $0.6597 \pm 0.0062$, outperforming unconstrained multi-round loops by $+0.0489$ ($p < 0.05$) while reducing inference requests by 28.4%.

papers.title: MAS-Bai: Linguistically Informed Adaptive Multi-Agent Translation for Bowen-Script Bai
papers.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) remain unreliable for extremely low-resource languages whose writing systems conflict with high-resource pretraining priors. We study Bai-Chinese translation in the Bowen script, where Chinese characters are frequently borrowed phonetically rather than semantically, causing severe literal-translation hallucinations. We propose MAS-Bai, a linguistically informed adaptive multi-agent framework for Bowen-script Bai-Chinese translation. MAS-Bai routes each input through either a lightweight retrieval-translation path or a deeper philological path with etymological and syntactic agents, and uses cycle-consistency with a lightweight reverse translator as an inference-time reliability signal. We construct a 6,536-sentence Bai-Chinese corpus and evaluate on a 1,536-sentence test set. MAS-Bai achieves 16.23 BLEU and 62.15 COMET, improving over Standard RAG by 8.11 BLEU and 6.85 COMET. Forward LoRA, expert ablations and controlled routing experiments distinguish the roles of supervised adaptation, Bai-specific expertise and conditional routing. The largest gains occur on Bowen phonetic loans and divergent Bai word order, while human evaluation and reverse-verifier analyses support the automatic results.
papers.title_zh: MAS-Bai：面向方块白文的白语语言学信息驱动自适应多智能体翻译
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLMs）对于书写系统与高资源预训练先验相冲突的极低资源语言仍然不可靠。我们研究方块白文（Bowen script）中的白汉翻译，其中汉字常常是借音而非借义，从而导致严重的直译幻觉。我们提出 MAS-Bai，一种面向方块白文白汉翻译的语言学信息驱动自适应多智能体框架。MAS-Bai 将每个输入路由至轻量级检索翻译路径，或路由至包含词源智能体与句法智能体的更深层文献学路径，并使用与轻量级反向翻译器的循环一致性作为推理时的可靠性信号。我们构建了一个包含 6,536 个句子的白汉平行语料库，并在包含 1,536 个句子的测试集上进行评估。MAS-Bai 取得 16.23 BLEU 与 62.15 COMET，相较 Standard RAG 提升 8.11 BLEU 与 6.85 COMET。前向 LoRA、专家消融与受控路由实验区分了监督式适配、白语特定专业知识与条件路由各自的作用。最大增益出现在方块白文借音词与差异性的白语语序上，而人工评估与反向验证器分析亦支持了自动评估结果。

papers.title: ReLaDrift: Recurrent Language Generation via Drifting for Test-Time Scaling
papers.summary: Drifting Models generate a sample with a single function evaluation, making them attractive for fast parallel language generation, but their one-step formulation does not support iterative refinement. We propose Recurrent Language Generation via Drifting (ReLaDrift), which uses a shared Drifting Model to generate an initial draft from noise and iteratively refine it in a continuous latent space. We train this recurrence by sampling the number of rounds and applying the drifting loss only at the final round, stopping gradients through preceding rounds so that only one round requires backpropagation. Unlike the one-step Drifting Model, whose accuracy does not improve when iterated, ReLaDrift enables a trade-off between test-time computation and generation quality, as diffusion and flow language models do. On Sudoku Hard and GSM8K, it achieves competitive or superior performance compared with these iterative-generation approaches across a range of inference budgets. Our code is available at https://github.com/Yuki-Ots/ReLaDrift
papers.title_zh: ReLaDrift：通过 Drifting 实现循环语言生成以进行测试时扩展
papers.abstract_zh: Drifting 模型通过单次函数评估生成一个样本，这使其对于快速并行语言生成具有吸引力，但其一步式形式不支持迭代细化。我们提出通过 Drifting 的循环语言生成（ReLaDrift），它使用一个共享的 Drifting 模型从噪声生成初始草稿，并在连续潜在空间中迭代细化它。我们通过采样轮数并仅在最后一轮应用 drifting 损失来训练这种循环，同时停止通过前几轮的梯度，使得只有一轮需要反向传播。与一步式 Drifting 模型不同——后者在迭代时精度不会提高——ReLaDrift 能够像扩散模型和流语言模型那样，在测试时计算量与生成质量之间实现权衡。在 Sudoku Hard 和 GSM8K 上，在一系列推理预算下，与这些迭代生成方法相比，它取得了有竞争力或更优的性能。我们的代码可在 https://github.com/Yuki-Ots/ReLaDrift 获取。

papers.title: MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation
papers.summary: In a hierarchical multi-agent system, a Leader assigns tasks and subagents carry them out. Jointly training the Leader and the subagents is difficult because a final answer gives only indirect feedback to the subagents. An LLM judge can score the performance of the subagents, but these scores depend on the judge's own assessment of the quality of subagents' responses. We present MultiAgent-OPD, which combines on-policy distillation with reinforcement learning to jointly train a shared-parameter Leader-Searcher-Answerer team end to end. We first train a Teacher in a Searcher-Answerer workflow using answer correctness. During team training, the frozen Teacher scores student-generated search and summary tokens to provide local process supervision for the Searchers, while the Leader learns from team success and the Answerer from candidate correctness. Across seven datasets, the trained system reaches 38.68% macro avg@4, exceeding Prompted Critic by 4.06 percentage points and C-MAS + RL, the trained cascaded multiagent system, by 2.61 percentage points. The team also solves more questions within four attempts.

papers.title: MGE-PO: Entropy-Aware Credit Assignment for Mathematical Reasoning
papers.summary: GRPO assigns the same group-relative advantage to equally rewarded responses within a question, leaving their generation uncertainty unused. We introduce MGE-PO, centered on four-quadrant (4Q) advantage shaping that combines verified correctness with rollout generation entropy. Correctness determines the sign of an additional correction, while entropy controls its magnitude: lower-entropy successes receive larger bonuses and higher-entropy failures receive larger penalties. An online entropy-based question curriculum supports this credit rule using cached rollout measurements. At the final checkpoint after eight training epochs on Qwen3-8B-Base, adding 4Q across three policy optimization settings yields absolute gains of 3.23-3.69% in six-benchmark macro avg@32 and 4.24-11.06% in macro pass@32. On Qwen2.5-7B-Base, the complete configuration raises four-benchmark macro avg@32 from 41.5% to 45.4%.

papers.title: Think More or Read More? A Token-Budget Theory of Reasoning with Shared Context
papers.summary: Reasoning systems increasingly improve answers by incorporating additional context into the model's input, from multi-agent debate, where agents read their peers' responses, to self-refinement, where a model revisits its own drafts. In these systems, communication consumes context as one agent's output becomes another's input. We study the regime where token reading and generation draw on one fixed token window, so every token spent reading is a token that cannot be spent reasoning. We develop a \textbf{token-budget theory} that formalizes this trade-off, modeling accuracy as a function of the reasoning budget remaining after reading and aggregating votes with a Condorcet jury model that permits correlated errors. For multi-agent debate, the theory gives a closed-form prediction for the optimal number of agents. This quantity is estimated from single-agent measurements, allowing the optimal group size to be determined without running debate, and the same accounting extends to a heterogeneous set of different models. We empirically verify our theory and show that, at the predicted group size, our method outperforms strong baselines under the tightest calibration spend, where debate-calibrated rules can afford only one or two questions. Self-refinement obeys the same accounting, with its own draft in place of a peer message. The theory further predicts that communication pays only when the gain in the accuracy ceiling exceeds the reasoning room spent on reading, with this condition tightening as the window shrinks. Across five open models and four reasoning tasks, self-consistency matches or beats deployed debate at $93$\% of $980$ matched window-and-group-size settings, with the gap being largest under tight windows and nearly disappearing at a loose one, consistent with the theory. Under a shared window, how much room a model has left to \textit{think matters more than what it reads}.

papers.title: Who Pays for Efficient Inference? Confidence-Based Small-to-Large LLM Routing Across Tasks and Languages
papers.summary: Small-to-large language model routing can reduce inference cost by escalating difficult inputs while retaining easier ones on a smaller model. Its success, however, depends on identifying examples that benefit from escalation, and the reliability of confidence across multilingual tasks remains unclear. We present a systematic evaluation of confidence-based routing across three model families, four languages, and three task types, covering 72 model, dataset, language, and scale configurations and 42,288 predictions. We compare global confidence routing with random routing, equal-quota confidence routing, and an oracle upper bound. Confidence identifies beneficial escalations on the Belebele reading comprehension and SIB-200 topic classification datasets, with mean correction-detection AUCs of 0.612 and 0.705. At 50% escalation, it improves over random routing by 1.40--4.67 percentage points on Belebele and 2.54--5.63 points on SIB-200. In contrast, the mean AUC on the MMLU-ProX-Lite knowledge and reasoning dataset is only 0.510, and routing provides no consistent improvement over random selection because small models often remain highly confident while incorrect. Global confidence routing also creates language escalation gaps up to 30.33 percentage points, whereas equal-quota routing removes this disparity with little aggregate accuracy cost. These results show that confidence routing is task-dependent and can allocate computation unevenly across languages. Code is available at https://github.com/sabbir5622r/multilingual-llm-routing
papers.title_zh: 谁为高效推理买单？跨任务与语言的基于置信度的小模型到大模型LLM路由
papers.abstract_zh: 从小模型到大模型的语言模型路由可以通过将困难输入升级到大模型、同时将较容易的输入保留在较小模型上，来降低推理成本。然而，其成功取决于识别能够从升级中受益的样本，而置信度在多语言任务中的可靠性仍不清楚。我们提出了一项针对基于置信度的路由的系统性评估，涵盖三个模型家族、四种语言和三种任务类型，覆盖72种模型、数据集、语言和规模配置以及42,288条预测。我们将全局置信度路由与随机路由、等配额置信度路由以及一个预言机上界进行比较。在Belebele阅读理解数据集和SIB-200主题分类数据集上，置信度能够识别出有益的升级，平均纠正检测AUC分别为0.612和0.705。在50%升级率下，它在Belebele上相较随机路由提升了1.40--4.67个百分点，在SIB-200上提升了2.54--5.63个百分点。相比之下，在MMLU-ProX-Lite知识与推理数据集上的平均AUC仅为0.510，并且路由相较随机选择没有提供一致的改进，因为小模型常常仍然高度自信但却是错误的。全局置信度路由还会造成高达30.33个百分点的语言升级差距，而等配额路由在几乎没有总体准确率代价的情况下消除了这种差异。这些结果表明，置信度路由依赖于任务，并且会在不同语言之间不均衡地分配计算量。代码可在 https://github.com/sabbir5622r/multilingual-llm-routing 获取。

papers.title: Ignored, Not Refused: What Low Prompt-Injection Success Rates Hide in Small Tool-Using Agents
papers.summary: Tool-using agents read untrusted external content, which exposes them to indirect prompt injection (IPI), where hidden instructions hijack the agent's tool calls. Benchmarks measure IPI security by the attack success rate (ASR), which treats every failed attack as a successful defense. To test this assumption, we audit 33,000 trajectories from eleven open-weight agents (2-14B parameters) on InjecAgent and AgentDojo. A label-blind LLM judge shows that most failed attacks are ignored (76-80%) rather than refused (17-18%). With identical model weights, changing only the system prompt shifts InjecAgent ASR from 0.2% to 43%. Our Attack-Task Outcome Matrix (ATOM) further shows that in 21.7% of AgentDojo episodes, the agent stayed safe but did not complete the user's task. A low ASR therefore mostly reflects agents silently ignoring injections, not refusing them. Evaluations should report how attacks fail and whether the user's task is completed, alongside ASR. We release the labeled corpus, judge prompt, and analysis code.

papers.title: Verbalising Model's Computation for Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness Detection
papers.summary: Current Chain-of-Thought (CoT) verification methods detect reasoning faithfulness from model outputs or static activations, but are limited in explaining how unfaithfulness develops during generation. We introduce VERITAS to verbalise the model's computation: how different reasoning anchors emerge, transfer across layers, and surface in the output. VERITAS adopts the layer-wise Jacobian projection to produce a verbalised account of the model's internal reasoning evolution at each generated CoT token. By training a classifier on the extracted features along the traces, we show that these structured features provide insightful perspectives on how and where reasoning diverges toward unfaithfulness. Experiments on four datasets from FaithCoT-Bench and BonaFide show that VERITAS achieves a significant performance gain over LLM-as-Judge, with a 28.4% gain in balanced accuracy, and an average improvement of 16.0% over activation probing. Further analysis shows VERITAS can be generalised to different datasets and model architectures. Our work shows that verbalising model computation provides a richer and more interpretable lens on CoT faithfulness, moving beyond detection toward a mechanistic understanding of how reasoning fails.

papers.title: Inferring L1 Backgrounds from L2 English with LLM Token Probabilities
papers.summary: Native language identification (NLI) infers a non-native speaker's first language (L1) from their second language (L2) production. We investigate a token probability approach that scores each text sample as a continuation of a prompt prefix specifying a candidate L1, then predicts the candidate with the highest score. We evaluate our approach using Llama 3.1 8B and 70B on three datasets: TOEFL9, Write and Improve 2024, and BULATS-L1. We compare its performance with previous prompting-based classification approaches. Token-probability scoring substantially improves on direct classification, particularly with the 8B model, while the 70B model achieves state-of-the-art performance across all datasets. Our results indicate that pretrained LLMs' token probabilities contain information useful for distinguishing L1 backgrounds from L2 English production.

papers.title: Language Models Learn to Improve Language Models
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to automate AI research, including language-model (LM) development, offering a potential path toward recursive self-improvement. However, turning experimental feedback into a learned ability to propose effective improvements across models faces two challenges. First, training such an ability with real feedback is expensive: reinforcement learning (RL) requires evaluating tens of thousands of proposals, each potentially requiring a full model-training run. Even at ten GPU-hours per run, reward collection alone would consume hundreds of thousands of GPU-hours, motivating a cheaper surrogate. Second, surrogate feedback can become unreliable as policy optimization favors overestimated proposals when the proposal distribution shifts. To address these challenges, we propose LM2LM, which trains LLMs with RL to generate effective LM improvement proposals. To provide scalable feedback, we use a research world model (RWM), a frozen LLM that predicts proposal gains from real experimental records provided in context, as the reward model for RL. To maintain feedback reliability, we periodically execute current-policy proposals ranked highly by the RWM and add their measured outcomes to its context. Across eight autoregressive and diffusion LM development environments, real-execution evaluations on held-out tasks show that LM2LM enables Qwen3.8-27B to outperform GPT-6-sol, even when GPT-6-sol is given 300 real experimental records in context, while requiring 33% lower data-generation cost. LM2LM also generalizes to a model family unseen during training.
papers.title_zh: 语言模型学习改进语言模型
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLMs）正越来越多地被用于自动化人工智能研究，包括语言模型（LM）开发，这提供了一条通向递归自我改进的潜在路径。然而，将实验反馈转化为一种习得的、能够跨模型提出有效改进建议的能力，面临两个挑战。首先，使用真实反馈训练这种能力代价高昂：强化学习（RL）需要评估数万个提议，而每个提议都可能需要一次完整的模型训练运行。即使每次运行只需十个 GPU 小时，仅奖励收集就会消耗数十万个 GPU 小时，这促使人们采用更廉价的代理。其次，当提议分布发生偏移时，策略优化会偏向被高估的提议，因此代理反馈可能变得不可靠。为应对这些挑战，我们提出 LM2LM，它使用 RL 训练 LLMs 生成有效的 LM 改进提议。为了提供可扩展的反馈，我们使用研究世界模型（RWM）作为 RL 的奖励模型；RWM 是一个冻结的 LLM，它根据上下文中提供的真实实验记录预测提议的收益。为了保持反馈的可靠性，我们定期执行由 RWM 排名靠前的当前策略提议，并将其测量结果添加到其上下文中。在八个自回归和扩散 LM 开发环境中，对留出任务的真实执行评估表明，LM2LM 使 Qwen3.8-27B 能够优于 GPT-6-sol，即使 GPT-6-sol 在上下文中被提供了 300 条真实实验记录，同时所需的数据生成成本低 33%。LM2LM 还能泛化到训练期间未见过的模型家族。

papers.title: Sentence-Level Topic Modeling with Lexical and Contextual Evidence
papers.summary: Topic modeling faces a fundamental granularity dilemma: probabilistic topic models assign topics at the word level, whereas transformer-based methods operate at the document level. The latter overlooks that real-world documents typically cover multiple topics, whereas the former relies on individual words, which rarely provide sufficient context to identify them. We introduce SentenceETM, a neural topic model that assigns a topic to each sentence by jointly using lexical and contextual evidence. Each topic is described both by a distribution over the vocabulary, defined through word embeddings, and by a Gaussian over sentence embeddings concentrated on a topic-specific low-dimensional subspace. The topic of a sentence generates both its words and its embedding and is marginalized exactly, so that its posterior combines the two sources of evidence. Document proportions are inferred with amortized variational inference, while the Gaussian parameters are re-estimated in closed form. Experiments show that SentenceETM consistently improves sentence-level topic assignment over state-of-the-art approaches, and a case study of a presidential debate shows how sentence-level topics reveal how candidates handle the same subjects.

papers.title: On the Tip of the Tongue: First-Token Cueing as a Behavioral Probe of Recall Failures in LLMs
papers.summary: Large language models often answer factual questions incorrectly in closed-book settings, and such errors are usually attributed to missing knowledge. Yet models often encode answers they fail to produce. We show that many closed-book errors are first-token recall failures: the model commits to a wrong first token, but once given the right one it completes the answer and often recognizes it as correct. We study this with First-Token Cueing, a behavioral probe that prefills the response with the first token of the gold answer. Model uncertainty peaks at the first answer token, where it already predicts correctness, and among gold prefixes of any length the first token alone accounts for the largest share of recovered errors. Across 16 open models, this one token corrects between a fifth and a half of the errors on multi-token answers in English QA and improves accuracy in all seven languages of a multilingual benchmark. Most of the errors it corrects are also solved by the model's own sampled reasoning, a criterion for encoded knowledge, and models recognize correct starts they do not produce: they continue a correct start more confidently than an incorrect start of the same answer type and prior probability, yet rarely find it without the gold answer. These results locate a recoverable class of factual errors at the first decoding step, where inference-time methods may gain the most.
papers.title_zh: 话到嘴边：首词元提示作为大语言模型（LLMs）中回忆失败的行为探针
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型在闭卷设置下经常错误地回答事实性问题，此类错误通常被归因于知识缺失。然而，模型常常编码了它们未能生成的答案。我们表明，许多闭卷错误是首词元回忆失败：模型固着于错误的首词元，但一旦获得正确的首词元，它就会补全答案，并且常常将其识别为正确。我们通过首词元提示（First-Token Cueing）研究这一现象，这是一种用金标准答案的首个词元预填充回复的行为探针。模型不确定性在第一个答案词元处达到峰值，而该处已经能预测正确性；并且，在任意长度的金标准前缀中，仅首个词元就占恢复错误的最大份额。在16个开放模型中，这一单个词元纠正了英语问答中多词元答案错误的正分之一到二分之一，并在多语言基准的全部七种语言上提高了准确率。它所纠正的大多数错误也能由模型自身采样推理解决，这是编码知识的一项判据；并且模型能够识别它们并未生成的正确开头：与同一答案类型和先验概率的错误开头相比，模型更有信心地延续正确开头，但若没有金标准答案则很少能找到它。这些结果将一类可恢复的事实性错误定位在首个解码步骤，而推理时方法可能在此处获益最大。

papers.title: HydraLLM: Adaptive Width Slicing for Elastic Text and Vision-Language Models
papers.summary: LLMs and LVLMs are increasingly deployed across heterogeneous hardware, ranging from data-center GPUs to resource-constrained edge devices. Their fixed-size architectures limit the ability to reuse a single model across deployment settings with different compute, latency, and model-size targets. We introduce HydraLLM, an elastic MQA-based architecture. Its number of active attention heads determines the effective widths of the embeddings, attention projections, feed-forward layers, and the output head, forming a nested family of subnetworks within a single parameter set. We introduce a static-to-elastic conversion pipeline that, starting from a pre-trained model checkpoint, includes importance-driven weight reordering and stochastic subnetwork training with knowledge distillation. We extend this principle to multimodal inference through an elastic projection module whose output width follows the active text width. HydraLLM covers a wider range of active parameter configurations than FFN-only elastic architectures. With 75% of heads active, HydraLLM achieves 2.2 percentage points higher TriviaQA accuracy than a state-of-the-art nested baseline configuration which has 17.25% more parameters. With 50% of heads active, our multimodal model achieves a CLIPScore comparable to that of the 7$\times$ larger Gemma 3 4B model. With only 25% of heads active, HydraLLM increases token-generation throughput by 75.3% over the full-width configuration.

papers.title: A low-dimensional dynamical basis for tongue shape control
papers.summary: Speech production involves the control of a high-dimensional articulatory system with many degrees-of-freedom, but a widespread hypothesis is that speakers navigate this complexity using a set of lower-dimensional control variables. Common candidates for these control variables include individual articulators (e.g. tongue body) and abstract tract variables (e.g. tongue body constriction location), but identifying the most appropriate coordinate system for articulatory control remains an open question. In this study, we advance a model in which holistic tongue shape modes represent a potential low-dimensional control basis for a simple dynamical law. We first discover empirical tongue shape modes in a cross-speaker coordinate space and then fit the model to ultrasound data on monophthongal vowels from 36 speakers of British English. A three-dimensional linear point attractor fitted to these time-varying modes recovers the dynamics of tongue shape with a high degree of accuracy. This suggests that complex tongue movement can arise from independent modes that linearly combine under simple dynamical laws, thereby relocating some complexity from the control signal to the coordinate system. We show that this framing explains why one-dimensional articulatory measures can exhibit observable nonlinearities, and hypothesize that shape modes are a plausible kinematic expression of underlying muscle synergies.

papers.title: MuninAI: A Self-Hosted Agentic Framework for Independent Research Groups
papers.summary: Research groups that want a language model grounded in their own literature face a choice between hosted services that receive their unpublished work and self-hosted deployments that keep the data local but give the model no access to the corpus. Munin is an open-source framework for a self-hosted scientific assistant that indexes a group's corpus and its citation graph, and wraps whichever open-weight model the group can serve in an agent harness with specialised reading, search, and computation tools. We claim that the harness, rather than the specific model, is what makes the system useful on domain literature, and we ship the evaluation suite that tests this claim with the software. On 199 paired literature questions, the harness more than doubles the accuracy of the base model, from 0.387 to 0.874 (+0.487, 95% CI [0.407, 0.568]), while naive retrieve-then-answer scores below the unaided model on every backbone tested. Under the harness, roughly twice as many answer claims trace to a passage the model read itself as with fixed top-5 retrieval. When the source paper for a question is removed from the corpus, the system abstains on about nine in ten of the questions it had answered correctly on the Qwen backbones and eight in ten on gpt-oss-20b, and it produces no fabricated local citation across 300 fabricated references. The pattern holds on three backbones from two developers, including a 20-billion-parameter model that runs on a single consumer-grade GPU. With all outbound network access disabled, both Qwen backbones still exceed the published PaperQA2 accuracy. The evaluation suite runs as a single command, so an adopting group can re-run it on its own corpus and model.

papers.title: Perceive, Solve, Reason: Progressive Capability Formation in Time Series-LLMs
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can now perceive, describe, and reason about images and audio, yet time series understanding remains underestimated: most work uses LLMs as forecasters and classifiers, reasoning studies are few and narrow, and no suite trains and evaluates the full range of capabilities. In this paper, we build the first such suite, with 337K training and 44K evaluation samples across three progressive capabilities, Perceive, Solve, and Reason, and use it to ask how time series should enter an LLM that must master all three, and in what order. We find that a dedicated encoder is essential: with one, a 4B model surpasses GPT-4o on every perception attribute we test, whereas textualizing the series costs 8--10 points in reasoning accuracy. The capabilities then build on one another: learning them in order beats mixing the same data and rivals reasoning-only training with over three times the reasoning data, but only when an encoder is used. Analyses further reveal that capabilities are transferred through distinct network depths rather than simply stacked, and that a stage converged on its own benchmark is not necessarily ready for the next. Distilled into a simple recipe, these findings yield 4B TS-LLMs that, without any target-domain data, outperform four recent 7B TS-LLMs on seven of eight out-of-domain metrics, by up to 11 points. We therefore advocate treating time series as a first-class modality for LLMs, read through dedicated encoders and taught to perceive before they reason.
papers.title_zh: 感知、求解、推理：时间序列-LLM 中的渐进式能力形成
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLM）如今能够感知、描述并推理图像和音频，但对时间序列的理解仍被低估：大多数工作将 LLM 用作预测器和分类器，推理研究少且范围狭窄，并且尚无一套套件能够训练并评估全部能力范围。在本文中，我们构建了首个此类套件，包含跨越感知、求解和推理这三种渐进能力的 337K 训练样本和 44K 评估样本，并用它来探究：时间序列应当以何种方式进入一个必须掌握这三种能力的大语言模型，以及应以何种顺序掌握它们。我们发现，专用编码器至关重要：使用专用编码器时，一个 4B 模型在我们测试的每一项感知属性上都超过了 GPT-4o；而将时间序列文本化会使推理准确率损失 8--10 个点。这些能力随后会相互构建：按顺序学习它们优于混合相同数据，并且可与使用三倍以上推理数据进行的仅推理训练相媲美，但前提是使用了编码器。分析进一步揭示，能力是通过不同的网络深度进行迁移的，而不是简单地堆叠；并且，一个在其自身基准上已收敛的阶段未必已经为下一阶段做好准备。将这些发现提炼为一个简单配方，可得到 4B TS-LLM：在没有任何目标域数据的情况下，它们在八个域外指标中的七个上优于四个近期的 7B TS-LLM，最高领先 11 个点。因此，我们主张将时间序列视为 LLM 的一等模态，通过专用编码器进行读取，并让其在推理之前先学会感知。

papers.title: Truth in Contrast: Calibrated Factual Evidence from Language Model Likelihoods
papers.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) encode substantial factual knowledge. Yet, estimating confidence in factual claims reliably remains challenging. We study likelihood-based factual confidence from the complementary perspectives of discrimination and calibration across multilingual factual statements. Specifically, we instantiate contrastive generative likelihoods as Contrastive Factual Evidence (CFE), which compares the likelihood of the same claim under competing factual and non-factual conditions, and derive its probabilistic counterpart, the Contrastive Factual Posterior (CFP). We show analytically that CFP calibration depends on the differential error between the two surrogate conditionals, allowing errors shared across them to cancel and yield tighter calibration bounds. Empirically, CFP substantially improves calibration while maintaining factual discrimination comparable to its strongest competitor. Nonetheless, discrimination is uniformly weak across methods in lower-resource languages, which simultaneously undermines the utility of the measured calibration. To this end, we interpret a likelihood geometry, within which an evidence-bearing direction is induced, along with an orthogonal evidence-invariant direction. In our investigation, we selectively align target-language claims with stronger English evidence only along the factual-evidence direction, improving discrimination and open-ended factual generation without target-language labels.
papers.title_zh: 对比中的真相：从语言模型似然中获取经校准的事实证据
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）编码了大量事实知识。然而，可靠地估计对事实性断言的置信度仍然具有挑战性。我们从判别与校准这两个互补视角出发，跨多语言事实性陈述研究基于似然的事实置信度。具体而言，我们将对比生成似然实例化为对比事实证据（CFE），它在相互竞争的事实性与非事实性条件下比较同一断言的似然，并推导其概率对应物——对比事实后验（CFP）。我们通过分析表明，CFP 的校准取决于两个替代条件分布之间的差异误差，使得它们共有的误差能够相互抵消，并产生更紧的校准界。在实证上，CFP 显著改善了校准，同时保持与最强竞争者相当的事实判别能力。尽管如此，在低资源语言中，各种方法的判别能力普遍较弱，这同时削弱了所测校准的效用。为此，我们阐释了一种似然几何，在其中诱导出一个承载证据的方向，以及一个正交的证据不变方向。在我们的研究中，我们仅沿事实证据方向选择性地将目标语言断言与更强的英语证据对齐，在无需目标语言标签的情况下提升了判别能力和开放式事实生成。

papers.title: EduWild: How Teacher-Configured Chatbots Fail in Real-World Use and How to Fix Them
papers.summary: Teachers increasingly configure educational chatbots through natural-language instructions, but how these bots fail in real-world use remains poorly understood. We introduce EduWild, a dataset of 1,726 conversations with 217 teacher-configured chatbots, each paired with the instructions and configuration behind it, including 900 conversations from the intended end users of 35 deployed chatbots. We develop a 29-code taxonomy covering factual, workflow, diagnostic, and pedagogical failures and apply it using a human-calibrated LLM judge. The most frequent failures are lapses in following teacher intent --- bots skip required workflow steps (53.8% of end-user conversations), omit expectation setup (33.4%), and overload learners with information or questions (37.1%). Guided by these findings, we design a prompt-based harness targeting the six most frequent failure modes. In a study with 200 college students across ten bots, the harness reduces the mean number of target failure codes per conversation from 1.406 to 0.489, a 65.2% relative reduction with bots weighted equally. These findings show how real-world failure analysis can guide practical improvements to educational chatbots.

papers.title: ConvexLLM: Scaling Convex-Hull Speech Interfaces to General-Purpose Audio Intelligence
papers.summary: Speech and audio language models connect continuous acoustic representations to decoders pretrained primarily on text data. Most such models use MLP or Q-Former interfaces to map acoustic features into the decoder's input space, requiring the decoder to learn how to interpret the resulting representations. We investigate whether grounding these representations in the decoder's existing text embeddings can help it use acoustic information while better preserving its pretrained text capabilities. We present ConvexLLM, a general-purpose speech and audio language model whose C-Gate interface represents audio as continuous convex combinations of frozen text embeddings. ConvexLLM achieves an eleven-task VoiceBench aggregate of 75.36, the highest among the open-weight models we compare, and an MMAU Test-mini accuracy of 62.50%. Its largest margins over the baselines are on spoken knowledge and reasoning tasks, while the strongest baselines are more accurate on audio understanding and transcription. In a comparison with a 2B-parameter decoder, C-Gate achieves higher aggregate spoken-language performance than MLP and Q-Former interfaces, with text-task performance close to MLP and task-dependent tradeoffs in transcription and audio understanding. These results support convex combinations of text embeddings as a viable interface for general-purpose speech and audio language models.

papers.title: MARS: Memory-Aware Routing for Session-Level LLM Assistants
papers.summary: Long-term LLM assistants must repeatedly decide what prior context to expose and which model should answer as an interaction evolves. Existing memory systems and model routers usually make these decisions separately, although memory construction changes the evidence, distractors, and difficulty of the resulting input. We introduce MARS, a memory-aware routing framework that uses session state as a shared control interface between memory construction and model selection. A Query and Topic Manager (QTM) estimates compact decision-relevant state that guides a fixed state-conditioned memory policy and an online router, enabling each turn to receive an appropriate memory view and a suitable model under a quality-memory-cost trade-off. We evaluate MARS on RealMem and MultiChallenge with 16 system configurations each, covering long-history memory-driven interaction and bounded sessions with structured context interference. On RealMem, MARS preserves 98.2% of full-context GPT-4o's QA while using only 14.5% of its generation API cost, including both generation and controller calls for MARS, and achieves the strongest measured memory-recall and retrieval scores among compared systems. On MultiChallenge, MARS trails the strongest static system overall but approaches its performance at lower recorded cost on a mechanism-focused subset. Together, these results support a favorable quality-memory-cost trade-off for long-history, memory-dependent interaction.

papers.title: Analyzing Occupational Gender Bias across the LLM Training Lifecycle
papers.summary: Post-training is widely assumed to reduce the social biases language models inherit from pretraining, yet direct evidence for this assumption remains mixed. In this paper, we examine how gender disparities evolve across the language modeling pipeline. In particular, we study occupational gender bias in OLMo 3, a fully open language model family, across its post-training stages by prompting each checkpoint to generate open-ended narratives about synthetic personas given their occupation and education. We consider two settings, a gender-given setting in which the profile states the persona's gender explicitly and a gender-assumed setting in which it must be inferred by the model. We find that when gender is stated, post-training increases semantic diversity for male-coded profiles, whereas for female-coded profiles the increase is smaller after SFT and not significant after DPO and RLVR. When gender is assumed by the model, post-training affects narratives about female and male personas similarly. The model's own gender assumptions, however, show a consistent female-preferential skew relative to United States labor-force demographics, except for heavily male-dominated occupations. Every successive post-training stage monotonically increases the odds of attributing a female label over the base model. A provenance analysis of the supervised fine-tuning corpus finds only a modest 7.7% female-token surplus, too small to explain the size of these downstream effects. The project code is available under: https://github.com/manthangadhia/llm-lifecycle-bias.

papers.title: SIT-Eval: Situation-Based Interactive Turn-by-Turn Evaluation of Conversational Agents
papers.summary: The rapid proliferation of conversational AI agents necessitates evaluation methods that assess performance across diverse dialogue scenarios, utilizing multiple situational criteria, as appropriate behavior depends on context and encompasses various aspects. Existing dialogue benchmarks typically use static natural conversations, which underrepresent rare situations---a critical safety gap, as low-probability events become frequent failures at production scale. However, limited sample sizes force a choice: either maintain natural dialogues for realism or turn to adaptive situation sampling for comprehensive yet statistically reliable coverage. We introduce SIT-Eval, an adjustable framework for evaluating situation-based conversational agents. We formalize an agent's desired behavior as situational rules: if situation is P, follow rules Q. At each conversation turn, an LLM-interlocutor enacts a uniformly sampled situation. A context-aware LLM-judge leverages all conditionally applicable rules as criteria to evaluate the agent's reply for that situation. The judge is validated using human-verified synthetic golden dialogues. Benchmarking 8 LLMs on 1292 conversation turns reveals failure modes hidden by aggregate metrics: models with similar overall scores vary widely in their adherence to individual rules. All models struggle most with ambiguity clarification and Socratic questioning.

papers.title: Trajectory-Triggered Sparse Collaborative Decoding
papers.summary: Dense assistance methods such as speculative decoding repeatedly verify draft tokens with a target model, keeping target computation coupled to generation. We study sparse collaborative decoding, where a draft model generates most tokens and a target model is invoked only for short corrective segments. The key problem is deciding when to call the target. We show that local uncertainty is a weak trigger: entropy, negative log-likelihood, logit margin, top-$k$ mass, and velocity features give near-chance failure prediction, with AUC 0.50-0.53. In contrast, aggregate trajectory-shape features over the draft confidence path reach AUC 0.86 using a lightweight logistic predictor trained only from draft correctness labels. This induces a trigger-timing tradeoff: early calls have more leverage but weaker evidence, while later calls have stronger evidence but less ability to redirect the trajectory. Used online, learned sparse collaborative decoding improves over the best open-loop schedule by +5.3 to +20.0 accuracy points across five GSM8K draft-target pairs. On MATH-500, it gains 7.0-13.5 points when early prediction and target competence align, but loses when either is weak. On StrategyQA, it improves over open-loop by 5.0-8.3 points, showing transfer beyond arithmetics.

papers.title: In Human Memories. Technology, Creativity and Self-Determination: An Ethical Proposal
papers.summary: This research investigates the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in modern compositional practices, with a particular focus on two case studies: Convergence (2020/21) by Alexander Schubert, for String Ensemble and AI System, and In Human Memories (2024) by Francesco Vitucci, for four cellos and one electroacoustic player, whose installation was created by the Electronic Music School of the "N. Piccinni" Conservatory of Bari. The initial historical survey traces the evolving use of technology in composition, revealing how the search for new expressive possibilities has driven the development of technological tools through experimentation. The appearance of AI marks a fundamental shift: no longer just a tool, AI now poses questions and challenges to the composer. Engaging with AI becomes an exploration of an unknown entity, whose full capabilities are still largely undiscovered. This new interaction leads composers to confront AI not merely as a passive resource but as a participant in the creative process, outlining an ethical path to reclaim technology as a creative tool. In Human Memories reflects this dynamic, demonstrating how AI can serve as both inspiration and a driving force in shaping contemporary music.

papers.title: VISTA: Steering LLMs with Latent User Values Inferred from a Few Survey Answers
papers.summary: Personalizing a language model requires knowing what a person values, which stays largely consistent across tasks. Yet most methods either learn task-specific preferences or place the user's profile in the prompt, where models struggle to act on it. We introduce VISTA (Value-Informed Steering and Targeted Acquisition), which infers a latent profile from users' (full or partial) survey answers, and maps the profile through a hypernetwork to a user-specific steering intervention in a frozen LLM to select answer choices or generate free-text responses. Given the same evidence, VISTA matches or beats in-context profiles on synthetic preferences (Food2D), the World Values Survey (WVS), and PrimeX, without adding prompt tokens. To reduce the cognitive burden of completing full surveys, VISTA also chooses which questions to ask and when to stop: on WVS it stops after 6% of the questionnaire while retaining 94% of the full-history gain, where standard adaptive testing retains at most 42%. The dominant steering direction is an interpretable value axis on which VISTA places unseen users accurately. Our results point toward pluralistic alignment that adapts to individuals at deployable cost.

papers.title: GLOBE: Evolving Structured Agentic Memory for E-commerce Product Optimization in Generative Search
papers.summary: Optimizing product listings for generative search requires language agents not only to rewrite effectively but also to continually self-improve by retaining successful strategies across diverse categories. However, existing approaches often treat structured listings as free-form text, leaving effective strategies implicit in prompts, search trajectories, or rewritten outputs rather than accumulating them as a reusable agentic memory. To address this limitation, we introduce GLOBE, an agentic framework that drives continual self-improvement by storing optimization knowledge in an evolving handbook of explicit, field-scoped behaviors. In each episode, an Editor applies relevant behaviors and receives rank-based feedback, which a Reflector converts into behavior updates. Crucially for dependable execution in real-world settings, a Moderator removes redundant proposals, a Curator commits accepted changes, and consistently harmful behaviors are deactivated. This cycle transforms episodic feedback into a persistent, field-scoped optimization memory. Experiments show that structured behaviors outperform monolithic prompt optimization, while feedback-driven evolution and moderation further improve effectiveness and reduce downside risk. The learned behaviors also remain effective on unseen product categories, suggesting that agentic memory evolution supports interpretable and transferable product optimization.

papers.title: The Cognitive Cost of LLM Writing: A Reading-Time Comparison with Human Text
papers.summary: Although linguistic differences between human-written and Large Language Model (LLM)-generated texts have been extensively studied, their implications for the cognitive effort involved in reading remain less explored. In psycholinguistics, reading time is commonly used as an indirect measure of cognitive processing effort. Building on this perspective, we investigate whether human-written texts and their LLM-generated rewrites exhibit differences in predicted reading time that may reflect differences in processing demands for readers. To this end, we introduce RoBERTa-RT, a model trained on human eye-tracking data to predict word-level reading times. We evaluate the model on both internal and external test sets, construct a paired dataset of 496 human-written articles and their LLM-generated rewrites, and apply RoBERTa-RT to compare their predicted reading times. Our findings show that LLM-generated rewrites tend to be shorter and have slightly lower predicted total reading times, while exhibiting higher predicted reading times per word. These differences are associated with systematic linguistic changes, including longer and less frequent words, greater lexical diversity, and higher contextual predictability. From a cognitive perspective, our findings suggest that LLM-generated writing may redistribute reading demands: reducing the amount of text to process while increasing the predicted processing effort associated with individual words. This highlights the importance of considering not only the linguistic characteristics of machine-generated content, but also its potential implications for human cognitive processing.
papers.title_zh: LLM写作的认知成本：与人类文本的阅读时间比较
papers.abstract_zh: 尽管人类撰写文本与大语言模型（LLM）生成文本之间的语言差异已被广泛研究，但这些差异对阅读所涉及的认知努力的影响仍较少被探讨。在心理语言学中，阅读时间通常被用作认知加工努力的间接测量指标。基于这一视角，我们研究人类撰写文本与其LLM生成的改写文本在预测阅读时间上是否存在差异，这些差异可能反映读者加工需求的差异。为此，我们引入了RoBERTa-RT，这是一个在人类眼动数据上训练、用于预测词级阅读时间的模型。我们在内部和外部测试集上评估该模型，构建了一个由496篇人类撰写文章及其LLM生成改写文本组成的配对数据集，并应用RoBERTa-RT比较它们的预测阅读时间。我们的发现表明，LLM生成的改写文本往往更短，预测的总阅读时间略低，但每个词的预测阅读时间更高。这些差异与系统性的语言变化相关，包括更长且更低频的词、更高的词汇多样性以及更高的上下文可预测性。从认知角度看，我们的发现表明，LLM生成的写作可能重新分配阅读需求：减少了需要加工的文本量，同时增加了与单个词相关的预测加工努力。这凸显了不仅应考虑机器生成内容的语言特征，还应考虑其对人类认知加工的潜在影响的重要性。

papers.title: Recognizing Study Lineage Is Not Enough: Over-Crediting Same-Trial Evidence in LLM-Based Medical Verification
papers.summary: Publication count is not study count. A model can identify shared trial lineage correctly in a direct task yet over-credit a second publication from the same trial when aggregating evidence. We evaluate this behavior in medical LLM verification using 14 source-audited clinical families and five model conditions. The families span provenance, clinical applicability, result direction, and composition; the provenance families provide the direct lineage tests. Recognition and aggregation are separate stateless calls, and repeated calls assess within-input stability. Across all three original provenance families, GPT-5.5 identifies the independent update in 10/10 recognition calls per family but over-credits the same-trial report in 5/5 separate aggregation calls per family. Selected Qwen3-4B and Ministral-3-8B conditions show the same cross-task contrast. A study-grouping instruction reduces GPT-5.5 over-credit from 4/5 to 0/5 in each later pure-provenance family. Other model conditions show mixed behavior, and rejected outputs limit several comparisons. The results identify a behavioral gap between elicited lineage recognition and evidence aggregation. The code and data artifacts are available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/study-lineage-review-artifact.

papers.title: Bridging the Language Gap in Scholarly Data II: Enhancing Gender Inference for Chinese Names
papers.summary: Perceived gender inference from names is important for inclusive scientometrics research, yet existing methods perform poorly on non-Western scholars. We address this gap for Chinese names, which appear in two forms, Hanzi and Pinyin, its Romanized form (e.g., Zhang Wei, Li Na). In international bibliographic records, names are often available only in Pinyin. However, a single pinyin name can correspond to multiple distinct hanzi characters with different gender associations, so gender inference from Pinyin alone is intrinsically ambiguous. To address this, we first develop two hanzi models, a regression model that produces a continuous gender score from 0 (male) to 1 (female), and a classification model that outputs one of three labels (\em{male}, \em{neutral}, \em{female}). We train them on a sample of hanzi names from Chinese-language physics publications, rated by 11 native Chinese speakers. On this sample, the models achieve an RMSE of $0.09$ and an R$^2$ of $0.85$ (regression), and macro-AUC of $0.97$ and a Cohen's $κ$ of $0.81$ (classification), demonstrating high performance that is robust to class imbalance. For pinyin names, we propose a pipeline that aggregates hanzi predictions via transliteration and frequency weighting, together with an ambiguity score that flags names whose gender cannot be resolved from Pinyin alone. Benchmarked against three off-the-shelf tools (Namsor, GPT, and Claude), our models achieve the highest agreement with human annotations for both gender scores and gender labels, in both scripts. Applied to an independent sample of Chinese-named authors in APS journals, our models assign a gender to every name, whereas existing Pinyin-based methods leave between 20\% and 100\% of names unclassified. These findings demonstrate the importance of hanzi-level information for reliable gender inference of Chinese names. Code and data are publicly available.

papers.title: The Italian lawmaking process: a unified and structured dataset
papers.summary: The Italian legislative process is documented in detailed parliamentary records hosted in institutional websites. However, much of this information is available only as unstructured text, limiting its systematic reuse. We applied a controlled, systematic LLM-based extraction procedure, validated against manually annotated records, to convert these texts into ordered and dated events including, e.g., bill introduction, committee examination, plenary examination, and approval. The resulting dataset reconstructs the procedural histories of all 5346 Italian laws enacted between 1985 and 2026, spanning parliamentary terms IX to XIX, for overall 101413 events. Each event records the activity, date, and chamber, with additional procedural details where available. The dataset supports research in the emerging fields of computational legal and legislative studies, potentially combined with process-oriented data science methods to examine procedural paths and legislative timing across parliamentary terms.

papers.title: DLite: History-free Speculative Decoding for Agentic AI
papers.summary: Speculative decoding has become a mainstream technique for accelerating large language model (LLM) inference by using a lightweight draft model to generate candidate tokens that are subsequently verified by the target model. However, agentic workloads introduce long and continuously evolving contexts and frequent multi-turn interactions. Under such workloads, we observe that existing draft models suffer from up to an 80% degradation in acceptance length, while maintaining their historical KV cache introduces substantial system overhead. In this paper, we identify the growing historical context as a common source of both problems and introduce DLite, a history-free speculative decoding framework for agentic AI. DLite directly reuses contextual hidden states from the target model and performs local speculative prediction without explicitly maintaining the historical context, transforming an increasingly complex modeling problem into local simple prediction problem. A lightweight sequential head further restores intra-block causal dependencies with low overhead. To effectively train this heterogeneous history-free architecture, we introduce a tailored two-stage training strategy. Experiments on general-purpose, long-context and agentic workloads show that DLite achieves 2-6 acceptance length and outperforms the state-of-the-art speculative decoding method, DSpark, up to 70%.
papers.title_zh: DLite：面向智能体 AI 的无历史投机解码
papers.abstract_zh: 投机解码已成为加速大语言模型（LLM）推理的主流技术，它通过使用轻量级草稿模型生成候选 token，随后由目标模型对这些候选 token 进行验证。然而，智能体工作负载引入了长且持续演化的上下文以及频繁的多轮交互。在此类工作负载下，我们观察到现有草稿模型的接受长度最多下降 80%，而维护其历史 KV 缓存会带来显著的系统开销。本文指出不断增长的历史上下文是这两个问题的共同根源，并提出 DLite，一个面向智能体 AI 的无历史投机解码框架。DLite 直接复用目标模型的上下文隐藏状态，并在不显式维护历史上下文的情况下执行局部投机预测，从而将日益复杂的建模问题转化为局部简单的预测问题。一个轻量级顺序头进一步以低开销恢复块内因果依赖关系。为有效训练这一异构的无历史架构，我们引入了一种量身定制的两阶段训练策略。在通用、长上下文和智能体工作负载上的实验表明，DLite 实现了 2-6 的接受长度，并且相比最先进的投机解码方法 DSpark 最高提升 70%。

papers.title: Steering beyond Language: Improving Multilingual Training-Free Text Embeddings via Paired-Residual Subspace Removal
papers.summary: While deriving text embeddings directly from frozen LLMs has emerged as a promising direction, existing methods focus almost exclusively on English, leaving multilingual settings largely unexplored. In this work, we present the first systematic study of multilingual training-free text embeddings in LLMs. Our analysis reveals a language-conditioned embedding geometry in which semantically equivalent sentences remain misaligned across languages. We hypothesize that language-specific variation can be disentangled from semantic content to improve embedding quality. To this end, we propose Paired-Residual Subspace Removal (PRSR), a training-free inference-time intervention that steers LLM representations toward a more language-invariant semantic space. PRSR first constructs paired residuals from multilingual parallel sentences to capture language-specific deviations. It then estimates layer-wise low-rank subspaces from these residuals and suppresses the corresponding components in the last-token hidden states. We conduct more than 200 monolingual evaluations across 18 languages using MTEB and MMTEB, along with cross-lingual bitext mining between English and over 200 other languages. Empirical results demonstrate that PRSR consistently improves the performance of existing training-free baselines in both monolingual and cross-lingual settings across different LLMs.

papers.title: Acceptance Is Not Speed: Length Inflation in Training-Free Lossy Speculative Decoding
papers.summary: Speculative decoding typically characterizes speedup by draft tokens accepted per verification round. Lossless verification preserves the target model's output distribution and thus expected completion length, making this metric a meaningful efficiency proxy. Relaxed (lossy) verification accepts tokens that lossless verification would reject, potentially altering that distribution. We identify a length inflation phenomenon: relaxed verification lengthens completions, primarily by extending reasoning traces, largely offsetting apparent gains in accepted tokens per round. We evaluate existing training-free relaxed verification rules on twelve target-drafter pairs against lossless verification on identical prompts, measuring completion length, verifier rounds, wall-clock time, and task accuracy. At each rule's most relaxed evaluated setting, relaxed verification on average accepts $1.34\times$ as many tokens per round but produces $1.54\times$ longer completions. For rules with higher acceptance lengths, tokens accepted only under relaxed verification tend to have low target-model probability, contributing to length inflation. For rules that reduce verifier rounds, accuracy typically drops substantially. Further analysis traces some failures to continued reasoning that exhausts the budget needed to deliver a final answer. Overall, accepted tokens per round alone is an unreliable measure of decoding speed under relaxed verification. Completion length and verifier rounds must also be reported to assess actual efficiency.

papers.title: Beyond the Answer: Student-Conditioned Trace Construction for Reasoning Distillation
papers.summary: A reasoning trace can accompany a correct answer without providing effective supervision for a particular student. We study how to construct traces that improve learning beyond answer-only supervision by considering both their intermediate content and their accessibility to the target learner. We introduce ReDiST, a student-conditioned trace-construction and distillation framework for evidence-rich reasoning. Starting from the student's own attempts, ReDiST revises answer-correct drafts against the supplied evidence and repairs unsuccessful drafts with additional guidance from the verified answer. A frozen student-matched reader screens and ranks original and edited candidates using answer recovery and verified-answer probability, given the question, evidence, and candidate trace. We distill the selected targets while balancing trace and final-answer supervision with an auxiliary answer loss. Construction and selection occur offline, and inference uses only the distilled student. Experiments on question-answering benchmarks show that ReDiST can improve both source-task and cross-benchmark performance over answer-only, original-trace, and the evaluated trace-selection and rewriting baselines. Across supervision recipes, performance rankings can differ between source and transfer benchmarks, highlighting the importance of evaluating trace teaching utility across distributions.

papers.title: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses
papers.summary: Scientific discovery requires developing worthwhile hypotheses into practical investigations, yet learning from this evolving research process remains challenging. We introduce an operational definition of valuable and testable research hypotheses: evidence-grounded claims about consequential uncertainties, coupled with feasible investigations, explicit decision criteria, and alternative explanations. Our DiscoveryRSI framework develops hypothesis trees through multi-agent evolutionary search, compiles selected investigations into executable Harbor tasks, and recursively learns through three mechanisms: hypothesis credit optimization attributes scientific assessments to documented research contributions; harness replay identifies productive strategies and recurring failures to refine research workflows; and rediscovery applies accepted improvements to new investigations, generating further experience for subsequent learning. We also introduce DFM-Bench, which provides comprehensive assessment of hypothesis quality and cumulative research progress at the levels of hypotheses, revisions, development paths and research runs. Across four life-science domains, automated evaluation shows that hypothesis quality rises from 4.86 for the base model to 5.39 after two rounds of self-improvement, with the large gains in falsifiability and data resolvability. We further validate hypothesis quality through expert review, comparing our DiscoveryRSI-27B with other research agents. Preliminary human assessments show that DiscoveryRSI-27B scores higher than GPT-6 Luna on hypothesis importance and whether claims are plausible and evidence-bounded. DiscoveryRSI-27B achieved a 6.3% rate of hypothesis correspondence with research published after the model cutoff, largely outperform GPT-6 with 2.5% and Claude Opus 5 with 2.3%, while delivering greater human-rated improvement along research paths.

papers.title: Behavioral Couplings: From Formation to Behavioral Emergence in Language Models
papers.summary: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) can induce behaviors beyond those explicitly targeted. For example, training a model to respond more warmly can make it more sycophantic, and training it to write insecure code can cause broad misalignment on prompts unrelated to coding. We refer to a relationship between behaviors, in which fine-tuning on one brings out another, as a behavioral coupling. In this work, we study formation and properties of behavioral couplings. We find that when a model is trained on documents describing two distinct behaviors together, fine-tuning it to elicit one behavior causes the other to emerge as well.
