Computed exactly, the floor and the best filter of each degree predict two spectral networks adapted from published architectures to within a tenth of a decade. A filter escapes the floor only if it weighs separately the offsets the adjacency lumps together, and must still resolve the coupling across the whole lattice. A strided filter of about fifty coefficients does both: fitted to the training labels, its test error is 52 times below the best published network's. A dilated convolutional network beats the best published result at 256 nodes, matches it at 1,024, and gives the first in-domain results at the three larger sizes, while a Fourier neural operator with its standard modes falls further behind as the lattice grows. At its standard budget the dilated network stays two to four orders of magnitude short of a larger strided filter fitted to the labels. The analysis carries over to the benchmark's second coupling.

papers.title: OrderFlowDiT: Transport-Regularized Diffusion Transformer for Probabilistic Limit-Order Supply Forecasting
papers.summary: We study the conditional distribution of limit-order volume submitted over the next five minutes, given the current order book and recent order flow. The task requires capturing price placement, total volume, and predictive uncertainty jointly. Coordinate-wise diffusion losses do not explicitly account for price displacement, while normalizing fields to unit mass removes information about total volume. Agreement on selected summary statistics also does not establish fidelity to the joint field distribution. We introduce OrderFlowDiT, a conditional Diffusion Transformer for unnormalized bid and ask volume-at-price fields, trained with an unbalanced optimal-transport (UOT) auxiliary loss. We also develop a full-field evaluation framework that combines a transport cost sensitive to price placement and total volume with proper scoring rules and calibration diagnostics. In the primary comparison on 1950 validation conditions across 30 U.S. equities, adding UOT reduces full-field transport cost by 45.8% and the transport energy score by 26.1% relative to training with mean squared error alone. Both measures improve for every stock. These findings support incorporating price geometry and volume into generative modeling, with field accuracy and predictive uncertainty evaluated together.
papers.title_zh: OrderFlowDiT：用于概率性限价订单供给预测的传输正则化扩散 Transformer
papers.abstract_zh: 我们研究在给定当前订单簿和近期订单流的条件下，未来五分钟内提交的限价订单量的条件分布。该任务要求联合刻画价格挂单位置、总量和预测不确定性。逐坐标的扩散损失并未显式考虑价格位移，而将字段归一化为单位质量则会移除关于总量的信息。在选定的汇总统计量上达成一致，也不能确立对联合字段分布的保真度。我们提出 OrderFlowDiT，一种面向未归一化买价与卖价价格-成交量字段的条件扩散 Transformer，并使用非平衡最优传输（UOT）辅助损失进行训练。我们还开发了一个全字段评估框架，该框架将对价格挂单位置和总量敏感的传输成本与适当的评分规则及校准诊断相结合。在覆盖 30 只美国股票的 1950 个验证条件上的主要比较中，与仅使用均方误差训练相比，加入 UOT 使全字段传输成本降低 45.8%，传输能量分数降低 26.1%。这两项指标对每只股票均有改善。这些发现支持将价格几何与成交量纳入生成建模，并将字段准确性与预测不确定性一起评估。

papers.title: Native Geometry vs. Linear Recoverability: How Alignment Changes Platonic Scaling
papers.summary: Do larger models learn increasingly similar representations of the same world? The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) predicts that they should, but similar can mean native cosine geometry---nearest-neighbour structure induced by cosine similarity before any learned alignment---or linear recoverability: correspondence revealed by a supervised linear map. Using matched Legacy Survey and Hyper Suprime-Cam (HSC) embeddings across five model families, we find that Ridge alignment strengthens the relationship between model size and cross-dataset neighbourhood correspondence relative to native cosine geometry. The effect appears in all five families and persists when both representations are reduced to dimension, so it is not simply that wider embeddings give alignment more dimensions to work with. The learned maps remain far from rotations or uniform scaling, and Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) and Block-Sparse Featuriser (BSF) features give no advantage over the same alignment applied to dense embeddings. Model scale thus improves linear recoverability more clearly than native cosine-neighbourhood correspondence, without establishing convergence toward a shared native metric geometry.

papers.title: Refusal Is Not Robustness: Measuring Harmful Reachability in Autoregressive Language Models
papers.summary: LLM safety evaluations via jailbreaking typically index on attack success rate (ASR): whether a generated response violates safeguards. However, ASR only evaluates sampled outputs and provides little information on the underlying generation process. Autoregressive language models define distributions over possible outputs, and a sampled refusal can coexist with substantial probability mass on harmful generation paths. We study this hidden structure through bounded continuation analysis (BCA), which models autoregressive generation as a stochastic process over token prefixes and computes the finite-horizon probability that generation reaches a harmful continuation. BCA constructs a bounded continuation tree, labels terminal continuations with a semantic harm evaluator, and estimates harmful reachability using exact probabilistic model checking. BCA complements ASR by measuring how much harmful behavior remains accessible beneath a sampled safe response. This makes it useful for distinguishing models that look identical under measured ASR values, and allocating red-team effort toward regions of the generation process with greater hidden risk. Across four instruction-tuned LLMs and 100 JailbreakBench behaviors, we show that BCA effectively quantifies hidden harmful behavior and provides a useful signal to guide red teaming.

papers.title: Acquisition Function-Guided Generation for Bayesian Optimization over Discrete Spaces
papers.summary: Bayesian optimization (BO) over discrete spaces is challenging due to missing gradients and the sparsity of valid solutions. Latent-space BO sidesteps both issues by fitting a surrogate in the latent space of a generative model, which however substantially complicates the direct incorporation of domain knowledge that is naturally expressed in the original discrete space. In this work, we instead combine a pretrained generative model with a surrogate defined directly in data space, where inductive biases such as domain-specific kernels can be readily incorporated. Rather than maximizing the acquisition function over the discrete design space, our method samples candidates from the generative model under a distribution tilted by the acquisition function. To recover useful gradients for sampling, we embed this tilted distribution into a diffusion bridge that yields a smooth, posterior-averaged acquisition function. This leads to \emph{acquisition function guided generation} (AFGG), which we instantiate with a categorical diffusion model and an autoregressive normalizing flow. Across a broad suite of molecular benchmarks, the diffusion model variant performs on par with leading BO methods, while the flow model variant outperforms state-of-the-art methods in most cases and remains highly competitive otherwise. Our implementation is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/afgg.
papers.title_zh: 面向离散空间贝叶斯优化的采集函数引导生成
papers.abstract_zh: 离散空间上的贝叶斯优化（BO）由于缺少梯度以及有效解的稀疏性而具有挑战性。潜空间BO通过在生成模型的潜空间中拟合代理模型来回避这两个问题，然而这极大复杂化了直接融入那些自然地在原始离散空间中表达的领域知识。在这项工作中，我们转而将预训练的生成模型与直接在数据空间中定义的代理模型相结合，其中诸如领域特定核等归纳偏置可以很容易地被纳入。我们的方法不是在整个离散设计空间上最大化采集函数，而是在由采集函数倾斜的分布下从生成模型中采样候选。为了恢复用于采样的有用梯度，我们将该倾斜分布嵌入到一个扩散桥中，从而产生一个平滑的、后验平均的采集函数。这引出了\emph{采集函数引导生成}（AFGG），我们用分类扩散模型和自回归归一化流对其进行实例化。在广泛的一组分子基准上，扩散模型变体与领先的BO方法表现相当，而流模型变体在大多数情况下优于最先进的方法，并在其他情况下仍具有高度竞争力。我们的实现可在 https://anonymous.4open.science/r/afgg 获取。

papers.title: Reusing Calibration Gains across Model Representations
papers.summary: Scale calibration learns an update for one model representation. We study how much of that update can be reused by another representation of the same pretrained model. Our transfer procedure extracts positive group-wise gains and installs them in the recipient's weights or native quantization scales without recipient-side optimization. On a quantized recipient, it preserves integer codes, zero points and storage layout. For a Qwen3-1.7B floating-point/GPTQ INT3 pair, bidirectional transfer retains 76.9-90.5% of the text-loss improvement from recipient-specific calibration on fresh WikiText and C4 cohorts excluded from project development. Shuffling the same gain values within each projection worsens both recipients, showing that their learned group assignment matters after transfer. A Llama-3.2-3B control keeps the initial native tensors at all four calibrated projections identical and changes nine projections elsewhere. Cross-installation retains 98.6-99.3% of the text-calibration benefit, alongside a small, resolved preference for each recipient's own gain. These results quantify both the adaptation carried by a reusable calibration update and the remaining benefit of recipient-specific training.

papers.title: Next Token or Vector? Learning How Far to Decode
papers.summary: Standard autoregressive decoding advances one token at a time, even when several upcoming tokens can be predicted together. We propose CADENCE (Context-Adaptive DEcoding), a generation method that learns both what to draft and how far to draft. Gaussian prediction heads represent future spans as continuous latent vectors, and a shared decoder converts the selected vector into token predictions in parallel. A learned router selects the prediction length from the model's own hidden states and predicted Gaussian parameters, adapting generation granularity to the current context with single-token generation as a fallback. The backbone verifies each proposed continuation and retains the prefix that matches its greedy predictions. Experiments with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on Alpaca, GSM8K, and HumanEval show that router-selected positions yield higher draft acceptance than applying the corresponding prediction length everywhere. CADENCE achieves up to 1.3x higher generation throughput than standard greedy decoding.

papers.title: Ori: Drift-Aware Streaming $k$-PCA for Very Low-Rank LLM Training
papers.summary: A prominent family of low-rank LLM optimizers, pioneered by GaLore, performs gradient-subspace projection: at each step, they project the gradient into a low-dimensional subspace and map the update back to the full model. Most existing work either recomputes the gradient subspace at certain intervals, or performs post-hoc adaptation to catch up to the moving subspace. In this work, we explicitly identify in practice the slow, stable manner in which LLM gradient subspaces drift across time. To this end, we propose Ori, a novel low-rank optimizer for training LLMs that captures the shifting principal gradient directions over time to achieve state-of-the-art accuracy under stringent low-rank constraints. Ori employs a streaming $k$-PCA algorithm inspired by Oja++, whose low per-step cost enables high-frequency, on-the-fly subspace tracking. In practice, Ori reduces the performance gap of the state-of-the-art low-rank optimizers to full-rank optimizers by up to 69.3\% on a 1B LLaMA pretraining task, and achieves the best performance on 10 out of 16 task scenarios in Roberta-Base fine-tuning. Together, these contributions allow Ori to further push the performance and efficiency frontiers of gradient-projecting optimizers, narrowing the gap to full-rank training for LLMs. Code can be found at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/Ori-Submission-2132.

papers.title: Partial-Revelation Panel Forecasting: Predictive Information Gain, Allocation, and Coarsening-Consistent Operators
papers.summary: We study partial-revelation panel forecasting: given $k$ of $n$ annotator votes on the previous dialogue turn, predict the full count distribution of the next turn's panel. This cross-turn predictive information differs from same-item annotation value. Under any nested revelation mechanism, the population decrement satisfies $V(k)-V(k+1)=I(Y;R_{k+1}\mid X_k)$; a fitted model also contributes adjacent excess-risk differences. Coarsened-completely-at-random (CCAR) masking supplies the exchangeable random-rater interpretation used in our operators. We define coarsening-consistent panel operators with a closed-form Dirichlet-multinomial realization, learned completion, and rater-count transfer. Against per-level lookup, cold-start count negative log-likelihood differences are -0.422/-0.166/-0.014 nats on IEMOCAP/M3ED/EmoWOZ. A held-out rater experiment measures same-item value: first and second additional votes reduce NLL by 0.583/0.221, 0.578/0.184, and 0.180/0.069 nats, respectively. Cross-turn and same-item gains are not interchangeable, and CCAR masks are controlled interventions rather than observed arrival processes. Consistency is auditable but does not guarantee predictive improvement; per-level marginalization can outperform a shared table. Target-free allocation beats uniform only where row-level signal is predictable: at budget one it recovers 83--93% of retrospective feature class headroom on IEMOCAP/M3ED but does not improve EmoWOZ. Gains are modest and corpus-dependent, with several small or null partial-revelation differences. Code and aggregate result artifacts accompany the preprint.

papers.title: Benchmarking and Enhancing Agentic Causal Discovery
papers.summary: LLM agents can now run causal discovery algorithms on a dataset and report what comes out. Whether they do more than that, such as noticing where an algorithm went wrong and fixing it with further tests, is hard to tell from current benchmarks. Most of them give the variables meaningful names, and an LLM shown only the names of the Tübingen cause-effect pairs already gets 99% of the directions right. With the names removed, the data are usually clean enough that picking a better algorithm than PC closes most of the gap. We introduce Heuresis, a benchmark of anonymous simulated datasets whose mechanisms range from linear Gaussian to heavy-tailed. For each family of datasets it separates what a better existing algorithm can gain from what only a closer look at the data can gain, and it traces every edge an agent changes. Every family leaves a gap that none of the algorithms, the router and the two causal-discovery foundation models we ran can close, so a score above the best chosen algorithm has to come from using the data. We instantiate the benchmark with an agent harness and three LLMs, GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5 and Qwen 3.8 Flash. GPT-6.1 Sol surpasses the best chosen algorithm on all six families, by 14% adjacency F1 on the most difficult one, and Claude Opus 5.5 does so by 7.4% there. A third of the true edges the two agents restore on the two hardest families appear in no algorithm's output. The code and data will be publicly released to facilitate future work.

papers.title: Learning to Be Guided: Shaping Latent Geometry for Classifier-Free Guidance
papers.summary: Classifier-free guidance (CFG) is a standard component of conditional diffusion models, and guided generation performance has become the \textit{de facto} measure of state-of-the-art models. Recent work on latent diffusion models seeks to learn latent spaces that are easier to model with diffusion. However, under CFG, generation additionally depends on how conditions are arranged in the latent space. We study this arrangement under discrete class conditions, termed \emph{class geometry}, and investigate what class geometry allows a latent space to work well with CFG. Under a Gaussian class model, we show that shifting variance from intra- to inter-class at fixed total variance makes classes more distinguishable under noise, and derive a noisy posterior objective whose per-sample descent direction is proportional to the oracle CFG correction. Based on the analysis, we propose Prototype Regularization (PR), a lightweight surrogate for the intractable noisy posterior objective, which applies a cosine prototype classifier to spatially pooled latents. With a controlled training budget (20 epochs for VAE, 80 epochs for DiT), adding PR to an LDM baseline reduces guided gFID on ImageNet from 3.31 to 2.28, surpassing a DINOv3-aligned VA-VAE (2.44) with negligible overhead. We further demonstrate that PR generalizes to pseudo-labels derived from clustering, continuous text-embedding conditions, and video latents. Together, our findings highlight class geometry as a critical factor in guided generation and take a first step toward CFG-compatible representation learning. Our project page is available at: https://maps-research.github.io/cfg-geometry/.
papers.title_zh: 学习被引导：为无分类器引导塑造潜在几何
papers.abstract_zh: 无分类器引导（classifier-free guidance，CFG）是条件扩散模型的标准组成部分，而引导生成性能已成为最先进模型事实上的衡量标准。近期关于潜在扩散模型的工作试图学习更容易用扩散建模的潜在空间。然而，在 CFG 下，生成还额外依赖于条件在潜在空间中如何排列。我们在离散类别条件下研究这种排列，称之为类别几何，并探究什么样的类别几何能使潜在空间与 CFG 良好配合。在高斯类别模型下，我们表明，在总方差固定的情况下，将方差从类内转移到类间会使类别在噪声下更具可区分性，并推导出一个含噪后验目标，其逐样本下降方向与 oracle CFG 校正成正比。基于该分析，我们提出原型正则化（Prototype Regularization，PR），它是难以处理的含噪后验目标的一种轻量级代理，将余弦原型分类器应用于空间池化后的潜在表示。在受控训练预算下（VAE 为 20 个 epoch，DiT 为 80 个 epoch），将 PR 加入 LDM 基线可将 ImageNet 上的引导 gFID 从 3.31 降至 2.28，以可忽略的开销超过与 DINOv3 对齐的 VA-VAE（2.44）。我们进一步证明，PR 可泛化到由聚类得到的伪标签、连续文本嵌入条件和视频潜在表示。总之，我们的发现突显了类别几何作为引导生成中的关键因素，并朝着与 CFG 兼容的表示学习迈出了第一步。我们的项目页面见：https://maps-research.github.io/cfg-geometry/。

papers.title: Batched Contextual Reinforcement II: Does RLVR Need Long Rollout Windows?
papers.summary: Long rollout windows make reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) expensive, yet simply shortening them can remove the correctness signal: when every single-problem rollout truncates before an answer, group-relative accuracy advantages vanish. As a technical continuation of Batched Contextual Reinforcement (BCR), we study how concurrent rewards relax this dependence on long windows. Concurrent Constraint Reinforcement (CCR) places three independently verifiable problems in one capped training completion. Correct answers completed before truncation retain credit, while a shared budget encourages shorter useful reasoning without an explicit length penalty. We connect this mechanism to conditional reward- and update-variance analyses and study 4B and 8B mathematical reasoning models. Against single-problem GRPO with a 32k window, CCR with an 8,000-token window reduces tokens per training step from 975,464 to 174,957 on 4B and from 793,832 to 165,788 on 8B, saving 82.1% and 79.1%, respectively. An 8B training trace shows increasing accuracy reward alongside shorter completions. Single-problem evaluations provide supporting evidence of retained reasoning quality. These results identify reward-preserving training structure as a practical route to lower per-step cost in short-window RLVR.

papers.title: What Accuracy Hides In Learned Transformer Programs
papers.summary: Transformer Programs (TP) (Friedman et al., 2023) constrain a Transformer's architecture so that its learned computation can be extracted as readable Python code. TP expose learned computations, but token accuracy can hide incorrect complete answers. In this work, we examine how program inspection provides insights beyond accuracy scores and helps guide training. We first evaluated TP on nine algorithmic tasks. We compared token accuracy with accuracy on complete output sequences and checked for failures missed by sampled tests. Further, we assessed training data improvements informed by program inspection and failure analysis, finding gains in sequence accuracy on several tasks. We examined a counting task where a program achieved 100% accuracy on sampled test sequences but failed on another input using the symbols and lengths allowed during training. The program counted correctly, but the required answer was missing from its output labels. After adding training examples with larger counts, the retrained models passed exhaustive evaluation over the bounded domain. In the frequency ranking task, inspection showed how correct counts contributed to incorrect answers in programs trained before and after changes to the training data. Finally, we studied constraints imposed by TP training and operations. The TP training process can lead to accuracy losses late in training. Our reference constructions also show how composing the restricted TP operations can use many layers or large lookup tables.

papers.title: A Feature Selection Layer Approach for Multi-Class Classification on Neural Networks
papers.summary: In the age of data-driven decision-making, deep learning models have become powerful tools for uncovering patterns and making predictions that influence many aspects of society. However, their broader adoption in scientific and business applications is often limited by a lack of interpretability. Feature weighting methods, which assess the relevance of individual features, are among the most widely studied approaches for improving interpretability. While post hoc techniques have advanced significantly, especially in modeling nuanced relationships between features and labels in multiclass problems, embedded methods typically fall short in this regard. Embedded techniques integrate feature relevance learning directly into the model training process, but they are often unable to capture label-specific relationships. To address the limitation, we propose multiple extensions to the Feature Selection Layer, an embedded feature weighting mechanism for neural networks. Through extensive experimentation, we identify the most effective extension and benchmark it against established feature weighting methods. Our results show that the proposed method matches existing techniques in identifying globally relevant features and outperforms them in capturing label-specific relevance. By leveraging the internal dynamics of the trained neural network, it reveals how individual features contribute to the prediction of specific labels, requiring no post-processing beyond the training process.

papers.title: Scalable Levenberg-Marquardt Training Framework for Deep Learning
papers.summary: The Levenberg-Marquardt (LMA) algorithm is a widely used nonlinear least-squares solver known for its rapid convergence. For small-scale neural networks, LMA provides better convergence and architectural robustness than first-order optimizers like Adam. However, LMA imposes prohibitive memory and computational costs. These costs are primarily from the Jacobian matrix, whose dimensions scale with both the number of samples and parameters. This bottleneck prevents its use in large-scale neural networks. Recent efforts scale LMA using preconditioned conjugate gradient (PCG) solvers to avoid materializing the Jacobian. However, PCG only approximates the solution, requiring many network propagations and a task-specific preconditioner. Other studies optimize LMA to reduce costs, but they restrict their methods to specific tasks or network architectures. As a result, LMA remains impractical for training general large-scale neural networks. In this paper, we propose LeMA, a distributed LMA algorithm for large-scale neural network training on multi-GPU platforms. Our contributions are twofold: First, an exact dual formulation of LMA removes the memory dependence on the parameter dimension. Second, a Jacobian sharding strategy computes Jacobian shards on the fly and in parallel to avoid materializing the full Jacobian. For large-scale neural networks, LeMA reduces the memory footprint of LMA from quadratic in the number of parameters to quadratic in the batch size. This makes exact LMA steps feasible for billion-parameter models without approximate PCG solves. Furthermore, for a convolutional neural network with 1,000,022,632 parameters on an 8-GPU node, LeMA achieves a 7.97x speedup over a single GPU, corresponding to a 99.7% strong scaling efficiency.

papers.title: Large Diffusion Models Need More Than EMA
papers.summary: Large-scale diffusion models are commonly trained with a constant learning rate (LR) and exponential moving average (EMA), despite the strong performance of LR decay and Schedule-Free optimization in training large language models. We study whether EMA is uniquely suited to diffusion training, or whether stronger alternatives have been underexplored. Our theory shows that averaging a constant-step trajectory has an inherent optimization limitation, whereas LR decay and Schedule-Free optimization admit vanishing stationarity guarantees under standard nonconvex assumptions. Empirically, LR decay and EMA provide complementary benefits: combining decay with EMA further improves the standard baseline at most tested starting points, although the gain remains sensitive to when decay begins. Schedule-Free avoids this timing requirement and consistently outperforms EMA with a constant LR across training stages, achieving both lower fixed-evaluation objectives and better generation quality. Our analysis further shows that all three strategies substantially reduce parameter variability, yet stronger stabilization is not always better: EMA with a constant LR retains comparatively higher parameter variability, while aggressive decay combined with EMA achieves the lowest checkpoint variability but also weakens continued optimization. Schedule-Free substantially reduces parameter variability while preserving more late-stage progress, providing a better balance between parameter stability and continued optimization. Finally, the benefits of Schedule-Free extend beyond pretraining to ReFL and generator-side DMD, demonstrating its transferability across distinct diffusion optimization settings. Overall, our results suggest that large diffusion models need more than parameter averaging alone: effective optimization requires balancing variance reduction with continued optimization.
papers.title_zh: 大型扩散模型需要的不仅仅是 EMA
papers.abstract_zh: 大规模扩散模型通常使用恒定学习率（LR）和指数移动平均（EMA）进行训练，尽管 LR 衰减和 Schedule-Free 优化在训练大型语言模型时表现出强劲性能。我们研究 EMA 是否特别适合扩散训练，或者更强的替代方案是否尚未得到充分探索。我们的理论表明，对恒定步长轨迹进行平均存在固有的优化局限性，而 LR 衰减和 Schedule-Free 优化在标准非凸假设下可提供趋于零的平稳性保证。在实证上，LR 衰减和 EMA 提供互补的益处：将衰减与 EMA 结合在大多数测试起始点上进一步改进了标准基线，尽管增益仍然对衰减何时开始敏感。Schedule-Free 避免了这一时机要求，并在各训练阶段始终优于使用恒定 LR 的 EMA，既实现了更低的固定评估目标，又获得了更好的生成质量。我们的分析进一步表明，三种策略都大幅降低了参数变异性，但更强的稳定化并不总是更好：使用恒定 LR 的 EMA 保持相对更高的参数变异性，而激进衰减与 EMA 结合则实现了最低的检查点变异性，但也削弱了持续优化。Schedule-Free 大幅降低参数变异性，同时保留更多后期进展，在参数稳定性和持续优化之间提供了更好的平衡。最后，Schedule-Free 的益处超越了预训练，扩展到 ReFL 和生成器侧 DMD，展示了其在不同扩散优化设置中的可迁移性。总体而言，我们的结果表明，大型扩散模型需要的不仅仅是参数平均：有效的优化需要在方差降低与持续优化之间取得平衡。

papers.title: On the tradeoff between robustness and geometric accuracy in adversarial training
papers.summary: For non-parametric binary classification in the presence of an adversary, we prove an optimal quantitative estimate for adversarial classifiers controlling geometric accuracy, as measured by the Hausdorff distance to the Bayes classifier, in terms or their robustness, as encoded by the adversarial budget $\varepsilon$. This rigorously shows that robust classifiers sacrifice at most $O(\sqrt{\varepsilon})$ or $O(\varepsilon)$ in accuracy, depending on the regularity of the underlying Bayes classifier. In contrast to prior work on the incompatibility of robustness and accuracy over low-complexity hypothesis classes, our work shows that high-complexity hypothesis classes allow for robust classifiers with precisely quantified accuracy. Our results apply for adversaries determined by any norm on Euclidean space and in both the infinite and finite data settings.

papers.title: Towards Hyperparameter Transfer for Differentially Private Optimization
papers.summary: Scaling laws and hyperparameter tuning remain central challenges in training large-scale models, particularly under differential privacy (DP), where optimization is further complicated by noise injection and per-sample gradient clipping. While Maximal Update Parametrization ($μ$P) allows for zero-shot hyperparameter transfer in standard training, we show that it fails under DP constraints due to the distinct spectral properties of high-dimensional noise versus low-rank gradients. In this work, we introduce DP-$μ$P, a theoretically grounded framework that extends $μ$P to the privacy-preserving setting. By analyzing the interaction between gradient clipping, noise injection, and feature learning, we derive a Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) condition that governs layer-wise learning rate scaling. Combining this with our proposed spectral scaling formulation, we provide specific scaling rules for DP-SGD, DP-Adam, and DP-Muon optimizers. Empirically, we demonstrate that DP-$μ$P enables effective zero-shot transfer of learning rates across model widths on diverse architectures (MLP, ViT, GPT-2), matching or exceeding the performance of individually tuned baselines while significantly reducing computational costs.

papers.title: TALLOP: Joint Optimization of Local Training and Communication Compression for Time-Constrained Federated Learning
papers.summary: Minimizing the wall-clock time required to reach a target accuracy is crucial in federated learning (FL), where many applications require frequent model updates as data distributions evolve over time. Nevertheless, in heterogeneous environments, slow clients with limited computational and communication capabilities can delay global synchronization, forcing faster clients to wait and increasing the overall training time. To mitigate this straggler effect, recent studies have introduced per-round time constraints and adapted client workloads within the available time. However, these approaches primarily focus on local computation, whereas communication can become a major bottleneck in communication-limited environments, motivating the joint optimization of training workload and communication compression. Although previous studies have explored such joint optimization, determining an effective training--communication balance under a fixed per-round time budget remains challenging, as the resulting model performance depends on both training progress and compression-induced degradation. We therefore propose TALLOP, which jointly optimizes the local training workload and communication compression under per-round time constraints. TALLOP predicts the training loss achievable under different computation budgets from the early-stage mini-batch loss trajectory (LENS), and estimates the degradation caused by communication compression using a compression-error model (CLEN). TALLOP combines these predictions to select the training-communication allocation that minimizes the post-compression loss under the given round time constraint. Experiments in heterogeneous FL environments show that TALLOP generally achieves competitive or improved time-to-accuracy compared with approaches that optimize only local training or neither, although the benefit over training-only adaptation depends on the setting.

papers.title: A Label Noise Robust Algorithm for Graph Data using Neighborhood Label Distribution
papers.summary: Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) have demonstrated exceptional performance on graph-structured data. However, their success heavily relies on the availability of clean labels, an assumption that often fails in real-world scenarios. The learnability of GCNs is intrinsically linked to the neighborhood structure of nodes, making it critical to understand how this structure changes in the presence of label noise. In this work, we investigate how the neighborhood label distribution of a node changes under label noise. We mathematically derive that label noise smooths this distribution, which inherently increases its entropy and severely decreases interclass distinguishability. To address this challenge, we propose Leave-one-out Entropy Node Screening (LENS), an end-to-end framework that identifies noisy nodes by measuring the reduction in neighborhood entropy when a specific node is removed. LENS further incorporates a relabeling mechanism to recover and preserve valuable feature information instead of entirely discarding the identified noisy nodes. Crucially, the end-to-end computational overhead of LENS is remarkably low. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that our algorithm achieves state-of-the-art node classification accuracy while executing an order of magnitude faster than existing noise-robust approaches.

papers.title: A Minimal ReLU Classifier on Non-Linearly Separable Data: Convergence and Implicit Bias at and beyond the Edge of Stability
papers.summary: Gradient descent (GD) with large learning rates can successfully optimize neural networks even though classical smoothness-based learning rate conditions are violated. Yet theory for this regime largely covers linear models or linearly separable data. We analyze a minimal setting outside both regimes. Specifically, a two-neuron ReLU network trained with logistic loss on 1D non-linearly separable data. The objective is nonconvex and nonsmooth, and GD exhibits edge-of-stability (EoS) behavior. We identify an active cone in parameter space that contains every perfect classifier, where the problem becomes piecewise logistic regression with a varying effective dataset. Within this cone, we prove a finite-time loss bound for constant learning rates and show that GD converges in direction to an explicit max-margin vector, while the orthogonal component converges to the unique minimizer of a non-strongly convex potential. We further establish catapult results where exponentially small loss is reached after a single loss spike. Furthermore, we propose an adaptive schedule that lets learning rates grow to infinity without leaving the active cone. We prove that this schedule achieves a loss rate of $O(1/(T\log{T})$, which is faster than the standard $O(1/T)$ rate. Our theoretical results extend to local convergence on more general network and are validated on MNIST dataset. Overall, we show that this setup provides a tractable neural-network model for studying large and adaptive step sizes beyond linear predictors and separable data.

papers.title: "Deep lifts": Neural networks can generalize even with the dumbest optimizer
papers.summary: Given a labeled dataset $\{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i = 1}^n$, consider drawing a parameter vector $\hatθ$ uniformly at random from those that interpolate the data within a width-$W$ depth-$D$ ReLU architecture with continuous weights bounded within $[-M, M]$. We study the generalization properties of $\hatθ$ in the case where the dataset can, in fact, be explained by a smaller $w$-by-$d$ ReLU network. Despite the obliviousness of the selection rule for $\hatθ$, it adaptively generalizes at the rate $\tilde O\left(\frac{wdWD}{n}\right)$, rather than being governed by the VC dimension of the full $W$-by-$D$ hypothesis class. The reason is due to a particular inductive bias in ReLU networks: the $w$-by-$d$ parameter *witnesses* an exponential volume of $W$-by-$D$ interpolating parameters, which dwarfs the volume of poorly generalizing parameters (conditioned on interpolation). We explicitly construct this set of near-equivalent $W$-by-$D$ parameters by a proof technique called *deep lifting*, and then tie the achievable volume to stability properties of the $w$-by-$d$ witness. Examples show that these techniques allow us to convert approximation-theoretic results into generalization guarantees for nonparametric classes. We further show that generalization of uniform-random interpolators can survive label corruptions.

papers.title: Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part I: Topology, Input Injection, Recurrent-State Design
papers.summary: Looped language models reuse physical Transformer blocks across logical depth, but established architectures entangle recurrence placement, input injection, and recurrent state organization. We isolate these axes in models trained from scratch at matched parameter scale, logical depth, and token budgets, and then test whether the resulting design principles transfer to resident- and active-parameter-matched Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models. The prelude-recurrent block-coda sandwich architecture consistently improves performance on context extraction and reasoning-intensive tasks. Input injection primarily enhances knowledge retrieval and context utilization, whereas random initialization and separate H/L recurrent states provide mixed or negative returns. Taken together, these results favor the Huginn-style design: at the 730M-parameter and 336B-token scale, the complete Huginn architecture outperforms Ouro across all ten benchmarks. The advantages of Huginn over Ouro transfer to MoE models. At the 8BA0.8B (32BA3B when unrolled) scale trained on 500B tokens, Huginn outperforms Ouro on nearly all benchmarks spanning knowledge, reasoning, and coding, while also exhibiting more balanced expert routing. Under matched training and inference FLOPs, the Huginn-style model uses 75% fewer resident parameters than a 112-layer feedforward MoE baseline. Despite its smaller physical parameters, it outperforms the feedforward baseline on DROP and GSM8K, matches it on MATH500, and remains competitive on the other benchmarks.

papers.title: GR-OPD: Group-Relative Sequence Credit for On-Policy Distillation
papers.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) provides token-level teacher feedback, yet common sampled-token updates assign credit locally and omit the effects of earlier actions on subsequent feedback. We introduce \method{} (Group-Relative On-Policy Distillation), which decouples feedback computation from credit assignment by aggregating token feedback into calibrated sequence-level credit. We establish a theoretical basis for this approach by showing that, under ideal on-policy assumptions, broadcasting raw summed feedback to every response token yields an unbiased estimate of the negative gradient of the sequence-level reverse-KL objective. To support effective learning in practice, \method{} discounts later feedback that may become less reliable under distribution shift and uses same-prompt rollout groups to calibrate teacher guidance. It preserves relative response preferences while retaining a controlled fraction of the group mean, which we term collective teacher pressure. Across five Qwen3 teacher--student settings and six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, \method{} outperforms vanilla OPD in macro Avg@K in every setting, including gains of 10.9 and 11.5 percentage points in two settings with matched thinking patterns. It also maintains stable training under mismatched thinking patterns, where vanilla OPD collapses. Ablations show that retaining an appropriate amount of collective teacher pressure can improve learning, while excessive collective teacher pressure or an unrestricted feedback horizon can destabilize training.

papers.title: Path to Prior-Data Fitted Relational Models via Learned Latent Multi-table Representations
papers.summary: Prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) show that pretraining on large populations of synthetic tasks can enable generalization to unseen datasets with little or no downstream fine-tuning. This paradigm is effective for transformer-based tabular and relational foundation models such as RDB-PFN, but remains largely unexplored for graph-based relational models built on message passing. We pretrain the graph-based relational foundation model Griffin on large collections of synthetic relational databases and ask whether curriculum learning, which benefits transformer-based relational learners, also improves message-passing representations. Rather than fine-tune on downstream tasks, we use the pretrained encoder as a general-purpose relational representation learner and pass its latent representations to a frozen in-context predictor (\ticl{}); no component is trained on the target task. On 16 real-world relational classification tasks, evaluated over five seeds against raw-feature and untrained-encoder baselines, a purely synthetic curriculum that begins with schema-guided data and continues with schema-agnostic data gives the strongest frozen in-context performance\rev{, outperforming real-data-only pretraining and every unordered single-stage mixture of the corpora; when appended after real-data pretraining, it yields the best encoders overall}. These results provide initial evidence that PFN-style synthetic pretraining transfers to graph-based relational foundation models.

papers.title: Where Latents Belong and How They Flow: Joint Identification of Structural Roles
papers.summary: Latent factors in dynamical systems can play different roles across observations and time. For example, an idea in a group meeting may be expressed by only some participants, inherit information from earlier discussions, and shape what is said next. We formalize this notion as the structural role of a latent factor, describing where it is expressed, whether it receives influence from the past, and whether it transmits influence to the future. The main challenge is correspondence, since the three structures may be identified under different permutations, while a structural role is defined only when they are aligned to the same latent coordinate. We show that, under suitable structural and variability conditions, all three roles are jointly identifiable under a common permutation at each time point. Guided by this theory, we develop RoleTrace, a framework that traces structural roles in a shared latent coordinate system. Synthetic experiments validate structural recovery, while experiments on multiparty meetings examine the identified roles in real sequential interactions.

papers.title: Towards a GraphNARX model for structural dynamics
papers.summary: The current paper introduces the GraphNARX model, a graph-based nonlinear autoregressive exogenous model for structural dynamics. The model is built to account for the geometry of structures and to model dynamic behaviour as the interaction between elements of the structure. Similar to other types of NARX models, GraphNARX is used for system identification. Nodal attributes of the graph encode past displacements and nodal forces, and the output of the model is the next-timestep displacement. The graph formulation of the model allows it to generalise to structures of different dimensions and degrees of freedom. Moreover, because graph-learning is performed locally between the nodes, the GraphNARX model can also learn to infer displacements of nodes for which data are not available, i.e.\ to perform virtual sensing. The proposed model's performance is evaluated in a system-identification framework and a virtual-sensing framework, and achieves good accuracy and exhibits generalisation capabilities to structures of different sizes.

papers.title: Domain-specific language alignment of multimodal embeddings towards explainable predictions
papers.summary: Multimodal data are commonly fused into latent representations that improve downstream task performance but are not interpretable, limiting their application in domains that require explainable model decisions. Vision-language alignment has made image embeddings interpretable through language, but requires vast image-caption training data. However, captioned data are typically not available for multimodal embeddings, as relevant features cannot directly be observed and annotated from embeddings alone. Here, we propose a framework to language-align any embedding space that can be linked to interpretable auxiliary data. Captioning functions convert auxiliary data into partial captions; a soft contrastive loss weights pairs by the similarity of their properties that each caption describes; and a rank-based concept retrieval task evaluates alignment against the auxiliary data rather than the captions. We apply this framework to multimodal Earth embeddings to facilitate explainable predictions for two species distribution modelling tasks: S2BMS and SatBird. AlphaEarth embeddings beat previous state-of-the-art models on 6/7 metrics, while our framework language-aligns domain-specific concepts of the embedding space, outperforming previous Earth observation vision-language models on average concept retrieval for both datasets. Finally, aligned concepts recover species-habitat associations ($ρ$=0.44) and relate habitat descriptions to species predictions, showing that abstract embeddings can be interrogated in the language of domain experts.

papers.title: LED: Improving Masked Diffusion Language Models by Lookahead Editing
papers.summary: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) have emerged as a promising alternative to autoregressive language models, enabling non-autoregressive text generation through parallel decoding. Existing dLLMs can be broadly categorized into two families: masked diffusion models (MDMs) and uniform diffusion models (UDMs) In this work, we theoretically show that MDMs are easier to optimize due to their mask-based transition schedule but have lower computational expressivity, whereas UDMs enable iterative state revision and greater expressivity but are substantially harder to train. This trade-off raises a natural question: can we obtain the expressivity of iterative revision without giving up the simple, easy-to-optimize transition schedule of MDMs? Motivated by this analysis, we propose Lookahead Editing (\ours{}), which augments masked diffusion decoding with a rewritable proposal state. At each decoding step, the model performs several lookahead updates to iteratively refine future predictions in this proposal state before committing tokens to the masked sequence. This design introduces a rewritable proposal that uses additional compute to improve expressivity while keeping the simple mask-based transition schedule of MDMs. We fine-tune Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen3-8B to obtain LED-\texttt{7B} and LED-\texttt{8B}, respectively. Across eight benchmarks, LED SFT yields average gains of $+11.4$ and $+7.7$ points over standard MDM SFT. Moreover, using SFT alone, LED-\texttt{8B} outperforms LLaDA2.1-16B Q-mode, which is trained with continued pre-training, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning.
papers.title_zh: LED：通过前瞻编辑改进掩码扩散语言模型
papers.abstract_zh: 扩散大语言模型（dLLMs）已成为自回归语言模型的一种有前景的替代方案，通过并行解码实现非自回归文本生成。现有的 dLLMs 大致可分为两类：掩码扩散模型（MDMs）和均匀扩散模型（UDMs）。在本工作中，我们从理论上表明，MDMs 由于其基于掩码的转移调度而更容易优化，但计算表达能力较低；而 UDMs 能够进行迭代状态修正并具有更强的表达能力，但训练难度显著更高。这种权衡引出了一个自然的问题：我们能否在不放弃 MDMs 简单且易于优化的转移调度的同时，获得迭代修正的表达能力？受此分析启发，我们提出前瞻编辑（\ours{}），它通过一个可重写的提议状态来增强掩码扩散解码。在每个解码步骤中，模型在该提议状态中执行若干次前瞻更新，以迭代地细化未来的预测，然后再将词元提交到掩码序列中。该设计引入了一个可重写的提议，它利用额外的计算来提高表达能力，同时保留 MDMs 简单的基于掩码的转移调度。我们对 Qwen2.5-7B 和 Qwen3-8B 进行微调，分别得到 LED-\texttt{7B} 和 LED-\texttt{8B}。在八个基准上，LED SFT 相较于标准 MDM SFT 取得了 $+11.4$ 和 $+7.7$ 个点的平均增益。此外，仅使用 SFT，LED-\texttt{8B} 就优于 LLaDA2.1-16B Q-mode，后者通过持续预训练、监督微调和强化学习进行训练。

papers.title: MetaCurate: Evolving Curation Filters for High-Quality Agentic Coding Data
papers.summary: Supervised fine-tuning on agent trajectories is an effective way to improve coding agents, but selecting useful training examples requires more than identifying successful runs. A resolved patch may follow inefficient reasoning or unnecessary tool use, while a failed run may still contain useful intermediate steps. Training pipelines therefore rely on rules and qualitative assessments to filter trajectories, yet designing these filters typically requires substantial human expertise, and validating improvements through repeated training and evaluation is expensive. We introduce MetaCurate, a training-free framework that evolves executable trajectory curation filters using pairwise LLM judgments. Disagreements between the filter's rankings and the judge's preferences provide targeted feedback for jointly revising its rules, rubric, and aggregation policy. The resulting filter scores trajectories independently, so pairwise comparisons are required only during search. Starting from a blank filter, MetaCurate autonomously discovers a curation strategy that achieves competitive downstream performance without task-specific handwritten criteria. We validate downstream utility through controlled SFT experiments on our uncurated trajectory pool and the Nemotron v3 SWE dataset, with random selection and hand-authored filtering as baselines. In our experiments, MetaCurate achieves the highest mean SWE-Verified score among the compared methods, including hand-authored rule-based filtering and a training-loop baseline whose search costs 3.5x as much.

papers.title: Local proxies for memory-efficient training
papers.summary: Local learning algorithms can reshape resource requirements of artificial intelligence. The memory bottleneck of standard end-to-end backpropagation lies in the need to store all network activations until the loss gradient has been propagated back through. Local learning avoids this, but typically at a cost in accuracy. We study how to achieve accurate and memory efficient local learning in transformers. For each transformer block, we train a local proxy network to predict the global network output via distillation. Gradients can be independently propagated through this local proxy while estimating well the backpropagation gradients. In theory, this approach is exact for deep linear networks; in non-linear residual models, the gradient error can be bounded when using the appropriate residual proxy. We verify this numerically and demonstrate that optimizing the distillation loss improves gradient estimation. Evaluating the performance of proxy propagation on CIFAR-100 in vision transformers, we find that it achieves a better accuracy/memory trade-off compared to other local algorithms. Finally, we show that the method is further relevant for fine-tuning large language models on a small memory budget. Our method trains faster and achieves higher performance than memory-efficient zeroth-order learning algorithms with comparable memory cost.
papers.title_zh: 用于内存高效训练的局部代理
papers.abstract_zh: 局部学习算法可以重塑人工智能的资源需求。标准端到端反向传播的内存瓶颈在于，需要存储所有网络激活，直到损失梯度完成反向传播。局部学习避免了这一点，但通常以精度为代价。我们研究如何在 Transformer 中实现准确且内存高效的局部学习。对于每个 Transformer 块，我们训练一个局部代理网络，通过蒸馏来预测全局网络的输出。梯度可以通过这个局部代理独立传播，同时很好地估计反向传播梯度。在理论上，这种方法对于深度线性网络是精确的；在非线性残差模型中，当使用适当的残差代理时，梯度误差可以被界定。我们通过数值实验验证了这一点，并证明优化蒸馏损失可以改善梯度估计。在视觉 Transformer 中评估代理传播在 CIFAR-100 上的性能时，我们发现与其他局部算法相比，它实现了更好的精度/内存权衡。最后，我们表明该方法进一步适用于在较小内存预算下微调大型语言模型。在可比的内存开销下，我们的方法比内存高效的零阶学习算法训练得更快，并取得了更高的性能。

papers.title: Grounded Credit Assignment in Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Turn Search Agents
papers.summary: Outcome-reward reinforcement learning such as GRPO gives every token of a search-agent rollout the same advantage, although the rollout exercises two capabilities: finding evidence and using it. We show that accuracy improves without grounding: Search-R1 raises accuracy on all seven QA benchmarks, yet on Bamboogle the evidence-supported share of correct answers falls from 84.0% to 42.9%. We attribute this to GRPO's credit assignment: rollouts that retrieve answer-bearing evidence are favoured in aggregate only in proportion to their accuracy gain over the rest, a grounding gap that answering from memory or misusing evidence shrinks or reverses. To address this, we propose Grounded Credit Assignment (GCA), which uses verifiable sub-outcomes (evidence retrieval and answer correctness) to correct search and answer credit separately: a wrong answer is blamed more than the search that found the evidence, and a correct answer that bypasses retrievable evidence is credited less. Never negative on evidence-finding search, the correction does not shrink with the grounding gap; capped at 10% of each token's advantage, it never overrides the outcome signal. Without extra models, rollouts, or training stages, GCA improves average EM over Search-R1 by 5.7 (Qwen2.5-3B) and 6.3 points (Qwen3-30B-A3B) and raises this share from 76.9% to 93.4%.

papers.title: Nearly Linear Private Learning of Littlestone Classes
papers.summary: Differentially private learning aims to learn from data while protecting individual training examples. For binary classification, finite Littlestone dimension characterizes approximate private PAC learnability (Alon et al., JACM 2022). Understanding how this dimension controls private sample complexity remains a central question. For classes of Littlestone dimension $d$, the first general upper bound was doubly exponential in $d$ (Bun, Livni, and Moran, FOCS 2020). Subsequent work improved this to $\widetilde O(d^6)$ (Ghazi et al., STOC 2021) and then to $\widetilde O(d^5)$ (Lyu, STOC 2026). We prove a nearly linear upper bound of $O(d\log d)$. Our main algorithmic contribution is a structural exponential mechanism for data-dependent candidate sets equipped with a rank satisfying suitable stability conditions. For natural Littlestone classes such as subspace indicators, this rank has a simple geometric interpretation: it is the codimension. This yields a private PAC learner for subspaces of dimension at most $d$ over any field, with tight linear dependence on $d$ and no dependence on the ambient dimension, improving the quadratic dependence of Kaplan et al. (STOC 2025). Our second contribution is combinatorial: drawing on model-theoretic ideas, we construct a suitable rank for general Littlestone classes and establish the counting bounds required by the mechanism.

papers.title: Structural Affinity: An Algorithm for Coherent Cage-Based Shape Design
papers.summary: Cage-based deformation (CBD) parametrises 3D geometry through a small set of control handles, effectively enabling a variety of tasks from animation and interactive modelling to tool-based co-design, neural deformation transfer, and aerodynamic shape optimization. Many optimization approaches relying on CBD employ regularisation strategies to reduce the distortion of the deformed mesh by encouraging smooth, regular cage deformations. These techniques offer soft guidance to an optimization algorithm towards desirable deformations, but compete with the task objective rather than changing the deformation parameterization itself. In this work we introduce Structural Affinity for CBD, an explicit regularisation method which enables smooth deformations through control cages by exploiting a two-cage structure to couple cage-handle motion directly. Structural Affinity precomputes an affinity matrix using mean-value coordinates, binding the inner control-cage to a coarser outer-cage. This matrix defines how much a cage handle displacement propagates to neighbouring handles which substantially decreases and often eliminates cage self-intersections, reduces mesh distortion, and adds linear overhead at deformation time. Across robotic control--morphology co-design, source-to-target neural deformation transfer, and aerodynamic wing shape optimization, Structural Affinity produces more regular deformations and substantially reduces reliance on hand-designed structural loss terms. We report consistent gains on three complementary diagnostics: the cotangent Laplacian, a proxy for surface smoothness; cage distortion, capturing whether control handles move coherently; and surface roughness, which measures undesirable oscillation in wing geometry.

papers.title: Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards has become a scalable post-training paradigm for large language models. However, training agents over long-horizon interactions presents two challenges: using only terminal rewards makes turn-level credit assignment sparse and high-variance, while sequential mini-batch updates on a fixed rollout batch introduce policy staleness as the current policy drifts from the behavior policy. Existing approaches obtain denser credit via learned critics, process reward models, or on-policy distillation, but they rely on a value network, step-level annotations, or a stronger external teacher that increase training complexity. Meanwhile, importance sampling and clipping mitigate policy drift, but they do not specify a finite target that stops sequential updates from overshooting. In this work, we introduce TreeOPSD, a critic-free, tree-aware posterior self-distillation framework for long-horizon agentic reinforcement learning. Treating each interaction turn as a tree node, TreeOPSD branches alternative continuations from shared prefixes and recursively backs up terminal rewards into implicit turn-level credit. It then maps each credit to a closed-form, bounded teacher distribution parameterized by the likelihood ratio relative to the frozen behavior policy. Minimizing the divergence between this teacher and the student policy recovers the policy-gradient direction as the tangent at the behavior policy while bounding updates toward a finite target across sequential mini-batches. Empirically, TreeOPSD improves agentic capabilities across several competitive benchmarks and model scales, especially for long-horizon tasks, e.g., raising the average accuracy of Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 by 4.97 points over GRPO on the Deep Research setting.
papers.title_zh: 用于长时程智能体强化学习的树感知后验蒸馏
papers.abstract_zh: 具有可验证奖励的强化学习已成为大语言模型的一种可扩展后训练范式。然而，在长时程交互中训练智能体面临两个挑战：仅使用终端奖励会使轮级信用分配变得稀疏且高方差，而在固定 rollout 批次上进行顺序小批量更新会引入策略陈旧性，因为当前策略会偏离行为策略。现有方法通过学习到的评论家、过程奖励模型或同策略蒸馏来获得更稠密的信用，但它们依赖于价值网络、步级标注或更强的外部教师，从而增加了训练复杂度。与此同时，重要性采样和裁剪可以缓解策略漂移，但它们并未指定一个有限目标来阻止顺序更新发生过冲。在本工作中，我们提出 TreeOPSD，一个用于长时程智能体强化学习的无评论家、树感知后验自蒸馏框架。TreeOPSD 将每个交互轮次视为一个树节点，从共享前缀分支出替代续写，并将终端奖励递归回传为隐式的轮级信用。然后，它将每个信用映射为一个闭式、有界的教师分布，该分布由相对于冻结行为策略的似然比参数化。最小化该教师分布与学生策略之间的散度，会在行为策略处作为切线恢复策略梯度方向，同时在顺序小批量上将更新约束到一个有限目标。在实证上，TreeOPSD 在多个具有竞争力的基准和模型规模上提升了智能体能力，尤其是对于长时程任务，例如，在 Deep Research 设置下，将 Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 的平均准确率较 GRPO 提高了 4.97 个百分点。

papers.title: A Stronger Teacher Within: Strengthening MoE Models via On-Policy Bidirectional Distillation
papers.summary: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has substantially improved Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs, but its outcome-level rewards provide only sparse supervision. On-Policy Distillation offers dense token-level feedback, yet requires a stronger compatible teacher, while on-policy self-distillation relies on hand-designed privileged information. We observe that the MoE architecture itself offers a way to resolve this dilemma, as increasing the activation budget per token exposes latent expert capacity and yields a potentially stronger teacher within the model. However, naive expansion degrades performance because newly co-activated experts are not optimized to work together. We therefore propose MoEvolve, a bidirectional distillation framework following a recovery-then-improvement strategy: we first restore the activation-expanded high-$k$ model and further strengthen it by exploiting its additional active capacity, then reverse the direction of distillation to transfer the enhanced capabilities back into the original low-$k$ configuration, retaining its inference-time activation budget. Across diverse MoE models and benchmarks, MoEvolve improves the initial models by up to $22.2$ domain-average points and outperforms same-budget RLVR baselines by up to $6.5$ points. Notably, the final low-$k$ models often surpass their activation-expanded teachers.

papers.title: LangNCO: Compiling Natural-Language Constraints into Inference-Time Interventions for Neural Combinatorial Optimization
papers.summary: Neural combinatorial optimization (NCO) rapidly produces high-quality solutions for problem structures encountered during training, but operational requirements may change after deployment and be communicated in natural language. We propose LangNCO, a framework that compiles instance-specific requirements into structured inference-time interventions for a frozen NCO solver, without changing the pretrained policy's architecture, learned input representation, or parameters. A pretrained LLM serves as a replaceable semantic front end, translating each requirement into a schema-validated domain-specific language (DSL) rule set. A deterministic Rule Executor applies the rules as nonexpansive hard action masks. Because local masking prevents immediate violations but does not ensure that a complete feasible continuation remains reachable, Critical-Offset Decoding extracts rule-referenced critical nodes and reallocates part of a fixed rollout budget to multi-strength biased rollouts. Using controlled task-specific language to isolate solver adaptation from open-ended language robustness, we evaluate a CVRP policy on road closures, time windows, vehicle assignments, visit-order requirements, all pairwise combinations, and twelve additional constraint types. LangNCO achieves 100% feasibility on the four primary datasets with mean reference gaps of 1.63--3.26%, 97.33--100% feasibility when separately generated rules are composed for pairwise constraints, and 98.67% feasibility across the additional constraints. These results demonstrate modular post-training adaptation of a frozen NCO solver through inspectable language-derived rules, without retraining.

papers.title: Non-Parametric Optimization for Scalable Learning in Stochastic Decision Problems
papers.summary: Stochastic optimization (SO) plays a central role in decision-making under uncertainty. Among SO problems, time-varying stochastic optimization (TV-SO) is particularly important due to its applications in adaptive control and machine learning. Non-parametric approaches have been proposed for time-varying deterministic optimization; however, they have not been developed for their stochastic counterparts. This work addresses that gap by developing a stochastic variational framework based on Malliavin calculus. This framework yields non-parametric optimality conditions for SO problems with stochastic decisions and supports the design of a scalable deep-learning algorithm that is insensitive to the parameterization dimension. This algorithm, called the Stochastic Path Follower (SPF), is applied to two important problems under distribution drift, namely least-squares recovery and logistic regression. Experimental results show that the proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art learning-based and gradient-based methods in both performance and scalability.

papers.title: Process Reward Modeling with Reliability- and Conservatism-Aware Bayesian Belief
papers.summary: Process Reward Models (PRMs) play a central role in test-time scaling for large language model (LLM) reasoning. However, PRMs may provide inaccurate process rewards for test-time scaling, which we identify as arising from two sources of uncertainty: (1) \textit{PRM uncertainty} that arises from insufficient supervision data and imperfect PRM training; and (2) \textit{policy uncertainty} that results from the mismatch between the policy to collect supervision data and the policy for test-time scaling, leading to systematic reward overestimation. Previous studies fail to jointly consider both uncertainties. To bridge this gap, we propose BayesianPRM, which treats the process reward as a random variable within a reward hypothesis space and maintains a Bayesian belief over it. Since exact Bayesian inference over the continuous hypothesis space is generally intractable, we discretize the reward hypothesis space with a reward ensemble and introduce two complementary belief updates, each targeting one source of uncertainty: (1) to address PRM uncertainty, we introduce \textit{reliability-aware belief updating} that measures how well each ensemble member explains the supervision data and updates the belief with an amortized belief network optimized by the evidence lower bound (ELBO); and (2) to tackle policy uncertainty, we propose \textit{conservatism-aware belief calibration} which further reweights the belief toward lower rewards to suppress overestimation. These two updates yield a reliability- and conservatism-aware Bayesian belief, whose expectation determines the process reward. Experiments on multimodal reasoning benchmarks indicate that BayesianPRM consistently yields more accurate process reward estimates while enhancing test-time scaling performance.
papers.title_zh: 基于可靠性与保守性感知贝叶斯信念的过程奖励建模
papers.abstract_zh: 过程奖励模型（PRMs）在大语言模型（LLM）推理的测试时扩展中发挥着核心作用。然而，PRMs 可能为测试时扩展提供不准确的过程奖励，我们指出这源于两类不确定性：（1）\textit{PRM 不确定性}，其源于监督数据不足和 PRM 训练不完美；（2）\textit{策略不确定性}，其源于收集监督数据的策略与用于测试时扩展的策略之间的不匹配，从而导致系统性的奖励高估。先前的研究未能同时考虑这两种不确定性。为弥补这一空白，我们提出 BayesianPRM，它将过程奖励视为奖励假设空间内的随机变量，并在其上维护一个贝叶斯信念。由于在连续假设空间上进行精确贝叶斯推断通常是难以处理的，我们使用奖励集成对奖励假设空间进行离散化，并引入两种互补的信念更新，每种更新分别针对一种不确定性来源：（1）为处理 PRM 不确定性，我们引入\textit{可靠性感知信念更新}，它衡量每个集成成员对监督数据的解释程度，并使用由证据下界（ELBO）优化的摊销信念网络来更新信念；（2）为应对策略不确定性，我们提出\textit{保守性感知信念校准}，它进一步将信念重新加权到较低奖励，以抑制高估。这两种更新产生一个可靠性与保守性感知的贝叶斯信念，其期望决定过程奖励。在多模态推理基准上的实验表明，BayesianPRM 在持续产生更准确的过程奖励估计的同时，提升了测试时扩展性能。

papers.title: Response-Informed Value Estimation for Cost-Aware Multi-Turn LLM Routing
papers.summary: Multi-turn LLM routing selects a model at every turn before its response is available, yet task success is revealed only when the interaction ends, leaving each intermediate choice without a label of its own. Logged trajectories, however, retain the response each call produced, which exposes what each turn required and how well the chosen model served it, evidence that outcomes alone hide. We introduce RIVET (Response-Informed Value Estimation for Turn-Level Routing), which exploits this post-call evidence during training while keeping routing strictly pre-call at deployment. RIVET jointly trains two value estimators over a shared state-model representation: a deployable Routing Value Estimator that scores candidate models from pre-call information, and a training-only Response-Informed Value Estimator that additionally observes the realized response. Conditioning on the response turns response-induced return variation from residual noise into an observed covariate, and we show that this reduces the leading asymptotic estimation error of the shared representation. On the MINT benchmark, RIVET solves more held-out tasks than the strongest multi-turn baseline while using 74.7% less total call cost.

papers.title: Anisotropic Representation Dynamics in Transformers
papers.summary: Small differences between internal representations can shrink or grow as they pass through a Transformer layer, affecting how information is preserved and how sensitive the model is to perturbations. Yet it remains unclear when changes in attention weights can turn a representation difference that would otherwise shrink into one that grows. We develop a \textbf{Mixture-Gated Theory of Anisotropic Representation Dynamics} that separates self-attention into value transport, query gating, and key gating. Our analysis reveals how the geometry of attended representations constrains gating and how interactions between these mechanisms can reverse contraction induced by value transport. We formalize this phenomenon as gating-induced regime switching, where a representation difference contracts under fixed attention routing but expands under full attention. We derive a necessary and sufficient spectral criterion that certifies the existence or absence of switching and identifies switching directions without exhaustive search. Beyond existence, our theory characterizes maximum relative switching strength, certifies the severity of contraction that gating can overcome, and determines the largest dimension of a subspace in which every nonzero direction switches. Experiments across four Transformer architectures validate these predictions through analytical and finite-forward comparisons, revealing distinct and joint query--key gating mechanisms and nontrivial switching subspaces. Our results provide a mechanistic and spectral understanding of how attention routing can alter local representation dynamics.

papers.title: FLARE: Physics-Grounded Evaluation of Language-Model Agents for Feeder Restoration with Degraded Observations
papers.summary: Restoring service after distribution-grid faults requires decisions from incomplete and conflicting information while respecting electrical constraints. Addressing this need, we introduce FLARE (Feeder-Level Agent Restoration Evaluation), a physics-grounded benchmark for post-isolation feeder restoration. FLARE con- tains 800 AC-feasible cases across five observation settings and allows agents to gather evidence, evaluate switches, and perform restoration actions under fixed operational limits. We evaluate five instruction-tuned models over 78,750 episodes, including topology, distributed-generation, and loading shifts. Mean normalized regret ranges from 0.082 to 0.148. Although every model has zero median regret, P95 regret ranges from 0.814 to 1.000, revealing an important failure tail. Shadow replay shows that 96.4% of 15,706 guard-rejected actions would have caused a physical violation. FLARE enables reproducible evaluation of language-model based restoration support while emphasizing the need for external safety checks.

papers.title: Sample, Mix, or Verify? Allocating Test-Time Compute under Imperfect Verifiers
papers.summary: A common way to make language models and agents more accurate is to spend more compute at inference time: generate many candidate solutions and submit the one a verifier prefers. Success then requires that some candidate is correct and that the verifier picks it. The first grows predictably with the number of samples; the second does not, because real verifiers (unit tests, majority votes, LLM judges, reward models) accept wrong answers, reject right ones, and make correlated mistakes. With a fixed budget, a practitioner must decide how many samples to draw, which models to draw them from, and how much to spend on verification, and today these choices are made by rules of thumb. We introduce SPLIT, which makes them from a small labelled pilot. It rests on an exact formula for the probability of submitting a correct answer under accept/reject and top-score selection that accounts for varying task difficulty, blind spots shared across models, and correlated repeated verifier calls. SPLIT fits the formula by empirical Bayes and uses it to plan budgets on unseen tasks. Across seven benchmarks spanning math, science QA, code and software-engineering agents, 26 models, 175 agent systems and six kinds of real verifiers, all from public releases, SPLIT lands within 0.02-0.8 percentage points of the best allocation in hindsight, while every fixed rule we test loses at least 2.5 points in some setting. Regret depends only on how well SPLIT ranks configurations, and it stays near-optimal under compute, price and latency costs and online. The formula also explains when asking more LLM judges lowers precision. As a forecaster far beyond the pilot, SPLIT beats power-law fitting when the verifier caps success, and we report where it loses.

papers.title: ADT: All-Atom Diffusion Tokenizer for 3D Molecular Structures
papers.summary: Discrete structural tokenization provides a promising route to autoregressive 3D molecular generation. Yet, existing tokenizers face a trade-off between compact representation and all-atom reconstruction: atom-level tokens preserve atomic details but produce long sequences, while compact residue-level protein tokens typically omit side-chain geometry. To overcome this limitation, we propose All-atom Diffusion Tokenizer (ADT), which decouples token granularity from reconstruction resolution. ADT uses one structural token per atom for small molecules and one token per protein residue that jointly represents backbone and side-chain geometry. To mitigate geometric distortion introduced by quantization, we leverage the generative capacity of diffusion models to recover fine-grained atomic geometry beyond deterministic decoding from discrete tokens. Extensive experiments across small molecules and proteins demonstrate that ADT achieves strong reconstruction from compact discrete representations while enabling high-quality autoregressive generation of both small molecules and all-atom protein structures. These results establish compact structural tokens as an effective discrete interface for all-atom molecular reconstruction and generation.
papers.title_zh: ADT：面向三维分子结构的全原子扩散分词器
papers.abstract_zh: 离散结构分词为自回归三维分子生成提供了一条富有前景的路径。然而，现有分词器面临着紧凑表示与全原子重建之间的权衡：原子级 token 保留了原子细节，但会产生长序列；而紧凑的残基级蛋白质 token 通常忽略侧链几何结构。为克服这一局限，我们提出了全原子扩散分词器（All-atom Diffusion Tokenizer，ADT），它将 token 粒度与重建分辨率解耦。ADT 对小分子使用每个原子一个结构 token，对蛋白质使用每个残基一个 token，该 token 联合表示主链与侧链几何结构。为缓解量化引入的几何失真，我们利用扩散模型的生成能力，在离散 token 的确定性解码之外恢复细粒度的原子几何结构。在小分子和蛋白质上的大量实验表明，ADT 能够从紧凑的离散表示实现强重建，同时支持小分子和全原子蛋白质结构的高质量自回归生成。这些结果确立了紧凑结构 token 作为全原子分子重建与生成的有效离散接口。

papers.title: Beyond Marginal Influence: Interaction-Aware Memory Selection for LLM Agents
papers.summary: LLM-agent memory selection often uses retrieval rankings based on record relevance or individual influence. Such rankings cannot identify sufficient subsets under redundant or jointly necessary evidence. We study per-decision memory sufficiency: selecting a small subset that preserves full-memory behavior. To separate search error from model error, we introduce JointCoreBench, a benchmark with nine interaction families, six workflow domains, natural-language decisions, and exact sufficient-set oracles, and JointCore, a relevance cost-ordered group-deletion baseline that tests blocks before individual records. On 6,912 exact conditions, cost-ordered JointCore recovers a minimum-cost sufficient set in 100.0% of cases, reduces subset evaluations from 30.00 to 11.13 (62.9%), and achieves 87.8% active-memory savings. Across four 12B-70B model families and 432 tasks per model, its unweighted mean is 10.28 versus 16.00 model queries and 50.6% versus 43.1% minimum-cost recovery relative to cost aware singleton deletion. Both methods preserve full-memory behavior under the deterministic primary interface. Tests with physical deletion, UNKNOWN masks, PENDING sentinels, counterfactual values, and alternative labels identify interface dependent behavior. JointCore is an efficient benchmark baseline; the study does not establish deployment-ready memory compression.

papers.title: DeDiCa: A Scalable Deconfounding Discrete Causal Generative Model
papers.summary: We introduce DeDiCa, a practical framework for efficient causal inference with discrete variables and hidden confounding that revisits classical probabilistic modeling through a tensorized parameterization of causal Bayesian networks, enabling tractable inference. Given a causal graph, DeDiCa is trained once on observational data by maximum likelihood, exactly marginalizing over hidden confounders, and can then estimate any (proxy-)identifiable interventional query. Despite this deliberately simple parameterization, DeDiCa matches state-of-the-art neural causal generative models in ATE estimation, while supporting memory-efficient CPU training and exact interventional inference in milliseconds. Compared with causal foundation models, DeDiCa scales more effectively with additional observational samples and achieves competitive accuracy at substantially lower inference time and memory. DeDiCa provides a tractable, accurate, and scalable approach to causal inference in discrete settings with hidden confounding.

papers.title: Data-Efficient Classifier Pretraining Through Diffusion Models
papers.summary: Machine learning with limited data is susceptible to overfitting, especially with modern deep neural networks. Prior to the introduction of AlexNet, reconstruction-based pretraining with auto-encoder and denoising auto-encoder were found to be beneficial, partially due to the limited size of the training sets at the time. Motivated by these traditional approaches, we propose DiffPT, a simple diffusion modeling approach to pretrain a given classifier backbone for limited domain-specific training data. We experiment on time-series data, standard natural-image benchmarks, and medical imaging datasets, and contrast the diffusion approach to a multitude of modern and traditional un/self-supervised methods. While contrastive pretraining performs better on CIFAR-10 and Tiny ImageNet in low-data regimes, DiffPT is particularly effective on medical imaging and time-series tasks, where it outperforms self-supervised baselines across a range of low-data regimes. Our results suggest that DiffPT is a simple and effective approach for data-efficient classifier pretraining on different modalities.
papers.title_zh: 基于扩散模型的数据高效分类器预训练
papers.abstract_zh: 在数据有限的情况下，机器学习容易过拟合，尤其是使用现代深度神经网络时。在 AlexNet 被提出之前，使用自编码器和去噪自编码器进行基于重构的预训练被发现是有益的，部分原因是当时训练集规模有限。受这些传统方法的启发，我们提出 DiffPT，一种简单的扩散建模方法，用于在有限的领域特定训练数据上预训练给定的分类器骨干网络。我们在时间序列数据、标准自然图像基准和医学影像数据集上进行实验，并将该扩散方法与大量现代和传统的无监督/自监督方法进行对比。尽管对比预训练在低数据情形下的 CIFAR-10 和 Tiny ImageNet 上表现更好，但 DiffPT 在医学影像和时间序列任务上尤其有效，在这些任务中，它在一系列低数据情形下优于自监督基线。我们的结果表明，DiffPT 是一种简单而有效的方法，可用于在不同模态上进行数据高效的分类器预训练。

papers.title: Untrained CNN and coefficient-space regularization for joint reconstruction in photoacoustic tomography
papers.summary: The joint reconstruction of the initial pressure and spatially varying sound speed in photoacoustic tomography from boundary measurements is considered. A regularized data-driven framework is proposed in which the unknown fields are represented in finite-dimensional wavelet spaces and fixed nonlinear features generated by an untrained convolutional neural network (CNN) are used to reconstruct the initial-pressure coefficients through Tikhonov-regularized least squares. A learned coefficient-space prior is subsequently used to infer the squared sound-speed coefficients. Numerical experiments demonstrate accurate reconstruction on held-out data and strong generalization to previously unseen phantom geometries. The frozen reconstruction map also remains stable under measurement noise not represented during training, with only minor changes in reconstruction accuracy for noise levels up to $10\%$. In comparison with the supervised trained-CNN approach considered in this work, the untrained representation yields substantially smaller reconstruction errors while requiring approximately one-sixth of the computational time. These results demonstrate that fixed random convolutional features combined with regularized coefficient-space learning provide an efficient and robust approach to joint reconstruction in photoacoustic tomography.

papers.title: Peak-Memory Schedules You Can Trust: Exact Realization, Certified Optimality, and the Limits of Recomputation for Inference
papers.summary: Real-time inference on small devices needs low activation memory without extra latency, which makes operator order the most valuable memory lever: it is free in time. We show that the usual way of deploying a better order, handing it back to the compiler and regenerating code, is unreliable. In PyTorch Inductor the regenerated program misses its predicted peak in 22 of 54 CPU configurations. It is worse than the stock program in 9 of them and in 19 of 50 on a GPU, and on the GPU it also changes numerical results. We instead profile the generated program, model its memory exactly from its own statements and their read/write effects, and permute those statements. We prove that this realizes the modeled peak whenever allocation does not depend on history. It does so to the byte, with bitwise-identical results, in all our CPU runs. On the GPU we characterize why the caching allocator breaks the condition. To know when to stop, we give forward and reverse "trap" lower bounds, each computable with $O(n^2)$ minimum cuts. They certify the found order optimal for 94% of held-out wrapper graphs and all 16 microcontroller-class models we study, in under a second. So most inference graphs are already scheduled optimally. Branching networks are the exception, where reordering is free and pays, e.g. 10.0% on DeepLabV3. In compiled training we save up to 7.6%. Beyond the certified optimum we study selective recomputation with per-operator caps.
