Under receding-horizon execution, consecutive action chunks predict some of the same future actions. RePlanMem-VLA treats unusually large disagreement between these temporally aligned predictions as evidence of a task-relevant event. We first compare 35 disagreement measures across single-task autoregressive decoder-only and Flow-Matching Transformers trained from scratch, then validate the selected signals on pretrained OpenVLA-OFT and $π_{0.5}$ policies over MIKASA-Robo-VLA tasks. The resulting detectors achieve ROC-AUC of 0.981-0.997. We then use the selected signals in RePlanMem-VLA to trigger updates to a bounded visual memory, with a robot-masked write filter suppressing redundant frames. In the evaluated memory-retention experiments, RePlanMem-VLA preserves task-relevant observations until the later decision point in 100% of episodes. Real-robot replay data further show that event selection and redundancy suppression extend beyond simulation. These results establish plan revision as a policy-internal signal for controlling what a VLA remembers. Website: https://vika787.github.io/RePlanMem/.

papers.title: Embodiment-Classifier Guidance: Transferring Frozen VLAs Across Robot Dynamics without Demonstrations
papers.summary: Flow-based policies such as $π_0$ are trained on a fixed set of embodiments, and transferring them to new ones is an open problem. To adapt a frozen $π_0$ to a new embodiment without additional demonstrations or parameter updates, we train a lightweight embodiment classifier to distinguish successful action chunks on the source body from those on the target body, using a few calibration tasks. On transfer tasks that $π_0$ saw on its source body but the classifier was never trained on, we nudge each denoising step of $π_0$ with the classifier's gradient, which estimates the direction from the distribution of successful actions on the source body toward that on the target body. On the LIBERO simulation benchmark with four modified controllers, embodiment-classifier guidance raises $π_0$'s average success on the target bodies from 72% to 80% across 12 suite-controller pairs, with a 31% relative reduction in failures (11 of 12 gain; 5 significant after Holm correction). In simulation, guidance is data-efficient, needing few target-body rollouts per task, which makes it promising for sim-to-real transfer, where rollouts are costly. Guidance is mixed on weak wrists and harmful on a locked wrist, when the classifier lacks data or favors infeasible motions. Collecting more target-body data with guided $π_0$ can fill such gaps: on one weak-wrist arm, guided $π_0$ solved a task on which unguided $π_0$ had zero successes in the original data, and retraining the classifier on the guided successes raised success from 52.5% to 70.7%.

papers.title: Shape-Aware Neural Time Fields for Rigid-Body Motion and Manipulation Planning
papers.summary: Rigid-body motion planning is fundamental to robotic transport and manipulation, where both object position and orientation determine whether a body can move through cluttered environments. This coupling makes planning chal- lenging because translation and rotation can be constrained very differently by surrounding geometry. We propose Shape- Aware Neural Time Fields, a physics-informed neural motion planning framework that learns a reusable travel-time, or cost- to-go, representation for rigid-body motion while explicitly accounting for these distinct geometric restrictions. The learned field captures local motion difficulty in translation and rotation and is paired with a sampling-based planner that balances progress toward the goal with the cost of reaching nearby poses. We evaluate the framework across 2D and 3D rigid- body planning tasks and non-prehensile manipulation through object pushing in diverse environments. Results show substantial improvements in planning success and inference efficiency over physics-informed neural planning baselines, while remaining competitive with classical sampling-based planners at significantly lower planning times. Ablation studies further validate the contributions of both the learned representation and the proposed planning strategy. Finally, closed-loop pushing experiments under execution deviations and external disturbances demonstrate that fast replanning enables reactive and adaptive task execution.

papers.title: Sample-Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Policy Improvement via Flow-Reversed Action Anchors
papers.summary: Generalist robot policies offer strong behavioral priors, but achieving deployment-level reliability and throughput remains difficult. Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve these policies, yet its effectiveness is constrained by the cost of online interaction. Existing methods adapt frozen flow-matching policies by treating noise space as a continuous action space. We show that this behaviorally unstructured space makes exploration inefficient, often preventing these methods from extracting meaningful learning signals on challenging tasks. We introduce AnchorQ, which enables coarse-to-fine policy improvement through a structured, refinable latent action representation. At each decision step, AnchorQ uses flow reversal to map reference behaviors to state-conditioned latent anchors, samples local particles around those anchors, and applies value-guided sampling to explore promising refinements. Our analysis shows that anchors reduce identification complexity at the cost of support bias; particle refinement trades this bias against action-class complexity; and critic accuracy determines the reliability of KL-regularized, value-guided selection. Across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, AnchorQ outperforms state-of-the-art post-training baselines in sample efficiency, delivering a 37% improvement in real-world success rate and 97% higher simulated task throughput under the same interaction budget. Additional visualizations are available on our website https://anchorq-rl.com/.

papers.title: Unifying Embodied Foundation Models via a Model-to-Policy Formulation
papers.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models and world-action models (WAMs) have emerged as promising approaches to robot learning and control. These models integrate multimodal perception and action generation, but differ in their architectures, output representations, and learning objectives. In this paper, we present a unified, architecture-agnostic probabilistic formulation for embodied foundation models based on stochastic kernels. Our formulation has two key components: (i) we characterize embodied foundation models through conditional output distributions and action-realization kernels, which together induce task-conditioned robot policies; and (ii) we connect pretraining and post-training to policy deployment, accommodating model-specific pretraining objectives and offline or online post-training strategies. We instantiate the formulation for OpenVLA and DreamZero, covering autoregressive action-token prediction and joint video-action generation.

papers.title: NestedVLA: Learning to Consolidate and Generate Skills for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.summary: Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models promise generalist robotic agents, yet consolidating skills learned across heterogeneous tasks and environments remains difficult: training data is fragmented across platforms, joint multi-task training suffers from interference, and model merging tends to introduce parameter conflicts or require architectural changes. We instead advocate a paradigm in which skills are first learned independently and then consolidated post hoc. To this end, we propose NestedVLA, which replaces parameter aggregation with parameter generation: a nested hypernetwork, conditioned on the target task, synthesizes task-adaptive action-expert parameters that compose with a frozen base VLA. Task-specific compressed VLM residuals are retained separately. This formulation enables flexible task-conditioned skill reuse while mitigating interference. Across three RL benchmarks (MetaWorld, ManiSkill, CALVIN), NestedVLA outperforms the strongest model-merging baseline by 41 pp on average, matches per-task fine-tuning within 1 pp on ManiSkill, and substantially closes the gap on CALVIN, pointing toward a storage-efficient route to skill consolidation. Code is available at https://github.com/WanyuGroup/NeurIPS2026-NestedVLA.

papers.title: Beyond Success Rate: Interventional Evaluation of Memory in Vision-Language-Action Systems
papers.summary: When we say that a robot uses memory, does that memory actually play a role? Success-rate ablations alone cannot establish the use of task-relevant facts: they change information and computation together, while aggregate rates can hide offsetting gains and losses. We propose an Interventional Memory Evaluation Protocol (IMEP) for vision-language-action (VLA) systems to address four questions: (1) Does memory provide a net benefit? (2) Under what conditions does memory help? (3) Do changes to memory alter task outcomes? (4) Are these effects specific to task-relevant facts? At the retrieval interface, we compare target-fact substitutions with fact-preserving replacements, minimal numerical perturbations, and exact replicas, while assessing decision correctness separately from motor execution success. We evaluate within-episode, cross-episode, and agentic memory. In cross-episode learned-bank experiments, a one-unit-in-the-last-place (ULP) intervention, including its installation procedure, changes 11.9% of seed-paired outcomes, while changing key facts produces no clear additional effect over fact-preserving replacements. To examine when memory helps, we introduce ChainBench, where correct decisions require historical information unavailable in current observations. The full memory configuration raises task success from 39.1% to 74.3%, matching the oracle-decision condition under shared recorded executions. These results show that correct history can support robot decisions, but establishing whether a memory system realizes this benefit requires fact-specific evidence beyond aggregate success rates.

papers.title: AWAM: Active Trajectory-Conditioned View Imagination for Robust Robot Manipulation
papers.summary: Rapid progress in embodied intelligence has enabled increasingly capable robots to follow language instructions and manipulate diverse objects. However, strong results in structured environments do not automatically transfer to open-world conditions, where clutter, occlusion, and changing viewpoints can obscure the spatial relationships required for action. To address this perceptual gap, a virtual active-perception paradigm is introduced. AWAM, an Active World-Action Model actively plans where to observe and imagines what will be seen along the planned trajectory before acting. Task-related virtual camera motion is predicted and used as a structured query into a geometry-conditioned world model, producing a reusable spatial prior for manipulation, which is later compressed into a fixed memory and fused with live observations through cross-attention for diffusion-based action prediction. AWAM achieves competitive success rates with 75.9% on LIBERO-Occ, 62.4% on LIBERO-Plus, 76.5% on RLBench-OG Occlusion1, and 94.4% in real-robot trials. These results support improved robustness to the evaluated occlusions and distribution shifts, addressing part of the gap between structured manipulation and less controlled environments.
papers.title_zh: AWAM：面向鲁棒机器人操作的主动轨迹条件化视角想象
papers.abstract_zh: 具身智能的快速进展使机器人能力不断增强，能够遵循语言指令并操作多样化的物体。然而，结构化环境中的优异结果并不会自动迁移到开放世界条件，在开放世界中，杂乱、遮挡和不断变化的视角可能会遮蔽动作所需的空间关系。为弥补这一感知差距，本文引入了一种虚拟主动感知范式。AWAM 是一种主动世界-动作模型，它在执行动作之前主动规划在何处进行观察，并想象沿规划轨迹将会看到的内容。任务相关的虚拟相机运动被预测出来，并作为结构化查询输入到几何条件化的世界模型中，产生可复用于操作的空间先验，该先验随后被压缩为固定记忆，并通过交叉注意力与实时观测融合，用于基于扩散的动作预测。AWAM 取得了具有竞争力的成功率：在 LIBERO-Occ 上为 75.9%，在 LIBERO-Plus 上为 62.4%，在 RLBench-OG Occlusion1 上为 76.5%，在真实机器人试验中为 94.4%。这些结果支持了对所评估的遮挡和分布偏移的鲁棒性提升，缩小了结构化操作与较少受控环境之间差距的一部分。

papers.title: Reason-guided Human Reward Modeling for Preference-based Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) policies optimized for task rewards may produce behaviors that are efficient but misaligned with human expectations, safety preferences, or intent. This paper presents a reason-guided preference-based reinforcement learning (PbRL) framework that learns a human reward model from trajectory-level feedback. In addition to preference labels, the framework incorporates reason tags explaining why a behavior is preferred, enabling the learned reward to capture both human choices and their underlying rationale. Compared with preference-only reward learning, the reason-guided formulation provides additional supervision for learning human-aligned rewards and improves the interpretability of the resulting policy. The learned human reward is combined with the environment reward during policy optimization, allowing the agent to improve task performance while producing more interpretable, human- aligned, and preference-sensitive behavior

papers.title: Beyond Action Prediction: Learning Search-Free Planning in Latent Space
papers.summary: Latent world models learn action-conditioned state transitions in a compact representation space, providing a predictive model for visual planning and control. However, planning with these models typically requires costly test-time optimization over action sequences. We propose to replace this online search with a goal-conditioned inverse model that directly predicts actions from current and goal observations. A key challenge is that action prediction alone neither ensures that goal representations encode action-relevant information nor that predicted actions are consistent with the learned latent prediction model. We introduce Hindsight Inverse JEPA Planning (HIJP), a search-free framework that addresses both aspects during training. HIJP relabels future observations along offline trajectories as goals, providing action supervision across multiple temporal horizons. By retaining gradients through the goal representations, this supervision directly shapes the visual representation. HIJP further feeds predicted actions into the latent predictor model and aligns the resulting next-state representations with encoded successor observations, enforcing action-transition consistency. At inference time, the inverse dynamics model and latent predictor models are applied alternately to generate multi-step action sequences without online search. Across four visual control tasks, HIJP achieves 86.8% overall success and a 1.9-16.5x planning speedup over search-based planning.

papers.title: Diverse Reasoning Paths Matter: Symbolic Equivalence Augmentation for Enhancing RL Exploration
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for improving the reasoning capabilities of LLMs. However, the role of supervised fine-tuning (SFT) data in enabling effective downstream RL remains underexplored. In this paper, we investigate a key hypothesis: the diversity of reasoning steps in chain-of-thought (CoT) during SFT is a critical enabler of RLVR performance. To test this hypothesis, we introduce EquivAug, a data augmentation framework that uses symbolic equivalence transformations to generate diverse yet provably correct reasoning paths. By converting CoT solutions into formal symbolic representations, applying equivalence transformations, and reconstructing natural-language explanations, EquivAug produces training data that differs in reasoning steps rather than surface-level lexical variation. Experiments on GSM8K and FOLIO across model scales demonstrate that EquivAug consistently achieves the highest reasoning path diversity after SFT and the strongest accuracy after GRPO. Our results establish that CoT diversity during SFT is positively correlated with downstream RLVR performance.

papers.title: Too Emotional to Be Fake? Intra-Utterance Emotion Shifts Expose Failure Modes in Speech Deepfake Detectors
papers.summary: Expressive speech synthesis can now change emotion within a single utterance, yet its impact on deepfake detection remains unclear. We introduce EmoShift, a benchmark comparing emotion-stable (AA) and emotion-changing (AB) speech to examine these effects while accounting for static emotion identity and acoustic confounds. It comprises 7,240 bona fide utterances from four source datasets and 9,720 synthetic utterances generated using four expressive TTS systems. Across seven detectors, we find that emotion changes can make synthetic speech appear more genuine, increasing spoof miss rates by up to 25.3 percentage points on OMG-Emotion at fixed thresholds. Conversely, emotion-changing bona fide speech increases false-alarm rates by up to 24.4 percentage points on IEMOCAP. Further analyses reveal detector-specific sensitivities to emotion trajectories, not fully explained by static emotion identity or splicing artifacts. These findings underscore the importance of emotion dynamics in deepfake detection.

papers.title: Framing Spatial Hearing within the Free Energy Principle: A Hierarchical Model of Perceptual Learning
papers.summary: Spatial hearing relies on dynamic internal representations to decode spatial information from ever-changing acoustic conditions. A fundamental example is sound localisation, where listeners infer the direction of an invisible sound. Bayesian inference provides a computational account of such a localisation process; however, modelling efforts are largely limited to static listening scenarios. Instead, the free energy principle (FEP) describes perception, learning, and action as joint minimisation of variational free energy (VFE), providing a principled framework to account for dynamic conditions. Here, we take a first step toward applying the FEP to spatial hearing. We characterise how listeners' beliefs evolve across trials, in which they estimated sound direction and received subsequent visual feedback on each trial. Listeners are described by a hierarchical generative model where visual feedback drives gradient descent on VFE, updating beliefs over three independent quantities: lateral and polar localisation precisions and hemifield disambiguation. The model captures individual learning trajectories and reveals components with different dynamics: lateral precision improves, as does hemifield disambiguation, consistent with increased sensitivity of the auditory pathway in decoding vertical direction. Notably, polar precision also increases, most for listeners with the lowest initial precision, suggesting that the observed vertical improvement is driven by both hemifield disambiguation and polar precision. This work establishes spatial hearing as a tractable domain for FEP and motivates future closed-loop experiments with full action-perception cycles.

papers.title: Interpreting SSL Representations for Spoof Detection: a WavLM Study
papers.summary: Self-supervised speech models such as WavLM achieve strong spoofing detection performance, yet which layers encode the most spoof-relevant information and what acoustic properties they capture remain opaque. We present a layer-wise interpretability study of WavLM using the ASVspoof 5 database, combining three complementary analyses: (i) per-layer linear probing with attack-level evaluation across speech synthesis, voice conversion, and adversarial attacks; (ii) a canonical correlation analysis (CCA) linking layer representations to spoofing-relevant acoustic features; (iii) an exhaustive grid search over layer subsets showing that use of five layers outperforms full thirteen-layer pooling. CCA analysis reveals that, while most acoustic features peak in alignment with mid-layers and then decay, voice quality measures jitter, shimmer, and the harmonics-to-noise ratio show the opposite trend, with correlation increasing toward later layers. Embedding visualisations reveal that deeper layers capture a continuous acoustic similarity among attacks rather than discrete categories, suggesting these layers encode fundamental synthesis artifacts rather than attack-specific signatures.

papers.title: Beyond the Benchmark: Conditioning, Domains and Failure Modes of Qwen3-TTS
papers.summary: Qwen3-TTS reports state-of-the-art zero-shot voice cloning, but its technical report leaves open how the model should be conditioned, how it behaves outside read speech, and how it fails. We characterise its two cloning interfaces, in-context learning (ICL) and X-Vector, against Chatterbox, XTTS-v2 and F5-TTS on read, meeting, emotional and air-traffic-control (ATC) speech, using eighteen objective measures, an LLM judge, a spoofing countermeasure and a listening test. Neither interface dominates: ICL clones timbre more closely from correctly transcribed references, X-Vector clones timing, and ICL degrades sharply when a short reference transcript is wrong. Domain explains four times more variance than system choice. Qwen3-TTS leads on intelligibility and pitch register but trails on prosody, and the objective measures rank systems differently from listeners. An off-the-shelf countermeasure flags its clones no more often than genuine recordings, and on ATC radio it fails for every system. Code and audio are released.

papers.title: VocalGrad: Evaluating Acoustic Perception in Audio Language Models
papers.summary: Recent large audio language models (LALMs) have extended their capabilities beyond lexical speech understanding to tasks requiring paralinguistic and non-linguistic audio understanding, such as emotion recognition. However, these models still struggle to reliably utilize acoustic information, particularly when it co-occurs with spoken linguistic content. Existing benchmarks do not clearly distinguish acoustic perception from higher-level reasoning, making it difficult to identify the source of these failures. To address this issue, we introduce VocalGrad, a benchmark designed to evaluate LALMs' ability to perceive low-level acoustic variations. VocalGrad formulates this problem as a simple binary classification of temporal change direction, enabling evaluation largely independent of higher-level reasoning or semantic understanding. Our benchmark results reveal a substantial gap in acoustic perception between human annotators and state-of-the-art LALMs: while human annotators achieve high accuracy, LALMs perform at near-chance levels. We further conduct linear probing to identify structural bottlenecks in these models. Our analysis reveals two distinct failure modes: for some categories, task-relevant information is preserved in internal representations but not utilized by the language model head; for others, the information becomes progressively less linearly decodable across model layers. Overall, our results reveal substantial limitations of LALMs in modeling acoustic variation under controlled settings and expose representation differences not observable from text outputs.

papers.title: Understanding LLM Hallucinations Caused by Soft Errors
papers.summary: While hallucinations in Large Language Models (LLMs) have been extensively studied from a software perspective, limited attention has been paid to hardware-level factors. In this paper, we performed a case study to understand LLM hallucination caused by soft errors on hardware. We introduce LLMEI to inject soft errors into LLMs during inference, based on what we evaluate the impact of soft error across diverse LLM architectures and tasks, including mathematical reasoning and code generation. We summarize the taxonomy of different failure modes based on LLM hallucination behaviors and analyze their distributions under different error rates. Our find- ings underscore the hallucination-specific diagnostics within the reliability of LLM implementation on hardware.
papers.title_zh: 理解由软错误引起的大语言模型幻觉
papers.abstract_zh: 尽管大语言模型（LLM）中的幻觉已从软件角度得到广泛研究，但硬件层面的因素受到的关注有限。本文开展了一项案例研究，以理解由硬件软错误导致的LLM幻觉。我们提出LLMEI，用于在推理过程中向LLM注入软错误，并基于此评估软错误在不同LLM架构和任务（包括数学推理和代码生成）中的影响。我们基于LLM幻觉行为总结了不同故障模式的分类体系，并分析了它们在不同错误率下的分布。我们的发现强调了在LLM硬件实现可靠性中针对幻觉的专门诊断。

papers.title: ForTress: Bringing Assurance and Determinism for LLM-Driven Fortran-to-Python Translation
papers.summary: Modernizing mature scientific software from Fortran to Python can improve accessibility and integration with modern computing tools, but manual rewriting is expensive. Large language models (LLMs) make translation more practical, yet generated code can pass regression tests while violating source-language semantics, and contextual corrections may not persist across subsequent translations. We present ForTress, which solidifies recurring LLM translation decisions into guarded executable rules for deterministic reuse and provides semantic assurance for a non-trivial subset of these rules. Its LLM-assisted auditing process expresses universally quantified preservation obligations over mechanized Fortran and Python semantics in Lean. Human experts review semantic fidelity and correspondence with production rules, and Lean's kernel checks proofs and refutations under explicit assumptions. These audit records expose the conditions either supporting correctness or identifying failure cases. We evaluate ForTress on 17 benchmarks from 15 scientific software spanning diverse domains. The translated programs achieve bitwise-identical with native Fortran on all evaluated tests under the recorded execution and initialization configurations. Against these software, ForTress accumulates 193 executable rules and 188 audit records, of which 121 have checked soundness proofs, including 31 established after counterexample-guided refinement. Cross-software reuse exceeds 90% for 14 of the 15 software. Even with additional assurance and determinism, the LLM usage cost is 44.2% lower than direct LLM translation.
papers.title_zh: ForTress：为 LLM 驱动的 Fortran 到 Python 翻译带来保证与确定性
papers.abstract_zh: 将成熟的科学软件从 Fortran 现代化到 Python 可以提高可访问性以及与现代化计算工具的集成，但人工重写成本高昂。大语言模型（LLM）使翻译更加实用，但生成的代码可能通过回归测试，却违反了源语言的语义，并且上下文修正可能无法在后续翻译中持续保留。我们提出 ForTress，它将反复出现的 LLM 翻译决策固化为带守卫的可执行规则，以实现确定性复用，并为这些规则中一个不可忽视的子集提供语义保证。其 LLM 辅助审计过程在 Lean 中针对机械化的 Fortran 和 Python 语义表达全称量化的保持义务。人类专家审查语义保真度以及与生产规则的对应关系，Lean 的内核在明确假设下检查证明和反驳。这些审计记录揭示了支持正确性或识别失败情形的条件。我们在来自 15 个科学软件的 17 个基准上评估 ForTress，这些软件涵盖多个不同领域。在记录的执行与初始化配置下，翻译后的程序在所有评估测试中与原生 Fortran 达到逐位一致。针对这些软件，ForTress 累积了 193 条可执行规则和 188 条审计记录，其中 121 条具有已检查的可靠性证明，包括 31 条是在反例引导的精化之后建立的。对于 15 个软件中的 14 个，跨软件复用率超过 90%。即使增加了保证与确定性，LLM 使用成本仍比直接 LLM 翻译低 44.2%。

papers.title: SIEVE: A Parameterized GitHub Corpus Builder for Software Engineering Research
papers.summary: Software engineering research increasingly relies on large, richly annotated corpora of real-world code. Still, researchers typically assemble these with ad-hoc scripts or static, pre-built datasets that offer no control over corpus composition. This leaves a gap for a reusable tool that goes below the repository level and builds annotated, function- and class-level code corpora under researcher-specified criteria. We present SIEVE (Software Ingestion & Extraction for Verifiable Evaluation), an open-source, parameterized GitHub corpus builder that, unlike repository-level mining tools, works at code granularity: it locates individual functions, methods, and classes in repositories and extracts them as records, giving direct control over corpus construction based on several criteria, including widely used programming languages (Python, Java, JavaScript, C++), repository quality, and creation date. To support software engineering research and LLM evaluation on real-world code, SIEVE extracts CodeSearchNet- and OpenClassGen-compatible records, each annotated with 22 structural metrics and AST-derived features, and optionally with a CodeBERT-based P(AI-generated) score (F1=0.9478, AUROC=0.9902), alongside the third-party dependencies declared in each repository's package manifest. These annotations enable researchers to conduct structural analyses, investigate code dependencies, assess AI-generated code, and construct customized benchmarks for evaluating LLMs, including under temporal constraints. A manual validation of 400 records in four languages and two granularities shows 100% accuracy in code metrics and import detection, 99.0% in source completeness, and 99.5% in metadata accuracy. SIEVE is publicly available with a live demo at https://mrahman2025-sieve.hf.space.

papers.title: Enjoying the Product but Not Joining the Builders: Investigating Why Students Don't Contribute to OSS
papers.summary: Open-source software (OSS) participation provides students with authentic exposure to collaborative, real-world software development, yet active contributions remain limited. This short paper presents an exploratory study of computing students' perceptions, knowledge, and experiences with OSS at the University of Hawai'i at Manoa. We administered a survey and analyzed 122 responses using both quantitative and qualitative methods. Students reported moderate OSS familiarity and frequent OSS use in coursework and personal projects, yet only 12.3% actively contributed and engagement with OSS communities was limited. Key barriers included skill gaps (72.89% of non-contributors), time constraints (59.81%), and codebase complexity (66.67% of contributors), often alongside imposter syndrome (36.45%). Students indicated that more time, mentorship, beginner-friendly issues, better onboarding/documentation, and curricular incentives (e.g., course credit) would most increase participation, while most reported their courses do not require or incentivize OSS contributions (58.20%). Grounded in a single institutional context, this study provides a nuanced understanding of how curriculum structure, faculty encouragement, and competing academic demands shape OSS participation. These insights inform the design of targeted curricular and institutional interventions aimed at supporting student onboarding and participation in OSS communities.

papers.title: No One-Size-Fits-All: Adaptive Code Editing with Feature-Based Strategy Selection
papers.summary: Large language models have shown strong potential in automating code editing (CE) tasks, yet most existing systems rely on a fixed CE strategy (i.e., one-step, search-replace, and plan-apply) across diverse scenarios. In practice, CE tasks vary widely in code context, edit locality, and semantic complexity, causing no single strategy to perform consistently well. Moreover, systematic studies on the relationship between strategies and CE tasks remain scarce, limiting further optimization of LLM-based code editing strategies. To address this gap, we construct CEBench, comprising 500 real-world CE tasks curated from SWE-bench. Then we compare three representative CE strategies (one-step, search-replace, plan-apply). Our study reveals two key findings: (1) each strategy exhibits distinct advantages for specific CE tasks, with no universal optimality; (2) strategy effectiveness is significantly influenced by four core task features: total lines of code, modification type, modification scope, and task type. Motivated by these findings, we propose Ace, an adaptive code editing framework that dynamically selects optimal CE strategies based on task features. Unlike classifier-based or instruction-prompting approaches, Ace employs a fine-tuned LLM that learns feature-strategy mappings from empirical data to recommend strategies with interpretable rationales. Extensive experiments on our CEBench-verified show that Ace outperforms state-of-the-art baselines: it boosts Pass@1 by 21.7% while reducing token consumption by 27.3% compared to the best baseline (AutoCodeRover). Our strategy selector achieves 72.6% selection accuracy with 69.9% rationale accuracy (Cohen's Kappa = 0.807), providing transparent and trustworthy decision-making for developers.
papers.title_zh: 并非一刀切：基于特征策略选择的自适应代码编辑
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型在自动化代码编辑（CE）任务中已展现出强大潜力，然而大多数现有系统在多样场景中依赖固定的CE策略（即一步式、搜索-替换和计划-应用）。在实践中，CE任务在代码上下文、编辑局部性和语义复杂度方面差异很大，导致没有单一策略能够始终表现良好。此外，关于策略与CE任务之间关系的系统性研究仍然稀缺，这限制了对基于LLM的代码编辑策略的进一步优化。为填补这一空白，我们构建了CEBench，其中包含从SWE-bench整理出的500个真实世界CE任务。然后我们比较了三种代表性的CE策略（一步式、搜索-替换、计划-应用）。我们的研究揭示了两个关键发现：（1）每种策略对特定CE任务表现出独特优势，不存在普遍最优性；（2）策略有效性受到四个核心任务特征的显著影响：代码总行数、修改类型、修改范围和任务类型。受这些发现启发，我们提出了Ace，一个基于任务特征动态选择最优CE策略的自适应代码编辑框架。与基于分类器或指令提示的方法不同，Ace采用一个微调后的LLM，从经验数据中学习特征-策略映射，以可解释的理由推荐策略。在我们CEBench-verified上的大量实验表明，Ace优于最先进的基线：与最佳基线（AutoCodeRover）相比，它将Pass@1提高了21.7%，同时将token消耗降低了27.3%。我们的策略选择器实现了72.6%的选择准确率和69.9%的理由准确率（Cohen's Kappa = 0.807），为开发者提供透明且可信的决策。

papers.title: MergeShuffle: Reconstruct Shared Libraries for Improved Performance and Security
papers.summary: Debloating shared libraries has been an active research topic for years. Tools for shared library debloating rely on either static or dynamic analysis techniques to discover which parts of the shared library is used. Once these parts are found, these tools take one of two routes, either removing parts of the library that are not used, requiring reconstruction of the library; or they simply overwriting the unused functions. However, recently a broad study~\cite{brown2024broad} on debloating tools has shown that some of these tools either increase the static binary size, or are generally less effective for complex workloads. In this paper, we argue that shared-library debloaters' performance can be improved by proper reconstruction of the shared-libraries once the used functions in the library are identifies. We propose \myapp, a novel tool for reconstructing shared libraries from a given set of file ranges to eliminate unused code based on user-specified requirements, without requiring access to source code. \myapp takes as input a shared library and a set of file ranges to retain, and performs a two-phase reconstruction: merging nearby ranges to reduce loading overhead, and shuffling them to minimize file size while preserving page-aligned memory mappings. The shuffling problem is formulated as a variant of the Traveling Salesman Problem and solved using a heuristic algorithm. \myapp utilizes program headers to remap retained code to its original memory addresses, preserving user-specified functionality. Our results show that \myapp achieves up to 60\% reduction in file size, 16\% reduction in memory usage, and 32\% reduction in runtime, while maintaining user-specified functionality and improving security.

papers.title: VulnSAGE: Adjudicating SAST Reports by Connecting LLM Reasoning to Program Structure
papers.summary: Static Application Security Testing (SAST) reports flag operations whose safety depends on project-specific context, and maintainers must decide which reports describe real defects. Large language models (LLMs) can interpret this context, but adjudicating a report with them requires the decisive code, which often lies far from the reported line, and a decision basis that program analysis can check. We present VulnSAGE, an adjudication system for SAST reports that connects LLM reasoning to program structure in both directions. Its report-centered slicer recovers the dependencies of the reported operation together with the program structure that explains them, such as the caller object on which a helper acts. CLAIM, an intermediate representation for report judgments, records each model interpretation as a semantic fact that cites the program relations it assumes. Program analysis checks these premises, and the verdict follows from the facts whose premises hold. Both mechanisms share a program graph, which lets the model cite the code it reads and lets the checker query those citations. Statically supported true positives then guide proof-of-concept generation and runtime reproduction. Across 187 labeled reports from four corpora covering five vulnerability families, VulnSAGE rejects 89 of 97 false alarms and retains 85 of 90 real defects. Under a common PoC procedure, 25 of its positive verdicts reproduce at runtime, compared with three for the LLM-based adjudicator LLM4SA. Applied to 45,440 alerts raised by five SAST tools on the 200 most-starred C/C++ projects on GitHub, it reproduces 104 defects at runtime. Maintainers have confirmed 24 of the 26 defects they have responded to, including ten previously unknown defects, nine of which are already fixed.
papers.title_zh: VulnSAGE：通过将 LLM 推理连接到程序结构来裁定 SAST 报告
papers.abstract_zh: 静态应用安全测试（SAST）报告会标记其安全性取决于项目特定上下文的操作，而维护者必须判断哪些报告描述的是真实缺陷。大型语言模型（LLM）能够解释这种上下文，但用它们来裁定一份报告需要决定性的代码——这些代码往往远离被报告的行——以及一个可由程序分析检查的决策依据。我们提出 VulnSAGE，一个用于 SAST 报告的裁定系统，它在两个方向上把 LLM 推理与程序结构连接起来。其以报告为中心的切片器会恢复被报告操作的依赖关系，以及解释这些依赖关系的程序结构，例如辅助函数所作用的调用者对象。CLAIM 是一种用于报告判定的中间表示，它把每个模型解释记录为引用其所假设程序关系的语义事实。程序分析检查这些前提，而判定则来自那些前提成立的事实。两种机制共享一个程序图，这使模型能够引用其阅读的代码，并使检查器能够查询这些引用。随后，得到静态支持的真阳性会指导概念验证生成和运行时复现。在来自四个语料库、覆盖五类漏洞家族的 187 份带标签报告中，VulnSAGE 拒绝了 97 个误报中的 89 个，并保留了 90 个真实缺陷中的 85 个。在一种通用的 PoC 流程下，其正面判定中有 25 个可在运行时复现，相比之下，基于 LLM 的裁定器 LLM4SA 为三个。应用于五个 SAST 工具在 GitHub 上 200 个星标最多的 C/C++ 项目上提出的 45,440 条告警时，它在运行时复现了 104 个缺陷。维护者已确认了其所回应的 26 个缺陷中的 24 个，包括十个此前未知的缺陷，其中九个已经修复。

papers.title: Efficient Program Reduction for Library Fuzzing Harnesses
papers.summary: Library fuzzing harnesses translate generated inputs into API calls. When a complex harness triggers a crash, developers must determine whether the cause is a library defect or invalid harness usage. A smaller reproducer can simplify this investigation, but obtaining one requires repeatedly building and executing modified harnesses and analyzing their crashes, making manual or even automatic minimization time-consuming. Moreover, data-dependent statements prevent the reducer to remove unnecessary code and the heavy stack trace symbolization in libraries also slows down the candidate execution. To address these challenges, we present HarnessMinimizer, a system for efficient minimization of C/C++ library fuzzing harnesses. Its optimized pipeline reuses header analysis and prepared libraries and runtimes to reduce the work required to build and execute each simplified harness during the reduction process. It records and replays input values so that unnecessary input operations can be removed without changing the values supplied to surviving calls. It also uses a fast method to check whether each simplified harness preserves the original crash, avoiding repeated stack trace symbolization. We evaluate HarnessMinimizer with four reduction engines on 200 crash cases from 21 open source libraries. Compared with the unoptimized pipeline, HarnessMinimizer achieves speedups of 3.46-4.51 times in average total wall time. Average harness size decreases from 1,352 original tokens to 143-263 remaining tokens after minimization. In crash triage using a large language model, accuracy in identifying harness bugs increases from 28% with the original harnesses to 44-51% with the minimized harnesses, while accuracy for library bugs remains at 100%.
papers.title_zh: 面向库模糊测试驱动的高效程序缩减
papers.abstract_zh: 库模糊测试驱动将生成的输入转换为 API 调用。当一个复杂的测试驱动触发崩溃时，开发者必须确定其原因究竟是库缺陷还是无效的测试驱动用法。更小的复现程序可以简化这一调查，但获得这样一个复现程序需要反复构建并执行修改后的测试驱动并分析其崩溃，这使得手动乃至自动缩减都耗时。此外，数据相关语句会使缩减器无法移除不必要的代码，而库中繁重的堆栈跟踪符号化也会拖慢候选执行。为应对这些挑战，我们提出 HarnessMinimizer，一个用于高效最小化 C/C++ 库模糊测试驱动的系统。其优化流水线复用头文件分析以及预先准备好的库和运行时，以减少缩减过程中构建和执行每个简化测试驱动所需的工作。它记录并重放输入值，从而可以在不改变提供给保留下来的调用的值的情况下移除不必要的输入操作。它还使用一种快速方法来检查每个简化测试驱动是否保留原始崩溃，从而避免重复的堆栈跟踪符号化。我们在来自 21 个开源库的 200 个崩溃案例上，使用四个缩减引擎评估 HarnessMinimizer。与未优化流水线相比，HarnessMinimizer 在平均总墙钟时间上实现了 3.46-4.51 倍的加速。平均测试驱动大小从原始的 1,352 个 token 降至最小化后剩余的 143-263 个 token。在使用大语言模型进行崩溃分诊时，识别测试驱动缺陷的准确率从原始测试驱动的 28% 提高到最小化测试驱动的 44-51%，而对库缺陷的准确率保持在 100%。

papers.title: Code Skill Server: A Large-Scale Search Engine for Code Generation Skills
papers.summary: Agent skills have proven to be an effective technique for improving agent ability on specific tasks, including software engineering, natural science, and mathematics. During such a process, using agent skills often involves manually discovering and organizing skills from heterogeneous sources, while existing skill retrieval methods mainly focus on selecting relevant skills from established skill libraries. However, with the rapidly increasing number and variety of reusable agent skills, manually searching for relevant skills across heterogeneous sources is becoming impractical at scale. In this paper, we introduce the Code Skill Server (CSS), a large-scale search engine for finding the most useful code generation skills for a target task. CSS consists of a skill server that incrementally collects and indexes publicly available code generation skills from multiple sources, with 993 skills included in the corpus used in this work. Extensive experiments across different retrieval methods and code generation benchmarks show that the best CSS configuration improves Pass@1 by up to 13.91% and consistently improves all evaluated models by at least 4.21% in the cross-model evaluation. These results demonstrate that CSS can effectively search for and serve relevant skills, improving code generation quality and enhancing models' code generation capabilities. Code and the CSS-993 corpus are available at {https://github.com/haoyuli-sdu/CodeSkillServer}.

papers.title: Towards Agentic Proof Harness Engineering
papers.summary: Formal verification of real-world projects requires substantial manual effort, from specifying correctness properties to constructing the infrastructure needed to check them. We envision verification agents that assist developers throughout this process. Among the many tasks involved, one stands out as both foundational and amenable to automation: proof-harness engineering. A proof harness defines an isolated verification environment for a program unit, such as a function or module, by providing symbolic inputs, initialization code, and models of its dependencies. Today, proof-harness engineering remains largely a manual task performed by verification engineers. To explore the potential of coding agents for this task, we propose an agentic proof-harness engineer that automatically constructs verifier-ready harnesses from a software project and a designated verification target. We combine the agent with formal soundness and precision guards to validate generated abstractions and guide their refinement. We evaluate the feasibility of our approach in an exploratory case study on curl and libuv, using three historical assertion violations already embedded in the source code as verification properties. Our results show that the agent successfully constructs proof harnesses that enable CBMC to detect all three violations. We further demonstrate the potential for reusing these harnesses with other verification tools.

papers.title: MLOps-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Production ML Engineering in Real Repositories
papers.summary: AI agents are increasingly expected to modify and maintain machine-learning systems in production, yet existing benchmarks primarily evaluate either competition-style ML experimentation or generic repository issue resolution. We introduce MLOps-Bench, a repository-grounded benchmark for production ML engineering. Unlike prior ML-agent benchmarks, MLOps-Bench evaluates executable lifecycle changes inside real ML repositories, spanning data pipelines, feature engineering, model training, model serving, monitoring, CI/CD and governance, and end-to-end integration. Each task is grounded in repository evidence and includes a natural-language requirement, oracle patch, plausible buggy baseline, fail-to-pass tests, pass-to-pass tests, and provenance metadata. The benchmark contains 212 validated tasks from 31 public ML repositories, with 636 fail-to-pass tests and 856 pass-to-pass tests. We evaluate six agents and find that the best system solves 31.2% of tasks while passing 68.7% of tests, showing that current agents often make partial progress but still fail production-relevant behavioral requirements. MLOps-Bench shifts agent evaluation beyond model building and issue fixing toward repository-native MLOps work where correctness depends on lifecycle reasoning, behavioral robustness, and preservation of existing system behavior.

papers.title: Recall-Oriented Precise Binary-to-Source Function Matching
papers.summary: Binary-to-source function matching supports software composition analysis by identifying reused third-party code, but existing embedding-based approaches restrict subsequent refinement to initially retrieved candidates. When the correct source function is absent from this set, selecting or filtering the available candidates cannot recover the match. Inlining further complicates the retrieval by combining multiple source functions into one binary function. In this paper, we propose BScout to improve matching precision and uncover additional matches. BScout uses the positional information of existing matches to supplement candidates for unresolved binary functions, extending the search beyond the initial candidate set, and adopts composition-aware training to address the inlined composition matching. Large language models are adopted to select and review matches, while positional information also helps filter inconsistent results. Experiments show that BScout is effective in binary-to-source function matching. BScout achieves overall higher precision, recall and F1 scores than BinaryAI and SBridge with acceptable analysis costs. Particularly, on large stripped binaries, BScout outperforms the competitors with a precision increment of 32% and approximately 2.9 times the recall.
papers.title_zh: 面向召回的精确二进制到源码函数匹配
papers.abstract_zh: 二进制到源码函数匹配通过识别被复用的第三方代码来支持软件组成分析，但现有的基于嵌入的方法将后续的细化限制在初始检索到的候选之上。当正确的源码函数不在该集合中时，对可用候选进行选择或过滤无法恢复该匹配。内联通过将多个源码函数组合成一个二进制函数，进一步使检索变得复杂。本文提出 BScout，以提高匹配精度并发现更多匹配。BScout 利用已有匹配的位置信息为未解决的二进制函数补充候选，将搜索扩展到初始候选集之外，并采用组合感知训练来处理内联组合匹配。采用大语言模型来选择和审查匹配，同时位置信息也有助于过滤不一致的结果。实验表明，BScout 在二进制到源码函数匹配中是有效的。在可接受的分析开销下，BScout 整体上取得了比 BinaryAI 和 SBridge 更高的精确率、召回率和 F1 分数。特别地，在大规模剥离二进制文件上，BScout 优于对比方法，精确率提升 32%，召回率约为其 2.9 倍。

papers.title: An Interactive GraphRAG Workspace for Reifying, Auditing, and Steering Conversational AI Memories
papers.summary: Conversational Large Language Models (LLMs) are widely employed in software engineering for code generation, debugging, and architectural design. However, as developers engage in multi-session development tasks, technical knowledge becomes siloed in isolated, linear chat histories. Reusing context across sessions leads to three critical challenges: (1) flat-vector retrieval fails to traverse multi-hop relational dependencies between distant architectural decisions; (2) temporal drift in software packages and APIs results in silent context poisoning when reusing aged dialogue logs; and (3) raw conversation concatenation induces prompt bloat and attention degradation. We present CognitiveCanvas, an interactive tool that transforms conversational AI memories from ephemeral text logs into persistent, manipulable, and audited knowledge objects. \textsc{CognitiveCanvas} integrates: (1) a Hierarchical Semantic Fact-Graph (HSFG) that distills dialogues into Goal, Fact, and Code artifacts, achieving a 92.2\% token reduction while enabling multi-hop GraphRAG traversal; (2) a Continuous Temporal Drift Auditor coupling 60+ regex heuristics with live calendar-anchored LLM verification for 1-click self-correction; and (3) a Spatial-Symbolic Prompt Compiler (SSPC) that translates 2D direct manipulation gestures (Voronoi clustering, node resizing, synthesis edges) directly into structured attention directives
papers.title_zh: 用于具化、审计与引导对话式 AI 记忆的交互式 GraphRAG 工作区
papers.abstract_zh: 对话式大语言模型（LLM）被广泛应用于软件工程中的代码生成、调试和架构设计。然而，随着开发者参与多会话开发任务，技术知识被孤立在彼此隔离的线性聊天历史中，形成知识孤岛。跨会话复用上下文会导致三个关键挑战：（1）扁平向量检索无法遍历相距遥远的架构决策之间的多跳关系依赖；（2）软件包和 API 中的时序漂移会在复用陈旧的对话日志时导致静默的上下文污染；（3）原始对话拼接会引发提示膨胀和注意力退化。我们提出 CognitiveCanvas，一种交互式工具，它将对话式 AI 记忆从短暂的文本日志转化为持久的、可操作且经过审计的知识对象。\textsc{CognitiveCanvas} 集成了：（1）分层语义事实图（HSFG），它将对话提炼为目标、事实和代码工件，在实现 92.2\% 的 token 减少的同时支持多跳 GraphRAG 遍历；（2）持续时序漂移审计器，将 60 多种正则启发式与以日历为锚的实时 LLM 验证相结合，实现一键式自我校正；（3）空间-符号提示编译器（SSPC），它将二维直接操作手势（Voronoi 聚类、节点缩放、合成边）直接转换为结构化的注意力指令

papers.title: Empirical Insights from AI-Powered Software Engineering in Practice
papers.summary: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is becoming indispensable in future software engineering. Its application spans a wide spectrum - from assisted development to autonomous software engineering, requiring organizations to address associated risks and challenges. This paper investigates these issues through three case studies, highlighting practical problems encountered during GenAI integration. Based on these findings, it provides targeted recommendations for managing risks and ensuring reliable outcomes. This paper provides guidance for effective and responsible GenAI adoption in software engineering based on empirical insights.

papers.title: Enforcing Code Reasoning in Agentic Scaffold for More Effective Issue Resolution
papers.summary: Reasoning is central to ReAct-based programming agents, yet whether and how they reason about code remains unclear. We study 7,955 issue-resolution trajectories from six single- and multi-agent scaffolds across four programming languages on SWE-bench-Verified, SWE-bench-Pro, and SWE-bench-Lite. We identify 12 forms of code reasoning in 66.95% of trajectories. Code reasoning is associated with higher resolution rates, and its intensity increases with task complexity. However, it remains largely unguided: agents may focus on surface-level symptoms during localization, fail to refine near-correct patches, overlook issue requirements, and generate tests with limited behavioral diversity. To address these limitations, we propose DeskCheck, an agentic scaffold that systematically guides code reasoning throughout repository-level issue resolution. DeskCheck simulates execution paths to localize root causes, simulates candidate patches to refine near-misses, audits patches against issue requirements, and reasons about corner-case inputs and expected outputs before generating tests. On 731 SWE-bench-Pro instances, DeskCheck improves resolution rates over mini-SWE-Agent and Claude Code by 6.29% to 10.53%, at an additional cost of $0.02-$0.28 per instance (average: $0.14). Per-phase analyses show higher method-level localization recall, more successful repairs of imprecisely localized issues, and better detection of missed corner cases in near-correct patches. Exact McNemar tests show statistically significant improvements across all subject LLMs (p < 10^-10), while repeated experiments support robustness to agent nondeterminism. These findings motivate systematic code reasoning as a means of improving programming agents.

papers.title: Whose Polarization Is It? Auditing Fairness in Network Polarization Measures
papers.summary: A polarization score is supposed to describe a community, not its surroundings. Yet when a minority community is embedded in a larger network, its measured polarization can rise or fall with the size and structure of the majority around it. We ask whether polarization measures are therefore fair to minorities and develop an audit built around two criteria: measurement invariance (MI), which asks whether otherwise equivalent majorities and minorities receive equivalent scores, and structural exogeneity (SE), which asks whether a minority's score changes when its surrounding majority changes. Resolution sensitivity (RS) is treated as a prerequisite for meaningful fairness assessment. We audit seven polarization measure families spanning the three network-operationalizable dimensions of polarization, introducing Network-Weighted Distance (NWD) to fill an unserved extremeness-separation combination. Across controlled synthetic networks, mechanism-isolating diagnostic topologies, and real political and communication networks, no measure passes all applicable checks. Minorities are systematically scored as more polarized than equivalent majorities. We trace this dependence to two separate channels: majority structure can alter the opinions that opinion-reading measures consume, and, on a different path, opinion-orthogonal structural change can affect the arithmetic of structural measures. Reading opinions is thus double-edged, letting contamination in when structure moves opinions but shielding the score when structure changes and opinions do not. We close with practical guidance for reporting polarization scores without inheriting these biases.

papers.title: Validating LLM-generated political networks with survey-reported partisan exposure
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate human behavior in social science research, including decisions, interactions, and social relationships. However, in network formation tasks, existing evaluations often focus on aggregate network properties, while networks with plausible structural properties may still fail to reproduce individuals' social and political environments. Here, we generate LLM-based political networks using personas sampled from the nationally representative ANES 2020--2022 Social Media Study and use respondents' survey-reported partisan exposure as an empirical benchmark for the political environments generated for the corresponding personas. We first characterize the structural properties and political assortativity of the generated networks, and then compare ego-level partisan exposure with the survey. We find that the structure and political assortativity of the generated networks vary across experimental configurations. More importantly, when comparing generated partisan exposure with the survey, some models generate stronger separation between Democratic and Republican egos than reported in the survey, with higher same-party and lower cross-party exposure, while others mainly underestimate Republican exposure across ego groups. Moreover, networks with similar political assortativity can still generate different partisan environments around the same personas, including among networks with plausible structural properties. Finally, generated networks show group-specific errors, under- or overestimating exposure to either Democrats or Republicans for specific social groups. These findings show that evaluating LLM-based social simulations only through aggregate outcomes can hide errors in the local environments through which those outcomes emerge, highlighting the importance of validation at both aggregate and individual levels.
papers.title_zh: 利用调查报告的党派接触验证LLM生成的政治网络
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地被用于社会科学研究中模拟人类行为，包括决策、互动和社会关系。然而，在网络形成任务中，现有评估往往聚焦于网络的聚合属性，而具有看似合理的结构属性的网络仍可能无法复现个体的社会与政治环境。在此，我们使用从具有全国代表性的ANES 2020--2022社交媒体研究中抽样的角色画像生成基于LLM的政治网络，并将受访者调查报告的党派接触作为对应角色画像所生成政治环境的经验基准。我们首先刻画生成网络的结构属性和政治同配性，然后在ego层面将党派接触与调查进行比较。我们发现，生成网络的结构和政治同配性随实验配置而变化。更重要的是，在将生成的党派接触与调查进行比较时，一些模型在民主党与共和党ego之间生成的分隔强于调查所报告的分隔，表现为更高的同党接触和更低的跨党接触，而另一些模型则主要低估了各ego群体中的共和党接触。此外，具有相似政治同配性的网络仍可能在相同角色画像周围生成不同的党派环境，包括在具有看似合理的结构属性的网络之间也是如此。最后，生成网络表现出群体特异性误差，即对特定社会群体低估或高估对民主党人或共和党人的接触。这些发现表明，仅通过聚合结果评估基于LLM的社会模拟，可能会掩盖这些结果得以产生的局部环境中的误差，从而突显了在聚合层面和个体层面同时进行验证的重要性。

papers.title: "You" Is Not Toxic: How LLM Labelers Rewrite the Web's Conversation Laws
papers.summary: What the Web community believes about toxic conversations, such as that toxicity rises in longer and deeper threads, was measured mostly with Google's Perspective API, which is shutting down; large language models (LLMs) will make the next measurements. We find that LLM labelers mistake second-person address for toxicity, and that this one bias manufactures laws that human labels do not show. On 1.25 million news comments with crowd labels, Claude Haiku flags 12% of the non-toxic comments that contain no "you" and 51% of those with four or more; a single crowd rater flags 6% and 10%. Deeper replies address someone more often, so under Haiku toxicity rises with reply depth (+0.93 percentage points per level), while under the crowd's labels it slightly declines (-0.12). Rewriting "you" in the third person removes two thirds of the false rise; flagging only as many comments as the crowd does not remove it, and showing Haiku the parent comment enlarges it. All seven LLMs we test over-flag "you", and at the crowd's flag rate, without the parent, any false rise of the open ones vanishes at a fixed number of second-person words; Haiku also over-flags "you" on Reddit, Gab and Wikipedia talk pages. Agreement with human labels does not reveal the bias: we prove that a fixed Cohen's kappa leaves a law nearly unconstrained. We therefore certify the law instead of the labeler. Threadsafe uses the labeler's scores to choose which comments human raters label and to predict the others, and corrects the predictions with the human labels; linear laws are estimated without bias whatever the labeler does. In simulated audits its intervals for the laws keep nominal coverage from 250 labels on, where uniform-sample methods such as PPI++ fall short, and at 1,000 to 8,000 labels are 0.75 times as wide as those of design-based supervised learning (DSL); a thousand human labels rule out Haiku's rising law.
papers.title_zh: “你”并不有毒：LLM 标注者如何改写网络的对话定律
papers.abstract_zh: 网络社区对有毒对话的信念，例如毒性在更长、更深的讨论串中会上升，主要是用谷歌的 Perspective API 测量得到的，而该 API 即将关停；大型语言模型（LLM）将进行接下来的测量。我们发现，LLM 标注者会把第二人称称呼误认为毒性，而这一单一偏差制造出了人类标注并不显示出的定律。在 125 万条带众包标注的新闻评论上，Claude Haiku 将不含“you”的无毒评论中的 12% 标记为有毒，将含有四个及以上“you”的无毒评论中的 51% 标记为有毒；单个众包评分者对应的比例分别为 6% 和 10%。更深的回复更频繁地称呼某人，因此在 Haiku 下，毒性随回复深度上升（每层 +0.93 个百分点），而在众包标注下则略有下降（-0.12）。将“you”改写为第三人称可消除三分之二的虚假上升；只按众包标注相同的数量标记评论并不能消除它，而向 Haiku 展示父评论则会扩大它。我们测试的全部七个 LLM 都过度标记“you”，并且在众包的标记率下、不提供父评论时，开放模型中的任何虚假上升都会在固定的第二人称词数量处消失；Haiku 在 Reddit、Gab 和 Wikipedia 讨论页上也过度标记“you”。与人类标注的一致性并不能揭示该偏差：我们证明，固定的 Cohen's kappa 会使定律几乎不受约束。因此，我们认证的是定律，而不是标注者。Threadsafe 使用标注者的分数来选择哪些评论由人类评分者标注，并预测其余评论，再用人类标注校正这些预测；无论标注者如何做，线性定律的估计都是无偏的。在模拟审计中，从 250 个标注起，其对定律的区间保持名义覆盖率，而 PPI++ 等均匀样本方法在此情形下表现不足；在 1,000 到 8,000 个标注时，其区间宽度是基于设计的监督学习（DSL）区间的 0.75 倍；一千个人类标注即可排除 Haiku 的上升定律。

papers.title: Graphlet-based Decentralized Finance Transaction Method Classification
papers.summary: Decentralized Finance (DeFi) transactions involve complex interactions among accounts, smart contracts, and tokens. We investigate whether network topology can identify transaction methods that describe DeFi operations. We extract directed graphlet features to classify the 30 most frequent methods. Our results show that graphlet features complement event log counts in improving classification performance. Using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), we further derive model explanations that reveal method-specific graphlet structural patterns.

papers.title: Beyond Latent Personalization: Integrating HRV-Conditioned Personalization via LLM for Interpretable Stress Detection
papers.summary: Stress detection based on heart rate variability (HRV) has received increasing attention. However, existing personalized approaches integrate personal attributes with HRV through latent representations, limiting the interpretability of their interactions. In this work, we propose an LLM-enhanced personalized stress detection framework that integrates HRV features and personal attributes through LLM-based semantic interpretation. The proposed framework achieves a 29.9% relative MCC improvement over the strongest baseline on TILES-2018 while providing human-readable descriptions of individual physiological responses. The results highlight the potential of LLM-based semantic interpretation for achieving both effective and interpretable personalized stress detection.

papers.title: ECG-SDI: Single-lead Electrocardiogram Enables Continuous Sleep Depth Index Profiling and Scalable Digital Biomarkers for Sleep Health
papers.summary: Conventional sleep staging provides a coarse-grained representation that obscures within-stage depth variation. We developed ECG-SDI, a single-lead electrocardiography (ECG) framework for continuous sleep-depth profiling and digital biomarker extraction. Using 12,392 overnight polysomnographic recordings, we trained and validated a two-stage deep learning model supervised by conventional sleep-stage labels. Correlations with ordered stages excluding rapid eye movement (REM) sleep were 0.828 in the pooled internal test set and 0.848 in the external Cleveland Family Study; corresponding REM classification AUROCs were 0.954 and 0.977. Overnight trajectories captured within-stage variation. Biomarker-based phenotyping identified a disturbed subtype associated with poorer subjective sleep quality and higher all-cause mortality in the Sleep Heart Health Study (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.20; 95% CI, 1.05-1.38). Among 507 participants with paired recordings before and after continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP), normalized sleep-depth area increased by 6.1% and shallow-sleep burden below 0.3 decreased by 16.0%. Exploratory analyses linked reductions in approximate entropy and depth variability to reduced oxygen desaturation and increased sleep efficiency, respectively (Spearman rho = 0.24 and 0.12); both associations remained positive after covariate adjustment. Mean ECG-SDI within N2 increased by 0.017 (95% CI, 0.004-0.030). A wearable proof-of-concept illustrated the acquisition-to-report workflow. These findings support ECG-based sleep phenotyping and further evaluation of CPAP response monitoring at home.

papers.title: Distributed Performance Boosting through Neural Control for Plug-and-Play Networks
papers.summary: We address the problem of improving the performance of pre-stabilized networked systems subject to plug-and-play (PnP) operations, namely additions or removals of subsystems. While distributed baseline controllers can preserve stability after a PnP transition, augmenting them with expressive neural policies can invalidate the formal stability guarantees. To overcome this issue, we build on recently proposed Performance Boosting controllers based on the Internal Model Control (IMC) principle, which reduce closed-loop stability to a finite $\ell_2$-gain requirement on an auxiliary operator. In the distributed setting, this operator is formed by interconnecting local neural operators that exchange information only between neighboring subsystems. We then derive free parametrizations of this interconnection, namely explicit maps from unconstrained trainable variables to interconnected neural operators satisfying a prescribed network gain bound for every parameter value. The obtained distributed neural controller can therefore be trained by unconstrained gradient-based optimization without stability constraints or projection steps, while retaining the prescribed gain bound at every training iterate. We develop two complementary parametrizations. A neighbor-based compositional parametrization uses local coupling bounds, so that after a PnP event only subsystems whose bounds change need to update their gain parameters. A network-norm parametrization instead uses a bound on the overall coupling matrix and can reduce conservatism, at the price of requiring network-wide information. A PnP DC-microgrid case study shows that the proposed neural layer improves voltage transients under topology changes and load variations while preserving nominal closed-loop stability.

papers.title: On the possibilities and limitations of LLM-based multi-agent systems for multi-criteria decision-making in healthcare operations management
papers.summary: Multi-criteria models for healthcare operations need weights that express how stakeholders trade off patient waiting time, provider workload, and operating cost, but these weights are difficult to quantify. Teams of large language model (LLM) agents, each prompted to represent a stakeholder, have been used to supply them. We propose a framework for assessing the reliability of LLM-generated preferences as inputs to multi-objective optimization and quantifying how their uncertainty affects decisions. We study explicit preferences by asking agents to rate the importance of the criteria in an outpatient appointment scheduling problem, and implicit preferences by inferring trade-offs from the agents' pairwise choices between emergency department configurations. The computational experiments show that the explicit preferences respond to the clinic's operating conditions and differ across roles, but deliberation among the agents can erase these differences, whereas simple averaging preserves them. The pairwise choices used to reveal the agents' implicit preferences depend largely on which option is presented first, and we find limited evidence that a statistical model using contextual information alongside presentation order predicts the agents' choices on new comparison pairs better than a model using presentation order alone. We then formulate robust weighted-sum optimization models to account for preference uncertainty. In most cases, these models select different schedules or configurations from those obtained using average preference weights. These results indicate that LLM-generated preferences need an audit of this kind before they are used as optimization weights in healthcare decision support.
papers.title_zh: 论基于LLM的多智能体系统在医疗运营管理多准则决策中的可能性与局限性
papers.abstract_zh: 医疗运营中的多准则模型需要权重，用以表达利益相关者如何在患者等待时间、提供者工作量和运营成本之间进行权衡，但这些权重难以量化。由大型语言模型（LLM）智能体组成的团队——每个智能体被提示代表一个利益相关者——已被用于提供这些权重。我们提出一个框架，用于评估LLM生成偏好作为多目标优化输入时的可靠性，并量化其不确定性如何影响决策。我们通过要求智能体对门诊预约调度问题中各准则的重要性进行评分来研究显式偏好，并通过从智能体在急诊科配置之间的成对选择中推断权衡来研究隐式偏好。计算实验表明，显式偏好会响应诊所的运营条件，并因角色而异，但智能体之间的审议可能抹去这些差异，而简单平均则会保留它们。用于揭示智能体隐式偏好的成对选择在很大程度上取决于哪个选项先呈现，并且我们仅发现有限的证据表明，一个同时使用上下文信息和呈现顺序的统计模型在预测智能体对新比较对的选择时优于仅使用呈现顺序的模型。然后，我们构建稳健的加权和优化模型，以考虑偏好不确定性。在大多数情况下，这些模型选择的调度方案或配置不同于使用平均偏好权重所获得的调度方案或配置。这些结果表明，LLM生成的偏好在被用作医疗决策支持中的优化权重之前，需要这种类型的审计。

papers.title: From Flow-Box Invariants to Global Conservation Laws: Machine Learning-Assisted Detection of Singularities and Near-Integrability
papers.summary: Conservation laws reveal invariant structure in dynamical systems and constrain their evolution to lower-dimensional level sets. Locally, however, per the flow-box theorem, every $d$-dimensional system generically admits $d-1$ functionally independent conservation laws near a regular point even though, generically, only a few such laws persist globally. Data-driven methods typically learn conservation laws on a prescribed region of phase space from which training samples are drawn, leaving their behavior beyond that region unresolved. We formulate this local-to-global continuation problem and develop an {expanding-domain neural deflation} framework that tracks the number of independent conservation laws over nested domains. The method recovers the expected $d-1$ local invariants and detects their successive breakdown as the domain expands, relaxing to the expected global conservation law limit. It distinguishes the local invariants (associated with Frobenius integrability) from persistent global structure and shows that the domain scale over which additional laws survive reflects proximity to Liouville integrability. Pointwise losses can localize isolated obstructions, whereas in more complicated dynamics the breakdown of our loss functions is gradual and spatially diffuse. The framework thus provides a data-driven approach for studying the persistence and breakdown of (so-far-learned) conservation laws across phase space.

papers.title: How the elastic axis folds the transonic flutter boundary: shock energy transfer and conformally calibrated active learning
papers.summary: Isogai's case A, a pitch-plunge aerofoil whose elastic axis lies half a chord ahead of the leading edge, has a folded transonic flutter boundary in inviscid flow: near the bottom of the transonic dip several flutter speeds coexist at one Mach number. We map this boundary, and the family obtained by moving the elastic axis, with coupled unsteady Euler simulations, a Gaussian-process surrogate of the damping coefficient trained by batch active learning, and split conformal prediction on independent random simulations, which turns the surrogate into stability calls with a distribution-free error rate. Three failure modes of time-domain damping labels that leave no trace in the residuals are documented, and the half-degree mean incidence left by the common one-degree start is shown to raise the flutter speed at the dip by 2.8%, more than any numerical setting. With 80 simulations the learned case A boundary labels 64 of 65 independent runs correctly, and calibrated calls are wrong in at most 1.6% of cases. Over Mach number, elastic axis and flutter speed index, 193 simulations and 40 calibration runs show that the fold exists only for elastic axes more than about 0.4 chord ahead of the leading edge; it closes between 0.39 and 0.33 chord ahead, on two meshes. Chordwise energy budgets, closed against the solver loads and the growth rate within a few per cent, explain the boundary. The lower branch is crossed through the reduced frequency at unchanged shock phase. On the upper branch the shock is pinned at the trailing edge, and moving the elastic axis aft brings the pivot of the flutter mode towards the section, so that the damping of the supersonic surface falls faster than the residual shock input and the fold closes.

papers.title: Wavelength Diversity Expands the Expressive Power of Optical Computing
papers.summary: Universal function approximation underpins neural networks' capacity to represent nonlinear relationships, but realizing this capability in optical hardware requires engineering the computational features encoded in light. Here, we show that wavelength diversity enhances optical function-approximation expressivity through wavelength-scaled Fourier features generated by a shared phase encoder, without increasing the number of input-encoded harmonics. Multiple wavelengths contribute to the representation of each output function rather than merely serving as independent computational channels. We establish theoretical scaling laws and approximation-error bounds, revealing that, for nondispersive encoders, the spectral endpoints determine the accessible computational bandwidth, while intermediate illumination wavelengths enrich the available harmonics within that bandwidth. Numerical studies demonstrate improved approximation of real- and complex-valued nonlinear functions, with a representative design achieving more than a 100-fold reduction in mean-squared error relative to tested monochromatic optical processors with the same number of trainable phase features. Experimentally, we validate enhanced approximation accuracy and demonstrate the simultaneous approximation of 4,136 distinct nonlinear functions using a compact, single-layer diffractive processor under five-wavelength illumination. These results establish wavelength diversity as an additional physical resource for scaling the expressive power of optical computing and enhancing the accuracy of parallel nonlinear function approximation.

papers.title: Reading the News Without Hindsight: NoLBERT Topics and the Cross-Section of Stock Returns
papers.summary: Language models that read financial news are usually trained on text from the same years used to test them, so a backtest can reward hindsight. We build news topics from NoLBERT, an encoder pretrained only on text published between 1976 and 1995, adapted into a sentence encoder by contrastive fine-tuning on passages of the same article, with no labels or returns. We compare it with LDA, MiniLM and FinBERT readers on 1.26 million articles from 2012 to 2024, convert each reader's topics into attention shocks and stock exposures, and forecast the returns of the 1,000 largest US stocks with eight models at three rebalancing frequencies. Models are fitted on 2013-2019, choices are made on 2020-2021, and 2022-2024 is held out. The experiment with the best validation score loses money at every frequency. Measuring attention shocks against the past 63 trading days instead of 5 raises the test rank IC of every reader. NoLBERT gives the most stable topics and forecasts about as well as LDA. An equal-weight combination of all readers and models earns a monthly net Sharpe ratio of 1.12, significant against zero before adjusting for the search but not against a price-only benchmark.

papers.title: Quantum-Classical Neural Networks for Solving Lindblad Master Equations
papers.summary: Variational quantum algorithms have emerged as a promising approach for simulating open quantum systems, yet their expressive power and trainability remain poorly understood. We propose a variational framework for solving Lindblad master equations by minimizing a residual cost function using a compositional ansatz obtained by combining a classical neural network with a parameterized quantum circuit. The density matrix is represented through a purification on an enlarged Hilbert space, ensuring positivity, Hermiticity, and unit trace by construction, while all gradients are evaluated exactly via the parameter-shift rule. Beyond the algorithmic formulation, we derive an upper bound for the covering number of the proposed compositional model and compare it with that of purely quantum neural networks. Our analysis shows that the classical parametrization enlarges the effective hypothesis class while providing finer control over its complexity, thereby establishing a theoretical connection between expressivity, covering numbers, effective dimension, and the barren plateau phenomenon. Numerical experiments validate both the accuracy of the proposed method for representative Lindblad master equations and the theoretical predictions regarding gradient concentration. These results provide a unified variational and theoretical framework for the simulation of dissipative quantum dynamics using compositional quantum machine learning models.

papers.title: Concrete Functions in Private Simultaneous Quantum Messages: Quantum Advantages and Structural Limitations
papers.summary: Private simultaneous quantum messages (PSQM) provide a minimal model of noninteractive secure multiparty quantum computation, yet their communication complexity for concrete functions remains poorly understood. We show that familiar total functions already exhibit both genuine quantum advantages and strong structural limitations. For three-party equality on $n$-bit inputs, which determines whether the players' $n$-bit strings are identical, we construct an entanglement-assisted protocol with asymptotic communication $(1.633\ldots)n$ qubits, whereas every perfectly correct protocol without prior entanglement requires at least $3n$ qubits. For three-bit majority, one shared GHZ state and one transmitted qubit per player suffice for perfect correctness and perfect privacy, reducing the communication from the optimal classical cost of six bits to three qubits. Three-bit AND behaves differently. No perfectly correct and perfectly private protocol exists when the players share an arbitrary three-qubit state, apply arbitrary local unitary encodings, and transmit one qubit each. However, increasing the local dimension overcomes this obstruction: one shared three-qutrit GHZ state and one transmitted qutrit per player yield a one-shot protocol with total communication $3\log_2 3$. Together with the six-bit classical lower bound, this gives a strict quantum communication advantage. More generally, for every $k\geq 3$, we construct a perfectly correct and perfectly private one-shot protocol for $k$-bit AND using one qudit of dimension at most $k$ per player, and hence at most $k\log_2 k$ qubits in total.

papers.title: Learning angles for quantum approximate optimization
papers.summary: The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) and its variants are leading algorithms to help solve challenging combinatorial optimization problems. QAOA maps these problems to Ising Hamiltonians such that their ground state is the desired solution. Candidate solutions are then drawn from a variational quantum circuit. The performance of QAOA hinges on a set of variational angles. However, finding good angles is an instance-specific and computationally expensive non-convex classical optimization task. Here, we learn the mapping from the problem instance to high-quality QAOA angles. Our learned models replace the per-instance optimization, that we call the solver, with a single forward pass that is several orders of magnitude faster than the solver with a near identical quality. Our models further generalize to unseen topologies such as Barabási-Albert and 2D grid graphs. Experiments on quantum hardware confirm that QAOA samples with angles produced by our open-source models are indistinguishable from solver angles. Crucially, models sensitive to the topology of the problem instance increase the quality of the QAOA angles. Our work amortizes a major bottleneck in QAOA by an up-front data generation and training cost. Importantly, this cost can be amortized over time in settings where many similar problems are optimized on a regular basis, as is often the case in applications for industry.

papers.title: SpinControl: Control Software for Prototyping and Benchmarking of Spin-Qubit Devices and Measurement Protocols
papers.summary: Quantum computers require software to control the states of the qubits. As the actions on qubits grow in complexity with circuit execution, calibration, and benchmarking, the complexity of the control software grows in tandem. Spin-qubit quantum computers are at a stage where experimentalists need low-level access for tuning and calibration, and quantum algorithm researchers want high-level circuit-level access. In this article, we present the software design of SpinControl. SpinControl integrates three architectural metrics: 1) customizability, to allow prototyping devices and measurement protocols, is achieved by separating data and behaviour; 2) modularity and extensibility are achieved by separating functionalities into different components; and 3) robustness, to reliably execute quantum circuits on many qubits, is achieved by CI pipelines and input validation. SpinControl allows different types of measurements while customizing the instruments used, the pulse or circuit program executed, and the data processing. It allows building standardized experiments from measurement and analysis building blocks and executing these for calibration in a custom and conditional order. SpinControl implements these functionalities alongside robust configuration and data management, a connection to the cloud, and calibration scheduling. Pulse and circuit compilation, virtual gate matrices, as well as spin-qubit-specific GUIs integrated by SpinControl, make heavy use of software packages developed by Delft University of Technology: pulse lib, core-tools (both open source), and QConstruct

papers.title: ConQUESTA: Topology-Aware Post-Training Structural Pruning of Quantum Neural Networks
papers.summary: Deploying quantum neural networks (QNNs) on sparse hardware requires preserving task accuracy while reducing compiler-induced two-qubit gates, SWAPs, and depth. We present ConQUESTA (\underline{C}onstrained \underline{Qu}antum \underline{E}ntangler \underline{S}election with \underline{T}opology \underline{A}wareness), a post training pruning framework that combines task saliency with compiler cost, screens candidate entanglers, and searches complete pruning masks under an explicit accuracy constraint. Unlike one-shot ranking, each mask is transpiled as a whole across multiple coupling topologies. Across 4-, 6-, and 8-qubit QNNs and eight model seeds at 55% pruning, ConQUESTA achieves mean resource reductions of 61.6% on Breast Cancer, 72.0% on Digits01, and 82.2% on Iris, exceeding the strongest matched simple baseline by 3.5, 1.7, and 8.9 percentage points, respectively.
